Introduction Title: Recruitment of a National Firm to Conduct End of Programme Evaluation - Spotlight Initiative 2.0 Joint Programme Under Gender for Development Uganda (G4DU) SCOPE: In 2024, Spotlight conducted a tailored baseline survey, covering 12 districts (Arua, Yumbe,Terego,Gulu, Kitgum, Omoro, Tororo, Amudat, Otuke, Kampala, Kyegegwa and Kasese) and selected national and district - based study participants (AGYW and ABYM in and out of schools, duty bearers, and Community members). The baseline survey provided vital information for determining the programme’s baseline and target values across the indicators in its results framework. The end of programme evaluation will assess progress and achievements against this framework. The final evaluation is being commissioned by UNRCO, the coordinating Office of Spotlight programme in Uganda on behalf of five UN Agencies (UNDP, UNFPA, UNICEF, UNHCR, and UNWOMEN) in collaboration with Ministry of Gender, Labour and Social Development (MGLSD) that coordinates the programme on behalf of government of Uganda. The main purpose of the evaluation is to undertake a comprehensive, gender-responsive and human-rights-based assessment of the programme’s performance and achievements against its goal and objectives; determine its contribution to preventing and responding to SGBV and VAC and advancing SRHR in the seventeen Spotlight-focused districts of Arua, Terego, Yumbe, Adjumani, Madi-Okollo, Nebbi, Oyam, Lamwo, Gulu, Kitgum, Omoro, Tororo, Amudat, Kampala, Otuke, Kasese and Kyegegwa; and identify lessons, good practices and actionable recommendations for sustainability, replication and scale-up. The evaluation shall assess differential results for women, adolescent girls, men and boys, including groups facing intersecting forms of discrimination, and examine the extent to which the programme addressed underlying gender inequalities, discriminatory social norms, unequal power relations, structural and institutional barriers, and strengthened the agency, voice, safety, rights and access to quality services of women and adolescent girls. It shall also identify intended and unintended positive or negative effects, including any backlash or reinforcement of harmful gender stereotypes. postings.text: Consultant-GL Cluster Team Leader | ICRISAT - The International Crops Research Institute for the Semi-Arid Tropics Skip to main content Consultant-GL Cluster Team Leader ICRISAT - The International Crops Research Institute for the Semi-Arid Tropics India Both national and international GL Cluster Team Leader level Speaks Hindi, Rajasthani Apply Summary by Impactpool ICRISAT is seeking a Consultant – GL Cluster Team Lead to oversee the implementation and monitoring of natural resource management (NRM) plans in Rajasthan, India. The role involves coordinating surveys, resource mapping, and community participation while supervising field staff and ensuring compliance with environmental safeguards. The ideal candidate will have a background in agricultural engineering or soil science and at least three years of relevant field experience. This is a 12-month contract position. Candidate Requirements: Bachelor’s degree in agricultural engineering or soil science At least 3 years of field experience in watershed or soil conservation Working ability with GPS and Excel/mobile survey apps Basic soil-water observation methods Supervision of field staff Fluency in Hindi/Rajasthani Willingness to travel Key skills Agricultural Engineering, Soil Science, Additional/Preferred Skills field experience in watershed Preferred Qualifications BTech BSc About ICRISAT ICRISAT is a non-profit, non-political organisation that conducts agricultural research for development in Asia and Africa, working with partners around the world. Drylands cover about 45% of the world's land, are home to 2.3 billion people (one in three) and support 45–50% of the world's livestock. ICRISAT's vision is a prosperous, food-secure and resilient dryland tropics. ICRISAT is headquartered in Patancheru, Hyderabad, India, with two regional hubs and eight country offices in Africa. For more information visit - www.icrisat.org Role Purpose ICRISAT seeks applications from dynamic and professional personnel for the position of Consultant – GL Cluster Team Lead. The incumbent will lead day-to-day implementation and monitoring in the assigned village cluster, linking technical NRM plans, field observations and community participation. The selected candidate will be based in the state of Rajasthan, India. Key Responsibilities:   Coordinate baseline surveys, village resource mapping, soil and land-use assessments, water-resource inventories, and identification of priority NRM interventions across project clusters. Prepare and coordinate village- and cluster-level implementation plans in consultation with the District Support Officer, NRM Expert, Gram Panchayats, and local communities. Supervise field implementation and monitoring of soil and water conservation measures, including khadin, tanka, nadi, field bunding, micro-catchments, dune stabilization, grassland restoration, and silvopasture interventions. Supervise Field Research Technicians and Community Resource Persons (CRPs), ensuring regular collection of rainfall, runoff, soil moisture, groundwater, soil sampling, vegetation, and other hydrological monitoring data. Coordinate Farmer Field School (FFS) activities, field demonstrations, community consultations, and capacity-building programs; maintain geotagged records of project interventions, monitoring sites, and implementation progress. Ensure timely field data verification, documentation, and reporting to the District Support Officer; identify implementation challenges, coordinate corrective actions, and ensure compliance with environmental and biodiversity safeguards.   Essential Qualifications and skills:   Bachelor’s degree in agriculture engineering, Soil Science or any other related field At least 3 years of field experience in watershed, soil conservation, restoration or village-level NRM implementation, preferably in arid Rajasthan. Working ability with GPS, Excel/mobile survey apps, basic soil-water observation methods and field staff supervision Well versed in Hindi/Rajasthani communication skills and readiness for regular travel. Terms of Appointment This is a contract role for 12 months (01 years). How to apply  The position will remain open until a suitable candidate is identified. Shortlisting will start from 25 November 2026. All applicants should apply with their latest resume, and the names and contact information of three references that are knowledgeable about their professional qualifications and work experience. All applications will be acknowledged; however, only short-listed candidates will be contacted. Applicants must be nationals of the country of assignment or possess a valid work permit and legal authorization to work in the country to be eligible to apply for this position. ICRISAT is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to increasing diversity and maintaining a progressive and inclusive workplace. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of their ethnicity, race, gender, religious beliefs, sexual orientation, age, marital status or whether they have a disability.   At Impactpool we do our best to provide you the most accurate info, but closing dates may be wrong on our site. Please check on the recruiting organization's page for the exact info. Candidates are responsible for complying with deadlines and are encouraged to submit applications well ahead. Before applying, please make sure that you have read the requirements for the position and that you qualify. Applications from non-qualifying applicants will most likely be discarded by the recruiting manager. postings.title: International Consultant to conduct a final evaluation of UN Women’s Making Migration Safe for Women programme UN WOMEN - United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women Remote | South Africa | Ethiopia | Multiple locations Senior
postings.text: International Consultant to conduct a final evaluation of UN Women’s Making Migration Safe for Women programme | UN WOMEN - United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women Skip to main content International Consultant to conduct a final evaluation of UN Women’s Making Migration Safe for Women programme UN WOMEN - United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women Remote | South Africa, Ethiopia , Multiple locations International Senior level Speaks English Apply Summary by Impactpool UN Women is seeking an International Consultant to conduct a final evaluation of its Making Migration Safe for Women programme. The evaluation will assess the programme's implementation in Ethiopia and South Africa, focusing on its relevance, effectiveness, efficiency, coherence, and sustainability. The consultant will analyze how human rights and gender equality principles are integrated into the programme and identify lessons learned and recommendations for future programming. This role requires strong analytical skills and experience in conducting evaluations related to gender equality and migration. Candidate Requirements: Master’s degree in gender/women's studies or related field At least 7 years of experience in evaluations Experience in gender equality and migration-related projects Strong analytical skills in quantitative and qualitative data Proven knowledge of Results-Based Management Fluency in English Background: UN Women, grounded in the vision of equality enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations, works for the elimination of discrimination against women and girls; the empowerment of women; and the achievement of equality between women and men as partners and beneficiaries of development, human rights, humanitarian action and peace and security. Economic empowerment is one of the priority areas of UN Women. UN Women works with governments and partners to promote women’s economic empowerment and increase their access to economic opportunities and outcomes, especially for those who are most excluded, including women migrant workers. In 2018, the Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration was adopted by UN Member States. And as the blueprint for the governance and coordination of international migration, it is critical that gender equality and the empowerment of women and girls are central in its implementation. UN Women works to help ensure that migrant women’s human and labour rights are effectively promoted and protected at all stages of migration, and that the Global Compact for Migration is human rights-based and gender-responsive.  Since 2023, UN Women has been implementing Phase 2 of the Making Migration Safe for Women programme. The programme aims to ensure that migration is safe for women and strengthen international norms and standards for the protection and promotion of migrant women’s rights. It places particular emphasis on ensuring that women have the information they need to make informed decisions about migration, including an understanding of the risks and challenges they may face. It also seeks to ensure that women migrant workers, including returnees, are protected by gender-responsive legal frameworks and have access to decent work. The final evaluation will assess Germany-funded programme implementation from 2023 to mid-2027 in Ethiopia and at the Global level, and from 2025 to 2026 in South Africa. As a summative evaluation, it will assess programme performance and results, with a particular focus on outputs, and examine the programme’s relevance, effectiveness, efficiency, coherence and sustainability. It will also assess the programme’s contribution to the promotion and protection of migrant women’s rights and identify lessons learned, good practices and recommendations to inform future programming, support strategic planning and strengthen accountability for development effectiveness. The evaluation will be conducted by an independent external consultant commissioned by UN Women Headquarters, and supported by the Making Migration Safe for Women programme team. An evaluation reference group will also be established to provide input and guidance throughout the evaluation process. The evaluation will adhere to UN Women’s Evaluation Policy and Evaluation Handbook, the Global Evaluation Reports Assessment and Analysis System (GERAAS) evaluation report quality checklist and the United Nations System-wide Action Plan Evaluation Performance Indicator (UN-SWAP EPI) framework. The final evaluation report will be submitted to the donor(s) alongside relevant progress reports and the final programme report. The consultant will be engaged by UN Women’s Economic Empowerment Section and will report to the Global Coordinator of the Making Migration Safe for Women programme. Description of Responsibilities/ Scope of Work The overall objectives of the final evaluation are to: Analyze how a human rights-based approach and gender equality principles are integrated into programme interventions. Assess the relevance, effectiveness, efficiency, coherence and sustainability of the programme in achieving its intended results. Assess the programme's contribution to changes in the lives of beneficiaries, communities and institutions, including progress towards gender-responsive migration policies, laws and services and the protection and promotion of migrant women's rights. Examine the contextual factors that enable or constrain the achievement of results, including programme management, financial management, human resource investment and partnerships. Assess the effectiveness of programme communication, advocacy, monitoring and knowledge management efforts. Identify lessons learned, good practices and recommendations to inform future programming. Key Evaluation Questions The following questions provide an initial framework for the evaluation. The consultant will refine the questions, evaluation criteria and indicators during the inception phase, in consultation with the programme management team. Relevance: To what extent has the programme responded to the needs and priorities of migrant women and to relevant national, regional and international commitments? Effectiveness: To what extent has the programme achieved its intended outputs and outcomes, and what changes has it contributed to in the lives of beneficiaries, institutional capacities, social norms and policy and legislative frameworks? Efficiency: To what extent have programme resources, including financial and human resources, been used economically and in a timely manner to achieve results? Coherence: To what extent has the programme complemented other relevant initiatives and contributed to synergies at country, regional and global levels? Sustainability: To what extent are programme results, capacities and partnerships likely to be sustained, and what factors may enable or constrain their continuation? Human rights and gender equality: To what extent have human rights and gender equality principles been integrated into programme design and implementation, including the meaningful participation of marginalized groups? Strategic positioning: What has been UN Women’s added value, and how effectively have partnerships supported programme implementation, policy engagement and advocacy? Monitoring, evaluation and knowledge management: To what extent have monitoring and evaluation systems, knowledge products and lessons learned supported evidence-based decision-making, programme adaptation and accountability? Communication and advocacy: How effectively has the programme communicated its results and met donor visibility requirements? Scope of the Final Evaluation The scope of the evaluation covers Germany-funded programme implementation in Ethiopia, South Africa and at the global level, over the following periods: Ethiopia : 2023 to mid-2027 South Africa: 2025 to 2026 Global level: 2023 to mid-2027 Methodology The consultant will develop a detailed evaluation methodology and present it for approval to the programme management team during the inception phase. The methodology should combine appropriate quantitative and qualitative methods and ensure participatory, inclusive and culturally appropriate processes that are responsive to human rights and gender equality principles. Data collection may include desk reviews, analysis of programme monitoring data, interviews and focus group discussions with relevant stakeholders, including government institutions, development partners, implementing partners, civil society, organizations, and migrant women. The methodology should ensure appropriate attention to data quality, reliability, validity and the meaningful participation of diverse stakeholders. Sampling limitations and other methodological constraints should be clearly documented. The evaluation will be conducted primarily through virtual consultations, supported by the relevant UN Women country offices and global programme team. Field visits may be undertaken where necessary and feasible, subject to agreement with UN Women. The consultant will document any limitations arising from the chosen methodology or approach to data collection. The consultant will ensure that privacy and data protection considerations are integrated throughout the evaluation process, including the collection, storage, processing and reporting of sensitive information, in accordance with UN Women’s applicable policies and procedures. The consultant may use generative AI tools only to support discrete, verifiable tasks. Any substantive AI use will be disclosed in the inception and evaluation reports, and outputs will be verified by the consultant against source material. Findings, conclusions, lessons and recommendations will remain human-led. Where AI supports the processing of evaluation data, the consultant will apply UN Women requirements on data protection and informed consent. Deliverables The consultant will be responsible for the following deliverables: Inception report and evaluation methodology: A report outlining the evaluation scope, evaluation questions, methodology, data collection tools, workplan and proposed structure of the final evaluation report. This will be informed by inception meetings with the programme management team and relevant staff and stakeholders. Draft evaluation report – South Africa: A draft report assessing the Germany-funded programme component in South Africa, covering implementation from 2025 to 2026. The report will present preliminary findings, conclusions and recommendations. Draft evaluation report – Ethiopia and Global component: A draft report assessing Germany-funded programme implementation in Ethiopia and at the global level, covering the period from 2023 to mid-2027. The report will present preliminary findings, conclusions and recommendations. Final evaluation report and presentation : A consolidated final evaluation report incorporating feedback. The report will include: Executive summary (maximum five pages) Introduction, including programme context, evaluation scope, methodology and limitations Key findings and conclusions, including assessment of programme results Recommendations for ongoing and future programming Lessons learned, challenges and good practices Annexes, including the list of interviewees and documents reviewed The consultant will also prepare a presentation of key findings in an accessible format, such as PowerPoint, for a debriefing with UN Women. All deliverables will be reviewed by the programme management team and the evaluation reference group in accordance with UN Women’s evaluation standards. The consultant will incorporate feedback and revise the deliverables to ensure that they meet the required quality standards. Deliverable Expected completion time (due day)  Payment schedule  Inception report, including evaluation methodology 10 December 2026 20%  Draft evaluation report – South Africa (2025 – 2026) 30 January 2027 20

postings.text: Assignment Title: CONSULTING SERVICES FOR TRANSPORT DEMAND AND SUPPLY DATA COLLECTION AND ANALYSIS AND LABOUR AND ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT ASSESSMENT. Reference N. º  AO-ANTT- 565666-CS-CQS The National Land Transport Agency (ANTT) has received a Grant from the World Bank to cover the costs associated with the preparation of the Angola Sustainable Urban Mobility Project and intends to use part of the funds to procure consulting services. The consulting includes: Identify and map the actual public transport network, including informal routes; Estimate transport demand and usage, and validate existing bus data; Provide a baseline for network restructuring, regulatory reform and financial modelling; Collect, validate and supplement existing data on bus services and other public transport operators; Characterise the informal occasional collective transport (OTC) sector, including operators, workers, livelihoods, working conditions and exposure to the effects of the planned reforms; Evaluate the labour and environmental dimensions associated with current operating practices and potential green transition pathways. The National Land Transport Agency invites eligible consulting firms to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested consultants should submit provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are: Legally registered national or international firm (or consortium) with at least 10 years of experience in relevant field. Proven completion of at least 2 (two) similar contracts over the past 5 years, including clear examples of the results delivered. Strong organizational setup, quality control processes, permanent support staff, and access to relevant industry software ( Note: Individual CVs will not be evaluated at this stage ). Established local office, formal in-country partner, or proven ability to mobilize staff and operations in Angola. A brief statement showing a solid grasp of the project's goals, local context, and main challenges. Experience working in Sub-Saharan African countries. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraph 3.13 of the World Bank’s ”6th Procurement Regulations” February 2025, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a subconsultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Terms of Reference and the rules and conditions described in the Procurement Regulations. Further information can be obtained at pmusa.geral@antt.gov.ao, during office hours from 08:00 to 15:00. Expressions of Interest shall be submitted in writing form both Portuguese and English to the aforementioned address, within 12 days from the date of publication.

The role involves developing and implementing strategies for malaria control, generating strategic information, and providing expert advice on malaria prevention and control policies. The consultant will also facilitate partnerships, resource mobilization, and capacity building in member states. This position requires a strong background in public health, epidemiology, and experience in malaria-related activities. Candidate Requirements: Medical degree with postgraduate qualification in public health or related field Minimum of seven years of experience in disease prevention and control Experience in policy formulation and implementation Expert knowledge of malaria epidemiology and control strategies Excellent communication and presentation skills Fluency in English or French, with knowledge of a second language desirable | Job Description - Consultant - Country Support Malaria Specialist (2605022) Consultant - Country Support Malaria Specialist-(2605022) Contractual Arrangement:External consultant Contract Duration (Years, Months, Days):6 Months Job Posting: Nov 17, 2026, 3:49:53 AM Closing Date: Dec 1, 2026, 5:59:00 PM Primary Location: Congo-Brazzaville Organization: AF/DPC Health Promotion, Disease Prevention and Control Schedule: Full-time IMPORTANT NOTICE: Please note that the deadline for receipt of applications indicated above reflects your personal device's system settings. .. Purpose of the consultancy The recruitment of a Consultant - Country Support Malaria Specialist will enhance WHO AFRO’s capacity to provide sustained, country-focused technical support to national malaria programmes, strengthen institutional and technical capacities, promote the systematic use of data and evidence for decision-making, accelerate the adoption and optimization of WHO-recommended innovations, and improve the coordination and effectiveness of technical assistance across countries Background After two decades of substantial progress, malaria control in the WHO African Region has reached a critical inflection point. Progress has stalled, with the Region continuing to account for more than 95% of global malaria cases and deaths and remaining significantly off track towards the 2030 Global Technical Strategy targets. This stagnation is occurring in an increasingly complex operating environment characterized by emerging and intensifying biological threats, including insecticide resistance, the spread of Anopheles stephensi, pfhrp2/3 gene deletions and emerging partial artemisinin resistance. These threats are compounded by climate variability, humanitarian crises and population displacement, which are altering malaria transmission patterns and increasing pressure on already fragile health systems. At the same time, the malaria control landscape is rapidly evolving, with the availability of next-generation insecticide-treated nets and other innovative vector control tools, alongside improved diagnostics, treatments, digital platforms, subnational tailoring approaches and predictive analytics. However, the availability of these innovations has not consistently translated into timely adoption, appropriate targeting or effective scale-up. National malaria programmes in many settings continue to face gaps in institutional and technical capacity, analytical expertise, surveillance systems and coordination mechanisms needed to convert epidemiological and entomological evidence into policy and investment decisions. The Tropical and Vector-borne Disease (TVD) programme of Health Promotion, Disease Prevention and Control (DPC) Cluster/WHO AFFRO has prioritized the position of a Country Support Malaria Specialist. The consultancy would strengthen WHO’s capacity to provide coordinated, timely and evidence-based technical support, promote harmonized approaches, and facilitate collaboration among national programmes, research institutions and partners. Scope of Work The consultant will be expected to perform the following duties: 1. Disease control coordination, partnerships and resource mobilization: Contribute to the development, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of the TVD Plan of action Develop and disseminate technical briefs, guidance materials, case studies, presentations and other knowledge products to support country decision-making and peer learning. Support high-level policy dialogue and advocacy with national authorities and partners to maintain malaria as a political and development priority and strengthen national ownership and accountability. Support countries in strengthening resource mobilization, investment prioritization and the effective use of domestic and external financing, with emphasis on value for money, sustainability and equitable impact. Represent WHO/AFRO in relevant regional, international and national technical meetings, providing authoritative technical advice on malaria control and elimination. 2.    Generation of strategic information and knowledge products: Facilitate periodic epidemiologic analysis and evaluations of malaria service delivery, intervention stratification and health system ecosystems in collaboration with partners and stakeholders within and outside WHO/AFRO;  Contribute to the generation of evidence to further improve the targeting of WHO recommended malaria prevention, control and elimination strategies,  Facilitate strengthening of existing surveillance and M&E systems including surveillance systems for malaria and TVD priority diseases and conditions;  Contribute to the production of various status reports on malaria and other TVD priority diseases.  Facilitate information-sharing through video conferencing, informal consultations and, as required, meeting at the country and inter-country level. Monitor progress of countries against agreed strategic and programme targets, identify implementation bottlenecks and provide recommendations for corrective action. Contribute to communication and advocacy products highlighting country achievements, lessons learned, emerging challenges and opportunities to accelerate malaria control and elimination. 3.    Development of WHO technical products, services, and tools: Provide expert advice to the Member States towards developing and implementing technically coherent malaria prevention and control policies, strategies, guidelines, protocols and plans. Participate in the development of tools/guidelines on malaria prevention and case management strategies in the context of other tropical and vector-borne diseases. Support the development, dissemination, adoption, adaptation and implementation of approved WHO guidance documents, global policy recommendations, technical products and tools for malaria and other vector borne diseases. 4.    Country support facilitation: Provide technical support to countries in line with the technical support plan and the TVD Framework, Contribute to mapping and prioritizing institutions and technical capacities in Member States for WHO capacity strengthening; support partnerships with selected institutions and strengthen their capacity to provide malaria technical support under WHO oversight. Support the development and implementation of regional and country capacity-building policies, strategies and approaches towards the implementation of best practices.  Contribute to the coordinated investment of malaria resources in strengthening health services delivery platforms to deliver optimally for disease control in the region.  Establish and maintain mechanisms to track technical assistance requests, outputs, outcomes and follow-up actions, using this information to improve the responsiveness and effectiveness of WHO country support. and citation in partner or NMP planning process. •    Annual reports published ahead of Regional Committee •    Technical inputs to sub-regional AMDR network meetings documented •    Regional biological threat analytic briefs produced and used to inform surveillance, procurement, strategic planning, and policy dialogue     3    Strengthen scientific leadership and innovation in malaria programmes through research, evidence generation and adoption of new tools and approaches. •    Regional research and innovation agenda on malaria elimination (including insecticide and drug resistance, novel tools and delivery models) •    Oversight and contribution to peer-reviewed publications, policy briefs or flagship technical reports •    Regional knowledge products and dissemination activities on malaria genomics and emerging genetic technologies, including malaria vaccines, new antimalarials, novel vector control tools, gene drive, developed and disseminated to Member States and partners     4    Support countries to optimize integrated malaria service delivery, improving coverage, quality and continuity of services, particularly for high-burden, fragile and underserved populations. •    Country costed prioritized and optimized operational plans  •    High-level TA to address policy, financing, supply chain, service delivery and quality-of-care bottlenecks •    Support for integration of malaria services within PHC, maternal and child health and community platforms •    National Health Sector performance assessments integrating malaria programme reviews  •    Malaria–PHC integration toolkit        Qualifications, experience, skills and languages Educational Qualifications •    Essential: Medical degree with a postgraduate degree/qualification in public health/ epidemiology, clinical care, internal medicine, and/or tropical diseases.  •    Desirable: Training or additional academic specialization in infectious diseases or malaria ;or related medical field will be an asset. The Team The K-12 Teaching and Learning team works to develop the products and approaches that can support teachers to ensure that no K-12 student remains below grade level for longer than 3 years. To do that, we invest in the development, validation, and adoption of effective K-12 curriculum and AI-enabled tutoring solutions, with a focus on math across early learning, middle grades, and high school. Embedded within and across these sub-teams, our Measurement, Learning, and Evaluation (MLE) function ensures that our investments are grounded in strong evidence-based hypotheses, that we collect relevant and timely evidence to test those hypotheses, and that we use that evidence to continuously improve those hypotheses over time. You have expertise in scale measurement methodology, market surveillance, and demand-side research in education . You bring significant experience in the application of that knowledge to support organizational improvement and decision-making. *Our preference is for this role to be located in Seattle, WA. No Visa support is available for this position. *Applications accepted until 5 PM Pacific Time on Monday, December 7th, 2026. enabling deep familiarization with the strategic hypotheses, grants, and grantees within and across those bodies of work Design and manage a portfolio of grants and contracts to monitor, test, and practice to support equitable outcomes for targeted populations Ensure that outputs and learnings from those investments are relevant, timely, and useful to strategy and partner decision-making Support use of evidence for decision-making (40%) Work closely with body of work Deputy Directors and Strategy Officers to ensure that progress and tests of strategy hypotheses are well-communicated and understood by strategy, division, and foundation leadership Support reporting processes, knowledge management systems, capacity-building supports, and learning routines that ensure staff and partners have timely and useful access and sense-making support to apply evidence to improve hypotheses and decision-making Improve and implement strategy-wide approaches to MLE (20%) Connect needs and experiences of portfolio hypothesis testing and improvement to the improvement and implementation of strategy-wide MLE approaches Connect to larger field trends and innovations in MLE and bring back that knowledge to inform and improve strategy-wide approaches Build reputation and awareness of K-12 approaches to MLE by engaging with external experts, conferences, convenings, and other speaking and networking opportunities Your Experience Through a relevant advanced degree or significant prior professional experience, proven expertise in measurement and evaluation methodology, including theories of influence or scale, survey and behavioral research at scale, market monitoring, and demand-side measurement Through a relevant credential or significant prior professional experience, proven ability to credibly communicate complex data and evidence for multiple audiences and support its application to decision-making Significant experience working across multiple teams or portfolios simultaneously, with demonstrated ability to coordinate priorities, maintain coherence, and build trust across diverse stakeholders Significant experience building and managing external partnerships with researchers, evaluators, and market research firms A commitment to meeting the needs of all K-12 students, regardless of background and circumstances, and the ability to apply that commitment to day-to-day work *Must have unrestricted work authorization in the country where this position is located. postings.text: Épidémiologiste / Suivi–Évaluation , SSA, NOB | WHO - World Health Organization Skip to main content Épidémiologiste / Suivi–Évaluation , SSA, NOB WHO - World Health Organization Bujumbura National No grade level Application deadline: November 26, 2026 (8 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The position of Epidemiologist/Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist at WHO in Burundi focuses on enhancing epidemiological surveillance and response to public health threats. The role involves planning, implementing, and evaluating integrated surveillance activities, supporting case investigations, and improving data collection and performance monitoring. The candidate will also contribute to project management and reporting, ensuring alignment with national frameworks and WHO guidelines. This position requires a strong background in epidemiology and project management to effectively address health challenges in the region. Candidate Requirements: University degree in medicine, public health, or epidemiology 2 years of experience in epidemiological surveillance 2 years of experience in health project management Proficiency in SNIS/DHIS2 systems Good command of French and Kirundi Availability for field missions | Job Description - Épidémiologiste / Suivi–Évaluation , SSA, NOB (2604936) Épidémiologiste / Suivi–Évaluation , SSA, NOB-(2604936) Grade:No grade Contractual Arrangement:Special Services Agreement (SSA) Contract Duration (Years, Months, Days):6 months Job Posting: Nov 17, 2026, 5:08:33 AM Closing Date: Nov 26, 2026, 5:59:00 PM Primary Location: Burundi-Bujumbura Organization: AF_BDI Burundi Schedule: Full-time IMPORTANT NOTICE: Please note that the deadline for receipt of applications indicated above reflects your personal device's system settings. .. I – CONTEXTE Le Burundi demeure exposé à un ensemble de menaces sanitaires récurrentes, dont plusieurs ont marqué son paysage épidémiologique au cours des dernières années. L’expérience récente de la pandémie de COVID 19, qui a profondément perturbé les systèmes de santé dans la Région africaine et entraîné une recrudescence globale des infections respiratoires aiguës (IRA), a mis en évidence la nécessité d’un renforcement durable de la surveillance, de l’investigation et de la préparation aux urgences.  Parallèlement, le pays continue de gérer les retombées de la ré émergence du choléra, un problème persistant dans plusieurs pays de la sous-région selon les bulletins de surveillance d’Africa CDC, qui soulignent une co circulation accrue de pathogènes tels que le choléra, la rougeole et Mpox au cours de l’année 2025.  En juillet 2024, le Burundi a confirmé des cas autochtones de Mpox, se classant parmi les pays les plus touchés en Afrique centrale, ce qui a nécessité une mobilisation significative du gouvernement, de l’OMS et des partenaires techniques. La dynamique de transmission du Mpox, notamment les taux élevés d’attaque secondaire documentés en Afrique australe, a montré l’importance d’une surveillance communautaire active et du suivi rapproché des contacts pour interrompre les chaînes de transmission. En outre, le Burundi reste vulnérable aux fièvres hémorragiques virales (FHV), en particulier au vu des flambées répétées observées dans les pays voisins (RDC, Ouganda, Rwanda) dont une épidémie de la maladie à Virus Ebola en cours en RDC, ce qui justifie le maintien d’un niveau élevé de préparation, de surveillance aux Points d’Entrée (PoE), et de capacités d’investigation rapide.  Dans ce contexte multisectoriel et à risques multiples, le Bureau de l’OMS au Burundi appuie le ministère de la Santé Publique afin :(i) de renforcer la surveillance épidémiologique intégrée (ii) de consolider le suivi évaluation (S&E) des interventions sanitaires et la redevabilité envers les bailleurs, et (iii) d’améliorer la coordination des partenariats (dans une approche Une Seule Santé, essentielle à la gestion des menaces émergentes et ré émergentes. II – OBJECTIF Contribuer à l’interruption des chaînes de transmission des maladies à potentiel épidémique au Burundi et à la réduction de la morbidité/mortalité associée, en assurant un appui technique en épidémiologie, en suivi–évaluation dans la mise en œuvre des projets. III – PRINCIPALES ACTIVITÉS/ DESCRIPTION DES TACHES Sous la supervision directe du Team Leader EPR de l'OMS au Burundi et la supervision générale du Représentant de l'OMS au Burundi, le/la titulaire du poste sera chargé de : A. Surveillance épidémiologique & riposte - Planifier, mettre en œuvre et évaluer les activités de surveillance intégrée ; - Appuyer l’investigation des cas et des foyers, le traçage et le suivi des contacts (selon les SOP nationales) et appuyer la documentation des chaînes de transmission ; - Appuyer le renforcement du système sentinelle (FOSAs, PoE) et les supervisions formatives intégrées avec des check‑lists standardisées ; - Renforcer l’interface épidémiologie–laboratoire avec l’INSP/Laboratoire National de Référence (prélèvements, transport, flux de résultats) ; - Contribuer à la production et à l’assurance qualité des SITREP, bulletins hebdomadaires et analyses rapides. B. Suivi–Évaluation, données & performance - Développer/mettre à jour le cadre S&E des projets (cadre logique, indicateurs SMART, référentiels) ; - Mettre en place des plans de collecte de données, des SOP et des audits de qualité ; - Automatiser des tableaux de bord de performance et produire des revues périodiques de performance avec recommandations. - Appuyer la production des évaluations rapides (After Action Reviews, Intra Action Reviews) et des leçons apprises, avec plans d’amélioration suivis. - Appuyer la mesure de l’efficacité des interventions  - Contribuer à l’élaboration de notes conceptuelles, propositions techniques et budgets; appuyer le suivi des subventions. - Veiller à l’alignement des activités sur les cadres nationaux et les recommandations OMS (guidelines, SOP, outils de formation). C. Gestion de projet & rapportage - Élaborer et tenir à jour les plans de travail ; suivre l’avancement (jalons, livrables, risques). - Préparer les rapports techniques et financiers (périodiques et de fin de projets) avec annexes de données vérifiables. - Contribuer au suivi de la conformité (procédures, achats, éthique, sauvegardes), et à la clôture technique des projets. D. Réaliser toutes tâches confiées par le superviseur. IV – QUALIFICATIONS ET COMPÉTENCES REQUISES Éducation - Essentielle: Diplôme universitaire en médecine, santé publique ou épidémiologie ; ou diplôme en gestion/administration de projet avec spécialisation santé. - Souhaitable: Master en santé publique/épidémiologie, FETP/TEPHINET ou équivalent. Expérience professionnelle - Essentielle: 2 ans d’expérience en surveillance épidémiologique (planification, mise en œuvre, suivi et évaluation) et 2 ans en gestion de projets/programmes de santé. - Souhaitable: expérience avec l’OMS, l’UNICEF, Africa CDC ou autres agences du système des Nations Unies ; expérience de coordination multi‑partenaires et de rapports bailleurs. Compétences techniques et informatiques - Maîtrise des systèmes SNIS/DHIS2 et d’analyses des données ; - Connaissance des cadres S&E (théorie du changement, cadre logique) et des normes Compétences de l’OMS - Travail en équipe - Produire des résultats - Communiquer de manière crédible et efficace - Respecter et promouvoir les différences individuelles et culturelles - Instaurer et promouvoir des partenariats dans et au‑delà de l’Organisation Autres exigences - Etre de nationalité burundaise ;  - Disponibilité pour effectuer des missions de terrain ; Langues: Essentielle: Bonne maitrise du français et du Kirundi Désirable: La connaissance de l'anglais et du swahili est souhaitable. Additional Information • This vacancy notice may be used to identify candidates for other similar consultancies at the same level. • Only candidates under serious consideration will be contacted. • A written test may be used as a form of screening. • If your candidature is retained for interview, you will be required to provide, in advance, a scanned copy of the degree(s)/diploma(s)/certificate(s) required for this position. Women, persons with disabilities, and nationals of unrepresented and underrepresented Member States ( https://www.who.int/careers/diversity-equity-and-inclusion ) are strongly encouraged to apply for WHO jobs.  Persons with disabilities can request reasonable accommodations to enable participation in the recruitment process. Requests for reasonable accommodation should be sent through an email to   reasonableaccommodation@who.int   • An impeccable record for integrity and professional ethical standards is essential. WHO prides itself on a workforce that adheres to the highest ethical and professional standards and that is committed to put the WHO Values Charter ( https://www.who.int/about/who-we-are/our-values ) into practice. • WHO has zero tolerance towards sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA), sexual harassment and other types of abusive conduct (i.e., discrimination, abuse of authority and harassment). All members of the WHO workforce have a role to play in promoting a safe and respectful workplace and should report to WHO any actual or suspected cases of SEA, sexual harassment and other types of abusive conduct. To ensure that individuals with a substantiated history of SEA, sexual harassment or other types of abusive conduct are not hired by the Organization, WHO will conduct a background verification of short-listed candidates. • WHO has a smoke-free environment and does not recruit smokers or users of any form of tobacco. • Consultants shall perform the work as independent contractors in a personal capacity, and not as a representative of any entity or authority.  • WHO shall have no responsibility for any taxes, duties, social security contributions or other contributions payable by the Consultant. The Consultant shall be solely responsible for withholding and paying any taxes, duties, social security contributions and any other contributions which are applicable to the Consultant in each location/jurisdiction in which the work hereunder is performed, and the Consultant shall not be entitled to any reimbursement thereof by WHO. • Please note that WHO’s contracts are conditional on members of the workforce confirming that they are vaccinated as required by WHO before undertaking a WHO assignment, except where a medical condition does not allow such vaccination, as certified by the WHO Staff Health and Wellbeing Services (SHW). The successful candidate will be asked to provide relevant evidence related to this condition. postings.text: SVN/2026/052Migration Health Nurse (Resettlement & Health Assessment), Makassar | IOM - International Organization for Migration Skip to main content SVN/2026/052Migration Health Nurse (Resettlement & Health Assessment), Makassar IOM - International Organization for Migration Makassar National GS-5, General Service - No need for Higher Education - Locally recruited position level Speaks Farsi, Arabic, English, Tamil Application deadline: December 01, 2026 (13 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The Migration Health Nurse will support the National Migration Health Officer in managing health assessment activities for refugees in Indonesia. This role involves coordinating with external partners, maintaining medical records, and ensuring the quality of health assessments. The nurse will also assist in training and vaccination management, while adhering to ethical standards and promoting the dignity of migrants. The position requires a commitment to confidentiality and effective communication in a culturally diverse environment. Candidate Requirements: University degree in nursing with valid Indonesian nursing registration Minimum two years of experience in IME/Health Insurance field Experience in operating room and large health assessments Paramedical skills including communication and nursing care Fluency in English and Bahasa Indonesia Job Description Reference No.              : SVN/2026/052 Position Title               : Migration Health Nurse (Resettlement & Health Assessment)  Duty Station                 : Makassar  Organization Unit       : Health Care Unit Classification                : G-5 Type of Appointment : Special Short-Term Contract Report to                      :   National Migration Health Officer  Estimated Start Date   : As soon as possible Closing Date                  : 1 December 2026 Introduction Established in 1951, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) is a related organization of the United Nations (UN), and as the leading UN agency in the field of migration and works closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners. IOM is dedicated to promoting humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It does so by providing services and advice to governments and migrants. Operational in Indonesia for more than 40 years, IOM Indonesia is one of the large IOM missions working on a wide range of activities in partnership with the Government of Indonesia, civil society, private sector actors, migrants and communities.  IOM Indonesia is engaged in several thematic areas, including Counter Trafficking and Labour Migration (CT/LM), Mobility and Resilience, Immigration and Border Management (IBM), Migrant Assistance, Migration Health, and Resettlement and Voluntary Returns. IOM aims to constantly enhance the quality of its resettlement activities as part of the Organization’s principled and people-centred programming and in the interest of assisting the people as best we can to provide safe and dignified resettlement process. The resettlement health assessment unit provides essential support to States in resettling refugees and other humanitarian entrance specifically in health assessment and related assistant. IOM’s pre departure health activities as well as health assistance during the travel ensure that refugees’ health needs are addressed prior to departure, that they are fit to travel, and that appropriate arrangements can be made for reception and continuity of care, when needed.  Under the direct supervision of National Migration Health Officer and overall Supervision of the Chief Migration Health Officer in close coordination with National Programme Officer (RSR Health) and Health Resettlement team in Tangerang, the incumbent will assist in the implementation of the Migration Health Assessments Programme and other migration health related activities in IOM Indonesia. The incumbent is expected to carry out his/her duties in accordance with medico-legal, moral and ethical standards with due respect for gender and socio-cultural differences and human dignity of the migrants    Responsibilities Responsibilities and Accountabilities Provide support to the National Migration Health Officer in establishing and maintaining optimal workflow in all health assessment-related activities in Indonesia and management of the routine health assessment programme for Refugees; Coordinates with external counterparts and IOM colleagues to schedule and implement the IOM migration health assessment activities for refugees as necessary; Under the guidance of the National Migration Health Officer maintain the overall quality and integrity of medical results/documents/files before they are submitted to the respective embassies; Establish and maintain a schedulling & filing system for all Immigration Medical Exams (IME) records; Maintain accurate and confidential electronic and paper-based medical records, ensuring that all health assessment outcomes, laboratory results, and vaccination records are documented in accordance with IOM procedures. Prepare reports and statistical summaries as required while maintaining strict compliance with data protection, confidentiality, and organizational record-keeping standards. Provide input in the preparation and suggest updates of standard operating procedures based on latest information received from authorities requesting Immigration Medical Exams (IME); Assure authentication of identity of IME clients, that all samples collected for IME purposes are directly observed for quality and quantity including preparation before collection, anonymity of samples and arrange timely, cold chain assured delivery to specific laboratories as necessary and assist the National Migration Health Officer   in medical examination including collecting medical history, checking vital signs, weight, height, visual acuity, implementing fraud prevention measures and providing overall counselling of the IME process when health assessment activities are performed by IOM physicians Support Health Assessment Programme Administrator in liaising with Manila Migration Health Department Global Support Unit in relation to statistical reports and validation of health assessment data; Responsible to assist the implementation of monitoring on treatment whenever needed, example: effective, verifiable, documented and safe directly observed therapy (DOT) for those patients deemed by the IOM migration health physicians in need of tuberculosis treatment, following international/ national guidelines of respective international/ national TB treatment guidelines ; Ensures that all necessary pre-departure treatments are completed in coordination with the migration health physician; Responsible to facilitate training with various topics such as communication with client, how to become a good trainer, skill such as vital sign, body measurement, vaccination, any infectious disease outbreak, including COVID-19, measles, polio, diphtheria and others communicable diseases. and experience in coordination to hold the training ; Responsible in vaccination management such as coordination on vaccination in nurse level in immunization management system, cold chain management, any infectious disease outbreak, including COVID-19, measles, polio, diphtheria and others communicable diseases, schedule arrangement, quality control vaccination missing and exceeding report ; Perform other duties as may be assigned.   Qualifications Required Qualifications and Experience Education University degree from an accredited academic institution in nursing with current valid Indonesian nursing registration and/or practice license (STR/SIP) as required by national regulations. Willingness to obtain, maintain, or renew the required professional licenses and practice permits through coordination with relevant professional associations and regulatory authorities to ensure compliance with national medico-legal requirements, or; Completed minimum a diploma in nursing subject (equal to Amd.Kep for Indonesian in academic institution) with at least 5 (five) years relevant work experience and valid certificate as above.   Accredited Universities are those listed in the  UNESCO World Higher Education Database. Experience Indonesian national with Minimum two years of experience in IME/Health Insurance field at a supervisory capacity; Experience in operating room and in large health assessments screenings and as national trainer or well-trained as a trainer with various topics, an advantage; Experience in paramedical skills including, but not limited to, good communication with client, nursing care such  as vital sign, body measurement, vaccination, surveillance and  infectious disease outbreak, including COVID-19, measles, polio, diphtheria and others communicable diseases;   Skills Able to maintain confidentiality and discretion in appropriate areas of work; Excellent communication and negotiation skills; Ability to prepare clear and concise reports; Proficient in computer applications: Ms-Office; Understanding of electronic medical record;  Ability to Identifies the immediate and peripheral clients of own work; Clearly communicates, and listens to feedback on, changing priorities and procedures; Persistent, calm, and polite in the face of challenges and stress;  Able to work effectively with people from different cultures by adapting to relevant cultural contexts; Knowledgeable about and promotes IOM core mandate and migration solutions.   Languages All IOM staff members in all categories are required to be fluent in one of the IOM's official languages (English, French, Spanish). For this position, fluency in English and Bahasa Indonesia is required (oral and written). Proficiency in languages spoken by migrants (Farsi, Arabic, Tamil, Rohingya dialect) is an advantage Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments. Required Competencies IOM’s competency framework can be found at this  link . Competencies will be assessed during the selection process. Values  - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values: Inclusion and respect for diversity : Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion. Integrity and transparency : Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct. Professionalism : Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges. Courage : Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance. Empathy : Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated. Core Competencies  – behavioural indicators Level 1 Teamwork : Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results. Delivering results : Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes. Managing and sharing knowledge : Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate. Accountability : Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work. Communication : Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way. Managerial Competencies  – behavioural indicators Level 2, if with direct reports Leadership : Provides a clear sense of direction, leads by example and demonstrates the ability to carry out the Organization’s vision. Assists others to realize and develop their leadership and professional potential. Empowering others : Creates an enabling environment where staff can contribute their best and develop their potential. Building Trust : Promote

postings.text: International Consultant – Clinical Trials, Research Governance and Responsible AI, WHO Western Pacific Regional Office, Manila, Philippines | WHO - World Health Organization Skip to main content International Consultant – Clinical Trials, Research Governance and Responsible AI, WHO Western Pacific Regional Office, Manila, Philippines WHO - World Health Organization Remote | Manila International B level Speaks English Application deadline: December 01, 2026 (13 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The WHO Western Pacific Regional Office is seeking an International Consultant to provide technical support in clinical trials, research governance, and responsible AI. The consultant will assess clinical trial ecosystems, strengthen health research governance, and develop guidance for AI in health systems. This role requires collaboration with member states to enhance their research capabilities and ensure ethical practices. The position is home-based with travel expected for consultations and support activities. Candidate Requirements: University degree in public health, epidemiology, or related field Five years of experience in health research projects Experience in evidence synthesis for health policy Engagement with research institutions in the WPR Capacity-building experience in clinical trials Strong scientific writing and communication skills Excellent interpersonal and negotiation skills Quantitative and qualitative research skills Fluency in English | Job Description - International Consultant – Clinical Trials, Research Governance and Responsible AI, WHO Western Pacific Regional Office, Manila, Philippines (2605027) International Consultant – Clinical Trials, Research Governance and Responsible AI, WHO Western Pacific Regional Office, Manila, Philippines-(2605027) Contractual Arrangement:External consultant Contract Duration (Years, Months, Days):11 Job Posting: Nov 17, 2026, 1:57:12 AM Closing Date: Dec 1, 2026, 5:59:00 PM Primary Location: Philippines-Manila Organization: WP/DSI Data Strategy and Innovation Schedule: Full-time IMPORTANT NOTICE: Please note that the deadline for receipt of applications indicated above reflects your personal device's system settings. .. Purpose of the Consultancy The Research, Ethics and Innovation Unit (REI) under the Data, Strategy and Innovation (DSI) Division at WHO Regional Office for the Western Pacific (WPRO) is seeking a consultant to provide technical support on the team’s projects and activities in research and innovation for health. Background Member States in the Western Pacific are working to strengthen their clinical trial capabilities and broader health research governance, including national policies, research ethics and priority-setting. At the same time, the growing use of AI in health systems creates a need for practical guidance, evidence and capacity building to support its responsible use and governance. The consultant is expected to support both pillars of research and innovation ecosystem strengthening and provide country support as needed. Deliverables Output 1: Technical review and assessment of clinical trial ecosystems and AI in clinical trials Deliverable 1.1: Conduct a technical review on the use of AI in clinical trials, including applications, anticipated benefits and risks, and governance considerations. The consultant will work under the supervision of the WHO country representative and will be responsible for assessing existing blood bank capacities, training regional actors, and creating integrated monitoring and evaluation frameworks. Key deliverables include ten budgeted regional plans and a national performance framework. The role requires expertise in public health, transfusion medicine, and strategic planning. Candidate Requirements: Doctorate in medicine or pharmacy specialized in transfusion medicine Minimum 5 years of relevant experience in public health or transfusion medicine Experience in health policy formulation and strategic planning Proven skills in designing monitoring and evaluation frameworks Excellent knowledge of the Cameroonian health system Strong analytical and synthesis skills Leadership and facilitation abilities Ability to work autonomously and meet tight deadlines Fluency in French or English and practical knowledge of the other | Job Description - Consultation National Elaboration Plan Regionaux Quinquennaux et Plan de Suivi et d'Evaluation CNTS du Cameroun (2603934) Consultation National Elaboration Plan Regionaux Quinquennaux et Plan de Suivi et d'Evaluation CNTS du Cameroun-(2603934) Contractual Arrangement:External consultant Contract Duration (Years, Months, Days):2 Months Job Posting: Nov 17, 2026, 5:05:21 AM Closing Date: Nov 30, 2026, 5:59:00 PM Primary Location: Cameroon-Yaounde Organization: AF_CMR Cameroon Schedule: Full-time IMPORTANT NOTICE: Please note that the deadline for receipt of applications indicated above reflects your personal device's system settings. . 1. Area of expertise Consultation National pour l'Elaboration des Plan Regionaux Quinquennaux et des Plan de Suivi et d'Evaluation du Centre National de Transfusion Sanguine du Cameroun 2. Purpose of consultancy Sous la coordination générale du Représentant pays de l’OMS et la supervision directe du Team Lead du cluster HSS au bureau OMS-Cameroun, le consultant sera chargé développer les plans régionaux de micro-planification de communication, de sensibilisation, de collecte de sang (2026-2030), ainsi qu'un système intégré de suivi-évaluation. De manière spécifique, il devra :   Diagnostic et État des Lieux : Réaliser un inventaire des banques de sang et évaluer les capacités de communication existantes au niveau des Districts de Santé.  Renforcement des Capacités : Former les acteurs régionaux et de district à la méthodologie de micro-planification de communication et de collecte.  Élaboration des Micro-plans : Développer 10 plans régionaux budgétisés intégrant la sensibilisation, le recrutement des donneurs et les stratégies de collecte.  Plan de Suivi-Évaluation : Concevoir un cadre de performance national avec des indicateurs d'impact clairs pour la période 2026-2030.  Cadre Collaboratif : Générer un mécanisme de synergie entre les acteurs déconcentrés, les associations et les communautés Selon le rapport d'évaluation des connaissances, attitudes et pratiques relatives au don de sang au Cameroun, l'exposition à l'information sur le don de sang est faible dans l'ensemble et constitue à cet égard un facteur de contrainte. Peu de sujets sont exposés aux informations relatives au don de sang, et notamment l'information concernant les éléments motivants tels que le caractère sécuritaire pour la santé du donneur. Seulement 34,8% des répondants affirment avoir déjà entendu des messages sur le don de sang ; moins de 1 sujet sur 10 (8,8%) a entendu un message sur le fait que donner régulièrement de son sang a un caractère sécuritaire. Les barrières socioculturelles telles que le niveau d'instruction, le poids des us et croyances constituent un frein à la mise en place du système de transfusion sanguine au Cameroun basé sur un opérateur unique, le Centre National de Transfusion Sanguine (CNTS). Les défis à relever pour le fonctionnement optimal de ce nouveau Système reposent sur trois principaux piliers :  • L'adhésion des communautés au don de sang et l'instauration de la culture du don de sang ; • L'organisation des communautés pour les collectes de sang régulières ; • La mise en place au sein des communautés des groupes/pool de donneurs réguliers. Dans l'optique de combler le déficit d'informations, de développer la culture du don éthique de sang au sein des communautés et de susciter l'adhésion des populations, il est important de mener des activités de sensibilisation et communication, d'organiser des collectes de sang au sein des communautés. Tout cela nécessite d'élaborer au niveau régional avec les Districts de Santé et les AODS une micro-planification avec un plan intégré de suivi-évaluation. 3. Background Le Projet de Renforcement du Système National de Transfusion Sanguine (PRESYNATS) occupe une place clé dans les dispositifs et mécanismes mis en place par le Gouvernement dans le cadre du train de réformes de la transfusion sanguine. En effet, le PRESYNATS est une offre consistante des capacités et des ressources visant à contribuer à la réduction de la morbidité et de la mortalité liées à l'absence de sang sécurisé. Cette ambition générale est désagrégée en deux objectifs spécifiques complémentaires, à savoir :  • Assurer l'accès universel et l'utilisation du sang sécurisé et de qualité. • Promouvoir un environnement social favorable à la transfusion sanguine. En dépit de diverses contraintes juridiques, programmatiques et financières ayant largement et longuement perturbé son rythme de mise en œuvre, la pertinence des centres d'intérêt du PRESYNATS est telle que le Gouvernement et la BID ont tenu à convenir de la restructuration de ce projet, afin que ses activités résiduelles soient réalisées sous un délai de deux ans. Ce consensus déterminant a été obtenu et formalisé dans un contexte où le Centre National de Transfusion Sanguine (CNTS), Opérateur unique de la transfusion, et bénéficiaire privilégié des activités financées par le PRESYNATS, est fonctionnel et déploie progressivement ses structures et ses activités. Son ambition, telle que déclinée dans ses Orientations stratégiques, est de doter le Cameroun d'un Système de transfusion sanguine sécurisé, efficace, pérenne, levier d'amélioration de l'offre de soins, capable d'offrir à tous les patients, du sang et des produits sanguins de qualité. Aussi, le CNTS s'est-il engagé à « Garantir la sécurité, l'accessibilité et la disponibilité du sang et des produits sanguins de qualité et ses dérivés afin de couvrir les besoins d'au moins 60% des besoins en produits sanguins de qualité d'ici la fin 2025 ». Les objectifs spécifiques qui découlent de ces orientations sont :  • Renforcer le cadre infrastructurel, organisationnel et normatif de la transfusion sanguine de manière à rendre opérationnelles aux normes 50% des structures de transfusion sanguine d'ici la fin 2025. • Mettre en place une stratégie de recrutement des donneurs de sang de manière à obtenir 30% de donneurs bénévoles, volontaires et non rémunérés d'ici la fin 2025. • Développer et mettre en œuvre par des personnels qualifiés les bonnes pratiques transfusionnelles dans 50% des structures de transfusion sanguine d'ici la fin 2025. • Assurer la gouvernance effective par l'Opérateur unique du sang du système de transfusion sanguine à tous les niveaux de manière à satisfaire au moins 50% des besoins en produits sanguins de qualité d'ici la fin 2025. Dans ce sillage, il est fort appréciable de constater que le paquet d'activités sous financement du PRESYNATS, et dont la préparation des Termes de référence et Fiches techniques est confiée au CNTS, s'inscrit opportunément en droite ligne des objectifs ci-dessus définis. 4. Deliverables - Package des dix (10) plans régionaux quinquennaux (2026-2030) de micro-planification (communication, sensibilisation, collecte de sang), dûment budgétisés. - Document du cadre national intégré de suivi-évaluation, comprenant la matrice de performance (indicateurs d’impact et de produit), les outils de collecte de données et le mécanisme opérationnel de synergie des acteurs. - Rapport final de fin de mission compilant l'ensemble du processus, les leçons apprises et les recommandations stratégiques pour le CNTS et l'OMS. 5. Qualifications, experience, skills and languages Educational Qualification - Essentiel: Doctorat en médecine ou pharmacie spécialisé en transfusion sanguine - Souhaitable: Diplôme d’études supérieures en suivi – évaluation, économie de la santé, santé publique, gestion des projets, communication pour le développement ou planification. Experience - Expérience globale : Minimum de cinq (05) ans d'expérience professionnelle pertinente, à l'échelle nationale ou internationale, dans le domaine de la santé publique, de la pharmacie, de la médecine ou de la transfusion sanguine. - Expertise en planification : Expérience confirmée dans la formulation de politiques de santé, l'élaboration de plans stratégiques nationaux, ou la micro-planification des services de santé (en particulier les stratégies de collecte de sang ou de vaccination). - Suivi et Évaluation : Expérience pratique avérée dans la conception de cadres logiques, de systèmes intégrés de suivi-évaluation, et dans la définition d'indicateurs de performance (KPIs) opérationnels et d'impact. - Connaissance du système de santé : Excellente connaissance du système de santé camerounais, de son organisation déconcentrée (Régions, Districts de santé) et du fonctionnement des structures communautaires (AODS, associations). - Expérience partenariale : Expérience de travail réussie avec le Ministère de la Santé Publique, des agences de coopération internationale (OMS, BID) ou des programmes de renforcement des systèmes de santé (ex: PRESYNATS). Skills/Knowledge - Esprit d'analyse et de synthèse : Capacité à traiter, structurer et synthétiser des données quantitatives et qualitatives complexes provenant de multiples districts de santé pour en faire des plans opérationnels clairs. - Leadership et facilitation : Excellentes compétences en animation de groupes, en facilitation d'ateliers participatifs et en négociation auprès de parties prenantes d'horizons divers (médecins, administratifs, leaders communautaires). - Autonomie et rigueur : Forte capacité à travailler de manière autonome sous la coordination de l'OMS, à prioriser les tâches dans un calendrier contractuel serré (02 mois) et à produire des livrables de haute qualité. - Communication interpersonnelle : Excellentes aptitudes relationnelles, diplomatie et sensibilité culturelle pour naviguer efficacement face aux barrières socioculturelles et susciter l'adhésion autour du projet. Languages and level required (Basic/Intermediate/Expert) Connaissance approfondie (parlée et écrite) du français ou de l’anglais et une connaissance pratique de l’autre. 9.
