postings.text: Consultant on leaving no one behind survey data analysis | UNESCAP - United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific Skip to main content Consultant on leaving no one behind survey data analysis UNESCAP - United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific Bangkok CON level Speaks English, French Application deadline: November 24, 2026 (6 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP) is seeking a consultant to support survey data analysis and visualization using the Leaving No One Behind (LNOB) methodology. The consultant will process and analyze household survey data from Bhutan and Pakistan, validate results, and prepare briefing notes. Additionally, the consultant will review and validate preliminary results from other countries and assist in publishing findings on the ESCAP LNOB Platform. This role requires expertise in data analysis, particularly using R programming, and a strong attention to detail. Candidate Requirements: Master’s degree in data science, economics, statistics or related fields At least 1 year of data analysis and visualization experience At least 1 year of intermediate coding experience with R Experience with household survey data processing and analysis Experience with Demographic and Health Surveys (DHS) or Multiple Indicator Cluster Surveys (MICS) Experience in drafting and publishing technical papers Fluency in English Result of Service Under the overall supervision of the Chief, Sustainable Socioeconomic Transformation Section (SETS), or her designate, the data analyst shall process and analyze several household surveys, validate results, draft briefing notes and support publication of results online both on the ESCAP LNOB Platform directly and through succinct knowledge products. Work Location Bangkok (in-person) Expected duration 01/01/27-31/05/27 Duties and Responsibilities The Sustainable Socioeconomic Transformation Section (SETS) within the Social Development Division of the United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP) has pioneered innovative data tools that help policymakers analyze inequality of opportunity and identify furthest behind groups in a range of basic opportunities, such as nutrition, education, healthcare and access to basic services, including basic drinking water, sanitation and clean energy, among others. This work builds on ESCAP’s experience in applying the Classification and Regression Tree (CART) analysis and the Dissimilarity Index on nationally representative survey data, namely Demographic and Health Surveys (DHS) and Multiple Indicator Cluster Surveys (MICS). Since 2019, SETS has generated a wealth of information on inequality of opportunity at national and subnational levels which led to the development of the ESCAP Leaving No One Behind (LNOB) Platform and its official online publication in 2023. SETS keeps maintaining and expanding this platform which currently covers 34 countries in Asia and the Pacific and 19 SDG indicators. Capacity-building activities took place in over 13 countries in close coordination with the National Statistics Offices who increasingly share other nationally representative household surveys with ESCAP including Household Income and Expenditure Surveys and Labour Force Surveys. At the same time, the LNOB results have been incorporated in Voluntary National Review (VNR) reports of 20 countries in 2020-2026 period. VNRs help countries take stock of their progress in the implementation of the 2030 Agenda on Sustainable Development. Building on this momentum, ESCAP has recently received technical assistance requests from member States to analyze new and country-specific survey data and integrate results in their national data dashboards. The requests include not only to deepen and customize the LNOB analysis but also widen its breadth by using other national data sources. To respond to this growing and substantial demand, ESCAP is implementing a technical cooperation project (2026-2029) targeting five countries (i.e., Bhutan, Indonesia, Sri Lanka, Pakistan and Viet Nam) with the aim to strengthen capacity among national and provincial policymakers and technical specialists to undertake LNOB analysis with a focus on their priority policy areas in social development. The ultimate objective is to ensure that relevant and robust LNOB analysis is independently generated within countries to inform inclusive and evidence-based policymaking. In this context, SETS is hiring a consultant to support SETS with survey data analysis and visualization by using the LNOB methodology in open-source statistical software programme R. The consultant will process survey data from Bhutan and Pakistan and apply the LNOB algorithm to obtain preliminary results on a range of selected outcomes which may include indicators relating to education, health and employment, among others. The consultant will validate the results against the published reports of data producers. Based on these results, the consultant will prepare succinct briefing notes and slide deck. In addition, consultant will review and validate preliminary results SETS had already obtained from analysing survey data from Cambodia, Fiji and Thailand and export them to the ESCAP LNOB Platform along with results from Bhutan and Pakistan. This process will include exporting metadata associated with these surveys, as well. Finally, as more survey data from multiple sources become available in Asia and the Pacific become available (e.g. DHS, MICS or Global Financial Inclusion Database), the consultant will be responsible for imitating the preliminary analysis, validate the results against published reports and support ESCAP to publish the results. Qualifications/special skills Master’s degree in data science, computer programming, economic, statistics or other related fields with emphasis on quantitative skills. At least 1 year of data analysis and visualization experience in the areas of economics, finance, development or social sciences is required. At least 1 year of coding experience at intermediate level with R is required. Experience with processing, cleaning and analysing household survey with R, STATA or other software programs, particularly experience working with Demographic and Health Surveys (DHS), Multiple Indicator Cluster surveys (MICS), or other national household survey data is desirable. Experience with research and data analysis in the context of Asia and the Pacific is desirable. Experience with data visualization and developing communication materials is desirable. Demonstrated ability to work with a high degree of accuracy and attention to detail, including the review and quality assurance of data, reports, and other deliverables. Experience in statistics and proficiency in R programming is required. Experience in analyzing survey data using R or other programming language is required. Experience in drafting and publishing technical papers is required. Languages English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For the consultancy advertised, fluency in English is required. Additional Information Not available. Background National Public Health Institutes (NPHIs) are science-based government bodies that provide national leadership and coordination of public health functions, and that promote health and prevent, detect and respond to public health threats. Consolidating dispersed public health functions under one credible, visible institution is now widely recognised as one of the most effective investments a country can make in population health and building health-system resilience. WHO sets out twelve Essential Public Health Functions (EPHFs), which guide the creation and development of NPHIs as well as to define an NPHI’s scope. In Zimbabwe, the Public Health Institute of Zimbabwe (PHIZ) is being established and operationalised by the Government of Zimbabwe, Ministry of Health and Childcare, spanning governance and institutional development, the legal and regulatory framework, public health surveillance, laboratory systems, health information systems, and workforce development. dispersed across MOHCC and allied institutions, give Government, other partners a single instrument for aligning and tracking the progress of PHIZ, and build a defensible case for sustained domestic budget allocation for the PHIZ.This Terms of Reference outline the technical support required for the development of the first Costed Strategic Plan for the Public Health Institute of Zimbabwe. * 2. ** Deliverables * 1. * Specific tasks to be performed The details of specific tasks that will be carried out in the course of the assignment are as shown below: Develop a Costed Strategic Plan for the postings.text: Food Security Analysis Specialist | FAO - Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations Skip to main content Food Security Analysis Specialist FAO - Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations South Africa International Consultant - Contractors Agreement level Speaks Chinese, Arabic, English, French, Russian, Spanish Application deadline: December 01, 2026 (13 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The Food Security Analysis Specialist will support the development and implementation of resilience programs in Southern Africa, focusing on food security and nutrition. This role involves providing technical assistance to FAO country offices, conducting food and nutrition security analyses, and collaborating with various stakeholders. The specialist will also engage in resource mobilization efforts and capacity development activities. The position requires strong coordination skills and the ability to work with diverse partners to enhance food security initiatives. Organizational Setting The FAO Subregional Office for Southern Africa (SFS) is a technical hub with the principal function of overall identification, planning and implementation of FAO's priority activities based on the needs of the member countries in the subregion. It is responsible for developing, promoting, overseeing and implementing agreed strategies for addressing sub-regional food security, nutrition, agriculture, forestry, fisheries and rural development priorities. The FAO Resilience Hub for Southern Africa (SFS-REOSA), which is an integral part of SFS, leads FAO’s work to build resilience, reduce vulnerability and risks of food and nutrition insecurity by strengthening the productive capacity and livelihoods of vulnerable groups in the subregion. It provides support, at subregional and country levels, to the overall identification, planning and implementation to respond to the needs of the member countries and regional bodies in the subregion. Reporting Lines Under the overall supervision of the Subregional Coordinator for Southern Africa, the direct supervision of the SFS Subregional Resilience Officer, and in close collaboration with the SFS multi-disciplinary team, the Food Security Analysis Specialist will support resilience programme development and implementation, including resource mobilization. Technical Focus Provide support to the resilience programme development and implementation, in resource mobilization efforts, in close collaboration with country offices, the Regional Office for Africa, the Office of Emergencies and Resilience and partners. Tasks and responsibilities DRR technical work and food security analysis • Provide technical support to FAO country offices in the design, implementation and operationalization of resilience programme. • Undertake subregional and support country food and nutrition security analyses • Provide technical support to the SADC Secretariat, relevant regional bodies and partners in the development and implementation of the resilience programme • Provide support to the country offices on disaster risk management, anticipatory action, including risk profiling, impact-based forecasting, trigger and threshold development, decision-making protocols and activation procedures. • Undertake benefit-cost, return-on-investment and counterfactual analyses and process, validate and document multi-source data for impact-based forecasting and trigger analysis. • Analyze food security and vulnerability data, including FIES, food consumption and coping indicators, IPC classifications and SOFI indicators, to inform anticipatory action targeting, triggers, monitoring and reporting. • Contribute to other FAO food security information products required at regional and global level • Design, deliver and follow up capacity-development activities for government officials, SADC institutions and partners, including regional training, technical working sessions and training of trainers and orientation sessions; • Contribute to the preparation of audience appropriate learning materials and standard operating procedures; and provide remote technical support on food and nutrition security monitoring and anticipatory action. Project Coordination and interagency collaboration • Provide support to the SFS-REOSA project portfolio management, identify opportunities for programme expansion and contribute to the formulation of related documents. • In close liaison with relevant Technical Officers, participate in technical meetings organized by the Regional Inter-Agency Standing Committee for Southern Africa (RIASCO), Food and Nutrition Security Working Group (FNSWG) and the Regional Anticipatory Action Working Group (RAAWG) and its technical units including Integrated Food Security Phase Classification. • Develop and maintain strong linkages with other UN Agencies, development partners and regional bodies to facilitate information sharing, technical exchanges and consensus-building; • Perform any other duties, as required. CANDIDATES WILL BE ASSESSED AGAINST THE FOLLOWING Minimum Requirements • Advanced university degree in disaster risk management, agricultural or development economics, food security and nutrition, climate or environmental science, statistics or a related field. postings.text: Consultant International pour les Test d'Assurances Qualité au CNTS du Cameroun | WHO - World Health Organization Skip to main content Consultant International pour les Test d'Assurances Qualité au CNTS du Cameroun WHO - World Health Organization Yaoundé International Band level A level Application deadline: November 30, 2026 (12 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The WHO is seeking an international consultant to assist the National Blood Transfusion Center (CNTS) in Cameroon in establishing an effective quality management system (QMS) that meets international standards. The consultant will evaluate the current QMS, propose necessary procedures, and develop a comprehensive action plan for implementation. Responsibilities include training CNTS staff on QMS requirements and ensuring compliance with accreditation standards. This role is crucial for enhancing the safety and quality of blood transfusion services in Cameroon. Candidate Requirements: Medical or biological pharmacist degree Postgraduate specialization in Quality Management or Blood Transfusion Experience in blood banks Proven track record in implementing QMS in blood transfusion centers Expertise in international accreditation standards (ISO 15189, ISO 9001) Minimum 3 years in transfusion sector in developing countries Excellent written and oral communication in French and/or English Ability to work in multidisciplinary teams | Job Description - Consultant International pour les Test d'Assurances Qualité au CNTS du Cameroun (2603309) Consultant International pour les Test d'Assurances Qualité au CNTS du Cameroun-(2603309) Contractual Arrangement:External consultant Contract Duration (Years, Months, Days):2 Months Job Posting: Nov 17, 2026, 5:04:24 AM Closing Date: Nov 30, 2026, 5:59:00 PM Primary Location: Cameroon-Yaounde Organization: AF_CMR Cameroon Schedule: Full-time IMPORTANT NOTICE: Please note that the deadline for receipt of applications indicated above reflects your personal device's system settings. . 1. Area of expertise Recrutement d'un consultant international pour les tests d'assurance qualité au Centre National de Transfusion Sanguine du Cameroun. 2. Purpose of consultancy Sous la coordination générale du Représentant pays de l’OMS et la supervision directe du Team Lead du cluster HSS au bureau OMS-Cameroun, le consultant sera chargé d'accompagner le CNTS dans la mise en place d'un système de management de la qualité efficace et conforme aux exigences internationales. De manière spécifique, il devra :   Faire un état des lieux du SMQ existant dans les banques de sang hospitalières et le CNTS ;  Répertorier et proposer les différents centres collaborateurs OMS habiletés à accréditer le CNTS et ses unités opérationnelles ;  Mettre en place les procédures et instructions nécessaires au bon fonctionnement du SMQ ;  Elaborer et proposer un plan d'actions pour la mise en place d'un système qualité dans le CNTS et ses unités opérationnelles, en adéquation avec la politique de transfusion sanguine nationale et suivant les normes et le cahier de charges de l'organisme accréditeur (Centre collaborateur OMS) choisi, et la pérennisation dudit système ;  Développer et exploiter les outils de suivi (indicateurs de performance) de la qualité ;  Accompagner la constitution d'un fonds documentaire nécessaire au niveau du CNTS et ses unités opérationnelles ;  Proposer une liste d'organismes pour le contrôle qualité externe ;  Accompagner le CNTS et ses unités opérationnelles pour la mise en œuvre du plan d'actions suscité ;  Former le personnel du CNTS et ses unités opérationnelles aux exigences du SMQ. 3. Background La transfusion sanguine est une composante importante des soins de santé. Elle permet de sauver des millions de vies humaines chaque année, dans les situations de routine et d'urgence. Elle facilite les interventions médicales et chirurgicales complexes et améliore de manière spectaculaire la qualité et l'espérance de vie des patients atteints de toutes sortes d'affections aiguës ou chroniques. Au Cameroun, à la faveur du Décret N 2019/067 du 12 février 2019 portant organisation et fonctionnement du Centre National de Transfusion Sanguine, Opérateur Unique en matière de transfusion sanguine, l'environnement de la transfusion sanguine est en profonde restructuration. Cette restructuration, qui impose un changement radical de paradigme dans le système existant doit s'opérer progressivement en garantissant dans tout son processus, la disponibilité, l'accessibilité et la qualité des produits sanguins. Dans cette optique, le projet de Renforcement du Système national de transfusion sanguine sous financement de la Banque Islamique de Développement (BID) vise à mettre en place au Cameroun un système moderne de transfusion sanguine susceptible de contribuer au fonctionnement optimal et harmonieux du Système de santé. L'objectif général du projet est de contribuer à la réduction de la mortalité et de la morbidité liées à l'absence du sang sécurisé. Spécifiquement, il s'agit entre autres d'assurer l'accès universel et l'utilisation du sang sécurisé et de qualité sur toute l'étendue du territoire national. Afin de promouvoir la sécurité, l'accessibilité des produits sanguins de qualité et réduire les risques liés à la transfusion sanguine, l'Organisation Mondiale de la Santé (OMS) recommande aux autorités nationales de santé publique une stratégie intégrée comportant 05 axes dont l'un est la mise en œuvre de systèmes qualité efficaces couvrant tous les aspects des activités des Banques de sang hospitalières et incluant la gestion de la qualité, le développement et l'instauration de normes de qualité ; la mise en place de systèmes documentaires efficaces ; la formation de l'ensemble du personnel et l'évaluation régulière de la qualité. Aussi, la qualité constante, la sécurité et la disponibilité des produits sanguins ne peuvent être obtenues sans systèmes qualité efficaces qui permettront de maintenir la sécurité globale du processus transfusionnel, depuis le recrutement des donneurs jusqu'à la transfusion des produits sanguins et au suivi des receveurs. L'obtention d'un système qualité efficace passe par l'accréditation des activités du CNTS et ses unités opérationnelles, gage d'efficacité et reconnaissance de la maîtrise scientifique et technique. Dans le but de mettre en place le système de management de la qualité (SMQ) au sein du CNTS par l'instauration des tests d'assurance qualité, un consultant international sera recruté selon les termes de référence établis dans le présent document 4. postings.text: Consultant: Consultant on Regional Environmental Assessment, Monitoring and Data Analysis | UNECE - United Nations Economic Commission for Europe Skip to main content Consultant: Consultant on Regional Environmental Assessment, Monitoring and Data Analysis UNECE - United Nations Economic Commission for Europe Remote | Geneva CON level Speaks English, Russian Application deadline: November 24, 2026 (6 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The United Nations Economic Commission for Europe (UNECE) is seeking a consultant to support the Environmental Monitoring and Assessment Programme, particularly in the development of the Eighth Pan-European Environmental Assessment. The consultant will be responsible for preparing thematic chapters, conducting research and data analysis, and contributing to policy briefs and training materials. This role involves collaboration with various stakeholders and requires timely delivery of high-quality outputs. The consultancy is expected to last for one month between December 2026 and March 2027. Candidate Requirements: Advanced degree in Environmental science, geography, or related field Experience in environmental monitoring and assessment Knowledge of environmental indicators and statistics Fluency in English and Russian Result of Service Depending on the specific assignment, the consultant shall prepare and submit for example the following deliverables: · Draft and final thematic chapters of the Eighth Pan-European Environmental Assessment. · Background papers, analytical studies and thematic assessments supporting the assessment. · Indicator analyses, datasets, visualizations, maps and graphics supporting assessment findings. · Review comments and revised chapter drafts following expert and peer-review processes. · Executive summaries, key messages and policy-relevant synthesis inputs. · Draft and final training materials, including exercises, case studies and participant handouts. · Training workshop agendas, presentations, speaker recommendations and workshop reports. · Evaluation and revision of training materials following delivery of capacity-development activities. · National or regional assessments related to environmental monitoring systems, indicators, statistics or reporting. · Substantive inputs to meetings of the Working Group on Environmental Monitoring and Assessment, the Joint Working Group on Environmental Statistics and Indicators and other relevant UNECE bodies. · Policy briefs, technical notes and other knowledge products developed under programme projects. In addition, the consultant is expected to prepare a one-page summary of outputs under the contract for each task. The summary should be accompanied by copies of deliverables in emails to the respective UNECE secretariat’s staff. The outputs should be delivered in a timely manner and with good quality to fit the overall process of the implementation of the activities. The outputs will be reviewed and approved by the UNECE secretariat staff, who should regularly be consulted and updated on the progress in their achievement. Work Location Home country Expected duration The consultancy will be for the period of one month between December 2026 to March 2027 Duties and Responsibilities Organizational Setting and Reporting The United Nations Economic Commission for Europe (UNECE) Environmental Monitoring and Assessment Programme assists member States in strengthening their environmental monitoring and assessment systems and in working with environmental data and information to ensure their timely flow and adequate assessment. In this way, the programme helps enable informed decision-making processes and sound environmental policy making, both nationally and internationally, in the environmental sector in support of a transition to sustainable development. The UNECE Working Group on Environmental Monitoring and Assessment serves as the environmental knowledge and assessment network for the UNECE region, under the oversight of the Committee on Environmental Policy, to aid informed decision-making in support of the transition to sustainable development and a green and circular economy in the UNECE region and engages partners such as UNEP, other organizations and programmes within the United Nations system, institutions of the European Union, including the European Commission and the European Environment Agency and its European Environment Information and Observation Network, the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) and the Group on Earth Observations, among others. A major priority of the Environmental Monitoring and Assessment programme in the coming year is the preparation of the Eighth Pan-European Environmental Assessment, which will provide an indicator-based assessment of the state and trends of the environment across the region. The assessment is being developed in cooperation with UNEP, national experts, academia, international organizations and relevant UNECE intergovernmental bodies and will serve as a key knowledge product informing environmental policy and decision-making in the pan-European region at the Tenth Environment for Europe Ministerial Conference scheduled for 2028. In addition, the programme supports environmental monitoring and assessment projects in Europe, the Caucasus and Central Asia, including work on environmental indicators, environmental statistics, the Shared Environmental Information System (SEIS), environmental reporting, capacity development and related policy-support activities. To facilitate timely implementation of these activities, UNECE maintains a roster of qualified consultants who may be engaged for specific assignments under the Environmental Monitoring and Assessment Programme. The roster serves as a recruitment and deployment mechanism enabling rapid access to pre-vetted experts for short-term technical assignments. Selected experts may remain on the roster for up to five years subject to satisfactory performance and continuing programme needs. The present call seeks to strengthen UNECE's roster of consultants with demonstrated expertise in environmental monitoring, environmental assessments, environmental statistics and indicators, environmental reporting and related analytical work. Objectives and Targets (Specific Functions of Consultant/Individual Contractor) The overall purpose of the consultancy is to support the activities under the Environmental Monitoring and Assessment Programme in implementing various activities and projects and, in particular, the development of the Eighth Pan-European Environmental Assessment in 2027. In particular, consultants will contribute to the preparation of thematic chapters of the assessment, by assessing the state of the environment, identifying trends and emerging issues, analysing policy responses, assessing progress in recent years and synthesizing environmental information from across the pan-European region for thematic chapters including on: Atmospheric air and the ozone layer; Climate change and greenhouse gas emissions; Fresh water; Coastal waters, marine ecosystems and seas; Biodiversity and ecosystems; Land and soil; Chemicals and waste; Noise; Environment and health; Environmental financing and public spending on environmental protection; Sustainable infrastructure; Circular and green economy; Nature based solutions Artificial intelligence and the environment. The work will include data collection, analysis, drafting, peer review processes, preparation of figures and visualizations, responses to review comments and finalization of assessment outputs. Priority responsibilities related to the Eighth Pan-European Environmental Assessment: Conduct research, data collection, analysis and synthesis of information for assigned assessment chapters and thematic areas. Draft, revise and finalize thematic chapters, background papers, case studies, summaries and other assessment materials. Analyze environmental trends, drivers, pressures, impacts and policy responses at regional and sub-regional levels. Develop and interpret environmental indicators and assessment methodologies. Prepare data visualizations, maps, charts and analytical outputs supporting assessment findings. Contribute to expert consultations, peer-review processes and revision of draft chapters. Support coordination with contributing organizations, experts and reviewers. Prepare presentations, briefing notes and supporting documentation related to the pan-European assessment process. In addition, consultants may support other activities implemented under the Environmental Monitoring and Assessment Programme, including projects related to environmental monitoring systems, environmental indicators, environmental statistics, SEIS and open data principles implementation, environmental reporting, data management, capacity development and thematic assessments in UNECE member States. The consultant(s) will work under the overall supervision of the Manager of the Environmental Monitoring and Assessment Programme and in close cooperation with UNECE staff, UNEP, international partners, regional experts and national institutions. Travel may be required depending on the specific assignment. Detailed Terms of Reference and additional guidance will be provided for each specific assignment. Qualifications/special skills Advanced degree in Environmental science, geography, environmental policy or related field. Experience in some of the listed subjects is desirable: Environmental monitoring and assessment/ SEIS and open data principles/ Environmental data and information/ Production of regional/international environmental indicators/ UNECE set of environmental indicators/ EEA core set of indicators or OECD green growth indicators or and indicators for the SDGs/ knowledge related to the state of the environment in the pan-European region and trends. Languages Fluency in English and Russian is required. Additional Information Not available. No Fee THE UNITED NATIONS DOES NOT CHARGE A FEE AT ANY STAGE OF THE RECRUITMENT PROCESS (APPLICATION, INTERVIEW MEETING, PROCESSING, OR TRAINING). THE UNITED NATIONS DOES NOT CONCERN ITSELF WITH INFORMATION ON APPLICANTS’ BANK ACCOUNTS. Candidates are responsible for complying with deadlines and are encouraged to submit applications well ahead. Before applying, please make sure that you have read the requirements for the position and that you qualify. Applications from non-qualifying applicants will most likely be discarded by the recruiting manager. postings.text: ​​Multimedia and Communications Associate/Consultant ​ | IOM - International Organization for Migration Skip to main content ​​Multimedia and Communications Associate/Consultant ​ IOM - International Organization for Migration Bunia Both national and international UG - Ungraded level Speaks English, French, Spanish Application deadline: November 24, 2026 (6 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The Multimedia and Communications Associate/Consultant at IOM will support the production, editing, and dissemination of multimedia materials that showcase the organization's work in the DRC, particularly in the north-eastern region. This role involves practical and technical support in photography, videography, video editing, graphic design, and digital content production. The incumbent will collaborate with the Media and Communications team to ensure that all materials are accurate, engaging, and aligned with IOM's branding. The position requires participation in field visits and providing audiovisual support during events. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.  IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move. IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at  IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration   Project Context and Scope ​Under the overall supervision of the Chief of Mission and the direct supervision of the Senior Media and Communications Associate, the Multimedia and Communications Associate will support the production, editing and dissemination of multimedia and communications materials showcasing IOM's work across the DRC, with particular emphasis on north-eastern DRC.​ The incumbent will provide practical and technical support in photography, videography, video editing, graphic design and digital content production. Working closely with the Media and Communications (M&C) team and relevant programme colleagues, the incumbent will help ensure that communications materials are accurate, engaging, ethically produced and aligned with IOM's branding and donor visibility requirements.​     Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing   Programme Support Unit  Responsibilities Tasks to be performed under this contract ​​Multimedia Production: Support the production and editing of photographs, videos and other multimedia materials documenting IOM's activities, including interviews, human-interest stories, events and donor visibility activities. Assist with filming, photography, sound recording and post-production. ​Content Development and Storytelling: Assist in collecting human-interest stories, success stories, testimonials and other communications content from programme teams and field locations. Draft captions, short articles, social media posts and accompanying text for review and approval. ​Graphic Design and Publications: Assist in designing and formatting communications and visibility materials, including infographics, factsheets, brochures, presentations, banners, social media graphics and other digital or printed products, following IOM's branding guidelines and approved templates. ​Digital Communications: Support the preparation and formatting of content for IOM DRC's website and social media platforms, under the guidance of the Media and Communications Officer. ​Field Documentation: Participate in field visits and programme activities, when required and authorized, to take photographs, record videos, conduct basic interviews and collect audiovisual materials documenting project activities and results. ​Media and Event Support: Provide photography, videography and audiovisual support during official visits, donor missions, workshops, campaigns and other events. Assist in preparing event-related communications and visibility materials. ​Multimedia Asset Management: Assist in maintaining an organized digital archive of photographs, videos, graphics and other communications materials, including appropriate file naming, captions, metadata, consent documentation and secure storage. ​Coordination and Administrative Support: Liaise with programme colleagues and field teams to collect information, photographs and other communications materials. Provide routine logistical, administrative and technical support for communications activities, as required. ​Perform such other duties as may be assigned Performance indicators for the evaluation of results Quality, accuracy and timeliness of communication products prepared and submitted for review. Effective coordination with programme teams and field staff, and satisfactory completion of assigned communications and visibility tasks within agreed deadlines.   Qualifications Required Qualifications and Experience Education ​​High school diploma with at least four years of relevant professional experience; or​ ​Bachelor's degree in Multimedia Production, Photography, Film and Video Production, Digital Media, Visual Communications, Journalism, Communications, Graphic Design or a related field from an accredited academic institution, with at least two years of relevant professional experience.​  Experience ​​Experience in photography, videography, video editing and multimedia content production. ​Experience using digital cameras, video equipment and multimedia editing software. ​Experience producing photographs, short videos, social media graphics and other digital communications materials. ​Experience drafting captions, short articles, social media posts or other communications content. ​Experience in basic graphic design and preparing branded communications materials. ​Experience supporting communications activities for humanitarian, development, non-governmental or international organizations is an advantage. ​Familiarity with ethical storytelling, informed consent and donor visibility requirements is desirable. ​Experience working in eastern DRC or in humanitarian or emergency settings is an advantage.​  Skills Good photography and videography skills, including basic knowledge of composition, lighting, sound recording and editing.   Good working knowledge of multimedia editing and graphic design software, such as Adobe Creative Cloud, Canva, DaVinci Resolve or equivalent tools.   Ability to produce and edit photographs, short videos, graphics and other multimedia materials following established guidelines.   Good writing and editing skills, particularly for captions, short articles and social media content.   Familiarity with social media platforms and digital content formats.   Ability to organize multimedia files and maintain accurate records and digital archives.   Good organizational skills, attention to detail and ability to complete assigned tasks within established deadlines.   Good interpersonal and teamwork skills, with the ability to work effectively in multicultural environments.   Willingness and ability postings.title: UN Women: National Consultant-Programme Support Associate, Dhaka, Bangladesh UN WOMEN - United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women Dhaka Senior
postings.text: UN Women: National Consultant-Programme Support Associate, Dhaka, Bangladesh | UN WOMEN - United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women Skip to main content UN Women: National Consultant-Programme Support Associate, Dhaka, Bangladesh UN WOMEN - United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women Dhaka National Senior level Speaks English Application deadline: December 02, 2026 (14 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool UN Women is seeking a National Consultant-Programme Support Associate in Dhaka, Bangladesh, to assist the Programme Team in developing and implementing effective programs aligned with UN Women regulations. The consultant will provide administrative, logistical, and financial management support, ensuring smooth program operations. Responsibilities include preparing work plans, budgets, and proposals, as well as supporting resource mobilization and knowledge sharing. The role requires collaboration with various stakeholders to promote gender equality and women's empowerment. Candidate Requirements: Completion of secondary education Bachelor’s degree in Business or Public Administration (asset) At least 6 years of experience in administration or programme management/support Experience in financial monitoring and logistics Fluency in English and Bangla Strong financial and budgeting skills Experience with office software and web-based ERP systems Background/Context UN Women exists to advance women’s rights, gender equality and the empowerment of all women and girls. As the lead UN entity on gender equality and secretariat of the UN Commission on the Status of Women, UN Women shift laws, institutions, social behaviours and services to close the gender gap and build an equal world for all women and girls. UN Women partnerships with governments, women’s movements and the private sector coupled with its coordination of the broader United Nations translate progress into lasting changes. UN Women strides forward for women and girls in four areas: leadership, economic empowerment, freedom from violence, and women, peace and security as well as humanitarian action. UN Women keeps the rights of women and girls at the centre of global progress–always, everywhere. Because gender equality is not just what we do. It is who we are.  UN Women in Bangladesh supports the government in implementing commitments to international normative standards on gender equality and women’s human rights. In line with the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) 2022-2027, the corresponding UN Women Bangladesh Strategic Note (2022-2027) defines UN Women’s strategic engagement in Bangladesh. The country strategy focuses on strengthening the national structures and mechanisms for gender mainstreaming in policies, plans and budgets; supporting efforts to prevent and eliminate violence against women; promoting women’s access to decent and safe work; promoting policies and government investment in women’s empowerment and resilience building in the context of climate change, humanitarian crisis as well as other threats to peace and security. UN Women works with a range of stakeholders in Bangladesh, including the government, civil society and women’s organizations, youth, UN agencies and donors, to promote gender equality and women’s empowerment.  UN Women is seeking the services of a National Consultant ( Programme Associate) to  support  members of the Programme Team in the development and implementation of effective programmes consistent with UN Women rules and regulations. The consultant will contribute  to research, financial management, and programme implementation including providing necessary operational, administrative and programmatic support. S/he/they will work in close collaboration with the operations and programme staff as required for resolving complex finance-related issues and exchange of information. Description of Responsibilities/ Scope of Work Under the direct supervision of Deputy Country Representative, UN Women Bangladesh, the consultant will undertake the following tasks: Provide administrative and logistical support to the formulation and management of programmes: Provide administrative support in the preparation of programme work plans, budgets, and proposals on programme implementation arrangements;  Provide technical guidance to the programme team and executing agencies on routine delivery and reporting of programme supported activities and finances;   Prepare information for the audit of programmes/ projects and support implementation of audit recommendations;    Review programme data from programmes/ projects ;  Identify sources, and gather and compile data and information for the preparation of documents, guidelines, speeches and position papers.       2. Provide administrative support to the financial management of the Programme Unit: Prepare budget revisions, revise project awards and status; and determine unutilized funds and the operational and financial close of a project; Provide backend support as needed for PRISM and Quantum entries  Provide administrative support in monitoring budget preparation and the finances of programmes/projects; including the finalization of FACE forms;  Support processing of payment for suppliers/ consultants;   Maintain internal expenditures control system;   Create requisitions in Quantum system for development projects; register good receipts in Quantum system;  Assist in the preparation and follow up of cost-recovery bills in Quantum system.       3. Provide administrative support to the  Programme Unit: Undertake all logistical, administrative and financial arrangements for organization for meetings, workshops, events, and missions;  Make travel arrangements for the Programme Team, including travel requisitions and claims;    Prepare public information materials and briefing packets;    Assemble briefing materials and prepare PowerPoint and other presentations;        4. Provide administrative support to Resource Mobilization: Prepare cost-sharing and other agreements; follow up on contributions within the BCO resource mobilization efforts;  Organize, compile and process information from donors,  and programme team, as inputs to various databases and documents.        5. Facilitate knowledge building and knowledge sharing: Provide administrative support synthesis of lessons learnt and best practices related to programme management and finance;  Provide administrative support to the organization of training for the office staff and partners on programme and operations related issues. The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization. Deliverables The national consultant will provide a monthly time sheet  and progress report with  the following deliverables  Deliverable Target Due Dates Evidence of administrative support on programme and financial management. These can include:  Draft work plans, budgets and proposals prepared or updated; compiled data sets and review notes Audit information packs and a tracker of audit recommendations and follow-up status Updated expenditure control tracker or monthly summary  Compiled inputs for documents, guidelines, speeches and position papers Payment will be processed at the end of each month for the number of days worked based on submission of progress report on tasks completed during the month with deliverables produced. Evidence of  logistical support provided for meetings, workshops, events, trainings and missions. These can include:  Event logistics plans and checklists; venue, catering and transport arrangements Attendance lists and invitations or agendas issued Travel requisitions and claims processed for the Programme Team (offline log) Mission or event arrangement files Evidence of inputs to briefing materials, presentations, reports. These can include:  Briefing packets and PowerPoint presentations assembled or contributed to Public information materials prepared Evidence of administrative support to resource mobilization. These can include:  Draft cost-sharing and other agreements prepared Donor contribution follow-up tracker Updated donor and programme database entries or compiled donor information   Evidence of support to knowledge building and knowledge sharing. These can include:  Lessons-learnt or best-practice summary notes on programme management and finance Training invitations, agendas, participant lists and materials for staff and partners   Payment Schedule Payment will be processed at the end of each month for the number of days worked, based on the submission of a progress report on tasks completed during the month, in line with the Terms of Reference. Consultant’s Workplace:  The consultant will be office-based.  Travel and DSA:  If unforeseen travel to Dhaka or elsewhere in Bangladesh is required for this assignment, upon prior agreement/approval from UN Women, such travel expenses shall be borne by UN Women and the individual contractor/SSA shall receive a per-diem not to exceed the United Nations Daily Subsistence Allowance rate in such other location(s) and actual travel cost. Competencies    Core Values:  •    Respect for Diversity; •    Integrity ; •    Professionalism .   Core Competencies:  •    Awareness and Sensitivity Regarding Gender Issues; •    Accountability ; •    Creative Problem Solving ; •    Effective Communication;  •    Inclusive Collaboration ; •    Stakeholder Engagement;  •    Leading by Example .   Please visit this link for more information on UN Women’s Core Values and Competencies:   https://www.unwomen.org/en/about-us/employment/application-process#_Values     FUNCTIONAL COMPETENCIES:  •    Good knowledge of programme management;   •    Ability to administer and execute administrative processes and transactions;    •    Ability to create, edit and present information in clear and presentable formats;   •    Ability to manage data, documents, correspondence and reports information and workflow;    •    Strong financial and budgeting skills;   •    Strong IT skills.     Required Qualifications Education and Certification: •    Completion of secondary education is required;   •    Bachelor’s degree in Business or Public Administration is an asset.     Experience: •    At least 6  years of progressively responsible experience in administration or programme management/support;   •    Experience in financial monitoring, logistics, and partner management. •    Experience in supporting a team and coordination experience is required.  •    Experience in working in a computer environment using multiple office software packages is required;   •    Experience in supporting a team is required; •    Experience in the use of a modern web-based ERP System, preferably Oracle Cloud, is desirable; •    Prior experience with the United Nations or other international agencies is desirable.    Languages: •    Fluency in English and Bangla is required.   Evaluation:  Technical Qualification Evaluation Criteria: The total number of points allocated for the technical qualification component is 100. The role involves planning routes, conducting vehicle inspections, maintaining accurate logs, and ensuring compliance with safety regulations. The Driver will also assist with logistical support for meetings and field activities while upholding FAO's values and standards of conduct. Candidates must have a valid driver's license, relevant experience, and a working knowledge of English. Organizational Setting FAO is a specialized agency of the UN that leads international efforts to defeat hunger. FAO's goal is to achieve food security for all and ensure that people have regular access to enough high-quality food to lead active, healthy lives. With 195 Members (194 Nations and the European Union), FAO works in over 130 countries worldwide. FAO Country Offices, working under overall corporate guidance and in line with the Strategic Framework, offer policy advice and support to countries in the mandated areas of FAO, facilitated through partnerships, resources and an active country programme to provide technical assistance, develop capacities and deliver core services while fully observing international standards of accountability to establish leadership and strengthen impact at the country level. The offices deliver on the programmatic priorities of each country as agreed in their respective Country Programming Frameworks (CPFs) aligned to the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) and ensure effective and efficient operations with adequate human and financial resources. Specifically, FAO Country Offices: • advocate, inform and support policies and investments in the areas of FAO's mandate. (ii) provide technical assistance and deliver core services. (iii) assist and catalyse partnership and resource mobilization activities to support agrifood systems transformation. (iv) position FAO as the specialized/authoritative technical agency in food and agriculture and agrifood systems transformation; and (v) ensure risk-smart and accountable operations and management. Reporting Lines The incumbent will work under the overall supervision of the FAO Representative (FAOR) in Malawi, and the direct supervision of the Assistant FAO Representative (Administration), in close coordination with Administration, Travel, Security and programme teams. Technical Focus The Driver will be responsible for providing safe, reliable and timely driving services for authorized personnel and official visitors, while ensuring proper care, documentation and efficient use of assigned vehicles. Tasks and responsibilities • Drive FAO personnel, official visitors and authorized passengers on approved official travel, using safe, courteous and defensive driving practices. • Plan routes in advance, monitor road and weather conditions, and comply with movement clearances, security advisories and journey-management requirements. • Meet and assist authorized personnel and visitors at airports or other arrival points, including support with official local formalities and hotel transfers when requested. • Conduct and document daily pre-trip and post-trip inspections, including tyres, brakes, lights, oil, coolant, battery, tools, first-aid kit, fire extinguisher and other safety equipment. • Maintain complete and accurate vehicle logbooks and records of mileage, fuel consumption, trips, servicing, repairs, incidents and vehicle-related expenditure; submit records within established deadlines. • Keep assigned vehicles clean, roadworthy, secure and properly equipped; report defects immediately and arrange authorized servicing or repairs through established procedures. • Monitor scheduled maintenance, insurance, roadworthiness, registration and other required vehicle documentation, escalating upcoming expiries or gaps promptly. • Obtain repair or service quotations when authorized, support vehicle inspections, and verify that completed work corresponds to approved requirements before vehicle release. • In the event of an accident, breakdown, security incident or traffic violation, protect passengers, contact emergency and supervisory focal points, and complete all required FAO, UN security, insurance and national reporting procedures without delay. Do not admit liability on behalf of FAO. • Transport and safeguard official mail, documents, equipment and other authorized items, maintaining confidentiality, proof of delivery and chain-of-custody records where required. • Provide basic logistical and clerical support for meetings, workshops and field activities, including loading and unloading authorized supplies, photocopying and records support, without compromising driving and safety duties. • Maintain professional conduct, punctuality, discretion and respect when interacting with FAO personnel, government officials, UN partners, service providers and communities. • Use FAO vehicles only for authorized purposes and comply with FAO rules on passengers, seat belts, speed, mobile-phone use, alcohol and drugs, smoking, fuel cards, parking and custody of keys. • Support environmental sustainability through fuel-efficient driving, route optimization, avoidance of unnecessary idling and timely reporting of excessive fuel consumption or emissions. • Perform other duties as required. Selection criteria • Experience working with government institutions, development partners, national organizations and community-based organizations. • Flawless and safe driving record. Desirable experience with International Organizations and Government entities • Recognized defensive-driving training • Basic vehicle-mechanics knowledge; • First-aid training; • Possession of any other UN official language including knowledge of the local language of the duty station is an advantage. postings.text: Statistician | FAO - Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations Skip to main content Statistician FAO - Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations Rome International Consultant - Contractors Agreement level Speaks English Application deadline: December 01, 2026 (13 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool FAO is seeking candidates for a roster of consultants and Personal Service Agreements (PSAs) for the Data Quality Unit and the Data and Statistics Coordination Team. The roles involve ensuring high-quality data and statistics related to food and agriculture, supporting governance and coordination of FAO's data activities, and contributing to statistical standards and quality assurance. Candidates will work under the supervision of the Director of ESS and collaborate closely with team members. This position is based at FAO headquarters in Rome, Italy. Candidate Requirements: Advanced university degree in statistics, mathematics, economics, data science or related fields At least 1 year of relevant experience in statistics or data analysis Working knowledge of English Experience in statistical governance and quality assurance Experience in data collection, processing, and analysis Proficiency in R or Python Experience with Shiny and Git Knowledge of a second FAO language is an asset CALL FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST - VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT : IMPORTANT NOTICE: Please note that Closure Date and Time displayed above are based on date and time settings of your personal device FAO is committed to achieving workforce diversity in terms of gender, nationality, background and culture. Qualified female applicants, qualified nationals of non-and under-represented Members and person with disabilities are encouraged to apply; Everyone who works for FAO is required to adhere to the highest standards of integrity and professional conduct, and to uphold FAO's values FAO, as a Specialized Agency of the United Nations, has a zero-tolerance policy for conduct that is incompatible with its status, objectives and mandate, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination All selected candidates will undergo rigorous reference and background checks All applications will be treated with the strictest confidentiality FAO’s commitment to environmental sustainability is integral to our strategic objectives and operations. Organizational Setting The Statistics Division (ESS) develops and advocates for the implementation of methodologies and standards for data collection, validation, processing and analysis, in the food and agriculture statistics domains. In these statistical domains, it also plays a key role in the compilation, processing and dissemination of internationally comparable data, and provides essential capacity building in support of Member Nations. The Division also disseminates publications, working papers and statistical yearbooks, that cover agriculture and food security statistics, including prices, investments, production, trade and agri-environmental statistical data. Finally, as the ESS Director also plays the role of FAO Chief Statistician, the Division supports the various functions of the Chief Statistician, that is to ensure stronger governance of FAO's data and statistical system, foster consistency of FAO's Data and Statistical programme within the Strategic Framework, ensure statistical excellence through the implementation of statistical standards and quality assurance mechanisms, and position FAO's presence in data and statistical discussions at global level. The aim of this Call for Expression of Interest is to populate a roster of consultants and subscribers of Personal Service Agreements (PSAs) for the Data Quality Unit and the Data and Statistics and Coordination Team of ESS at FAO headquarters in Rome, Italy. The Data Quality Unit aims to ensure that the Organization produces and disseminates high-quality data and statistics related to its mandate. The unit develops, updates and implements corporate quality frameworks, policies, standards, procedures and tools to ensure that statistical processes are sound and disseminated data and statistics are of the highest possible quality. It also monitors and assesses the quality of FAO data and statistics and supports FAO technical units in improving their compliance to internal quality policies, standards and procedures. Finally, it provides quality assurance support and tools to FAO technical units and member countries to improve the quality of food and agriculture data and statistics produced at the national level. The Data and Statistics Coordination Team supports the governance and coordination of FAO’s data and statistical activities, both within FAO and within the broader international data and statistical community. It oversees the planning, monitoring and reporting on FAO data and statistical programme of work and more generally supports the monitoring of FAO’s corporate results. It coordinates FAO’s role as custodian agency for 22 Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) Indicators. Finally, it acts as focal point for any queries on intellectual property matters concerning FAO databases. Reporting Lines Candidates selected for assignments with the Data Quality Unit (DQU) will work under the general supervision of the Director of ESS and the direct supervision of the DQU Team Leader, and in close collaboration with other members of the Unit. Candidates selected for assignments with the Data and Statistics Coordination (DSCT) Team will work under the general supervision of the Director of ESS, and the direct supervision of the DSC Team Leader, and in close collaboration with other members of the Unit. Technical Focus Candidates selected for assignments with the Data Quality Unit will contribute to the quality assurance efforts of the Division, such as the development and review of statistical standards; the implementation of peer reviews, quality assessments and user consultations; and the provision of support and capacity development activities on statistical and data-quality related matters. Candidates selected for assignments with the Data and Statistics Coordination Team will provide data analysis and programming support to the governance, coordination, planning, monitoring and reporting of data and statistical activities at corporate level, in particular in the area of SDG monitoring, and to the design and monitoring of FAO results framework. Tasks and responsibilities Candidates selected for assignments with the Data Quality Unit will: • Support efforts to ensure the quality of statistical outputs produced and disseminated by FAO, statistics produced using non-traditional data sources, such as Earth observation and other big data sources. • Contribute to the implementation of FAO's Quality Assessment and Planning Survey (QAPS), statistical and data production. • Perform other related duties supporting DQU’s areas of work as requested. The role involves implementing monitoring, evaluation, and accountability frameworks, promoting transparency, and supporting evidence-based decision-making. The officer will engage with humanitarian partners, facilitate knowledge sharing, and contribute to the planning of monitoring missions. This position aims to ensure a results-oriented and collaborative approach to humanitarian response efforts. Candidate Requirements: Advanced university degree in relevant field or Bachelor's with additional experience Minimum 2 years of relevant experience (4 years with Bachelor's) Excellent interpersonal communication skills Proven experience in report writing Experience with office software and web-based management systems Fluency in English and the national language of the duty station Background and organization context The position is located in the Crisis Response Division (CRD), Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA). OCHA is the part of the United Nations Secretariat responsible for bringing together humanitarian actors to ensure a coherent response to emergencies. OCHA also ensures there is a framework within which each actor can contribute to the overall response efforts. OCHA's mission is to mobilize and coordinate effective and principled humanitarian action in partnership with national and international actors in order to alleviate human suffering in disasters and emergencies; advocate for the rights of people in need; promote preparedness and prevention; and facilitate sustainable solutions. This multiple-duty-station temporary job opening is being advertised for the position of Monitoring and Reporting Officer and is located across a number of OCHA Humanitarian Financing Units (in Uganda, kenya and Mozambique). Under the overall supervision of the Head of Office, the incumbent reports to the Head of Humanitarian Financing Unit/Fund Manager. The Humanitarian Fund Units in OCHA Regional and Country Offices manage multi-donor country-based pooled funds under the leadership of the Humanitarian Coordinator/Resident Coordinator. These funds receive unearmarked contributions from donors. The funds are allocated to humanitarian actors for ongoing humanitarian operations and to respond to new emergencies. Position Purpose Under the supervision of the regional humanitarian pooled fund manager, the Monitoring and Reporting Officer will play a central role in strengthening accountability, effectiveness, and learning within the Humanitarian Funding Unit (HFU). The position is responsible for leading the implementation of monitoring, evaluation, and accountability frameworks that ensure compliance with established standards, promote transparency, and deliver measurable impact among partners and stakeholders. The Monitoring and Reporting Officer will support evidence-based decision-making by developing and piloting innovative monitoring approaches, documenting best practices, and generating insights on the operationalization of localization strategies. Through active engagement with coordination forums and close collaboration with humanitarian partners, including local and national NGOs, the role facilitates inclusive participation, capacity strengthening, and knowledge sharing across the humanitarian system. The position will also contribute to the planning and execution of monitoring missions, provide technical guidance to partners, and ensure systematic documentation and dissemination of results, lessons learned, and success stories. By maintaining strong coordination with field offices and stakeholders, the M&E Officer enhances program quality, promotes risk-sharing initiatives, and supports continuous improvement in fund management and delivery. Overall, the role aims to ensure that the HFU operates in a results-oriented, accountable, and collaborative manner, while advancing localization and strengthening the effectiveness of humanitarian response efforts. Actively contribute to discussions, influence decision-making processes, and ensure that HFU priorities and perspectives are effectively integrated into inter-agency coordination efforts. • Identify, conceptualize, and pilot innovative and context-appropriate monitoring models and approaches aimed at strengthening oversight, improving data quality, and enhancing the overall effectiveness and efficiency of Country Fund interventions. • Work in close collaboration with Resident Coordinator’s Office (RCO) area offices, UNHCR, and implementing partners to strategically plan and execute monitoring missions. Provide hands-on technical assistance during these missions to ensure compliance, strengthen partner capacity, and enhance programme delivery on the ground. • Maintain continuous and proactive engagement with the broader humanitarian community by participating in joint field missions alongside HFU and OCHA field staff, fostering collaboration, information sharing, and coordinated responses to emerging humanitarian needs. 2.) Design, coordinate, and facilitate webinars and other knowledge-sharing platforms aimed at strengthening the technical and operational capacities of partners, while promoting the exchange of experiences, expertise, and innovative practices across the humanitarian ecosystem. Ensure that these insights are effectively documented and disseminated to inform strategic decision-making and continuous improvement within the HFU. Generate, synthesize, and disseminate evidence on the operationalization of the Uganda Humanitarian Fund’s localization approach by documenting both successful implementation models and key challenges or bottlenecks encountered in practice.  Develop high-quality analytical products, including case studies, success stories, and practical examples, to effectively communicate lessons learned and showcase impact to the Fund’s Advisory Board and other strategic stakeholders. postings.text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES - FIRMS SELECTION)   COUNTRY: Republic of Mozambique NAME OF PROJECT: Transport Corridors for Economic Resilience (TRACER SOP2) Grant No.: IDA-E4810 Assignment Title : Consultancy Services for Climate Risk and Vulnerability Assessment and Feasibility Study for Resilience Interventions and Monitoring of Construction Improvements on the Nacala Corridor   Reference No . (as per Procurement Plan): 45A000141/CP/06/2026 The Government of Mozambique (GOM) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Transport Corridors for Economic Resilience (TRACER SOP2) and intends to apply part of the proceeds towards the payment for consulting services. The consulting services (the “Services”) shall comprise the climate risk vulnerability assessment, the feasibility study for resilience interventions, and the monitoring of the civil works for rehabilitation, in accordance with the duties and responsibilities of the “Engineer” as defined under the applicable FIDIC Conditions of Contract. The Consultant shall also take all necessary measures and provide appropriate technical advice to the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) to ensure that the studies and construction contracts are completed in a timely and cost-effective manner, in full compliance with the applicable contract conditions and technical specifications. The Consultant shall undertake the required studies and monitor the construction improvements, including reviewing the designs prepared by the Contractor and submitting recommendations to the Client for approval. The Consultant shall develop, implement, and document a structured theoretical and on-the-job training program for two (2) graduate engineers selected by the PIU and assigned to the Project. During the Defects Liability Period (DLP), the Consultant shall, on behalf of the Client and in accordance with the applicable Conditions of Contract, monitor the performance of the completed works, carry out periodic and final inspections, identify and document any defects or deficiencies, and instruct the Contractor, as applicable under the Contract, to carry out the necessary corrective and remedial measures. For the provision of these services, the Consultant shall deploy suitably qualified personnel to undertake the required studies, monitor the construction improvements, and carry out the final inspection through a dedicated team. The Consultant shall also prepare and issue the Final Certificate in accordance with the applicable Conditions of Contract. The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) for the assignment can be obtained from the address provided below. The Ministry of Transport and Logistics (MTL) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are: Company profile and core business activities, demonstrating at least 15 years of experience in providing civil engineering consulting service; General experience of the firm (must be at least 15 years) in the field of design and construction supervision of roads and bridge contracts; Description of at least five (5) similar assignments demonstrating experience in Climate Risk and Vulnerability Assessment & Feasibility Study for Resilience Interventions and Monitoring of Construction Improvements or Rehabilitation contracts; Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage. The shortlist will contain Five (5) to Eight (8) shortlisted firms. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Seventh Edition, September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. postings.text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)   REPUBLIC OF ARMENIA WATER AND IRRIGATION SERVICES ENHANCEMENT (WISE) PROGRAM – PHASE 1 PROJECT Loan No.: 9831-AM   Assignment Title: Feasibility Study, Preparation of Preliminary and Detailed Designs, Bidding Documents, Technical Supervision for Irrigation Systems Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): AM-WC-CS-03/1   The Republic of Armenia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Water and Irrigation Services Enhancement (WISE) Program – Phase 1 Project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The consulting services (“the Services”) include feasibility studies, environmental and social assessments, investment assessment and ranking, and preliminary designs for five irrigation systems: Kotayk, Lori, Arzni-Shamiram, Lower Hrazdan (including the Ranchpar Two-Stage Pumping Stations and pressure pipelines), and Debetavan. Kotayk and Lori shall be prioritized outside the ranking process. The Services also include detailed designs, technical specifications, bills of quantities, cost estimates and bidding documents for irrigation systems selected for implementation under WISE Phase 1, as well as technical support during procurement of construction works; a separate detailed feasibility study for the Mkhchyan Two-Stage Pumping Stations and associated pressure pipelines; technical supervision and quality assurance of construction works; and training of operation and maintenance personnel. The work encompasses necessary surveys and investigations, evaluation of technical alternatives, and the integration of environmental, social, health and safety, and climate resilience requirements.   The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this request for expressions of interest. The Water Committee, under the Ministry of Territorial Administration and Infrastructure of the Republic of Armenia, now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are: (1) At least 10 years of overall experience in consulting services related to the construction or modernization of water systems, such as pressurized irrigation networks, pumping stations, reservoirs, canals, pipelines or other hydraulic structures, with experience covering all of the following activities: planning and feasibility assessment, design, and construction supervision; (2) Successful completion, during the last 10 years, of at least two contracts involving projects of comparable scale and complexity for each of the following activities: feasibility studies, detailed design and construction supervision, in the field of water infrastructure described in point (1). The same contract may cover more than one of these activities; (3) Experience in the preparation of bidding documents and technical specifications for civil works contracts related to the construction or modernization of water infrastructure described in point (1); (4) At least one of the contracts submitted to demonstrate compliance with the requirements under point (2) shall have been carried out under a project financed by an International Financial Institution (IFI), such as the World Bank, AFD, EBRD, ADB or similar organizations ; (5) Experience in the preparation of environmental and social studies and management plans for water infrastructure projects.   For the purposes of shortlisting, similarity of assignments will be assessed based on the nature, scale and technical complexity of the water infrastructure concerned and the scope of consulting services performed. Consultants should provide relevant quantitative information for each referenced assignment, such as irrigation command area, canal or pipeline length, pumping or storage capacity, and estimated value of construction works, as applicable. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. The qualifications and experience of sub-consultants shall not be considered for the purpose of shortlisting. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations. Interested Consultants are requested to submit a brief company profile and information on relevant assignments demonstrating their qualifications and experience against the shortlisting criteria specified above. For each referenced assignment, Consultants shall provide the project name, client, country, implementation period, brief description of services performed, the Consultant’s role, and relevant information on the scale and complexity of the project. In the case of an association, the respective roles of the participating firms shall be clearly indicated.
