postings.text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – SELECTION OF CONSULTING FIRMS)     Country: Republic of Uzbekistan   Implementing Agency: National Agency for Social Protection (NASP) under the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan.   Project Name: “Innovative Social Protection System for Inclusion of Vulnerable Populations” (INSON, P504420)   Financing Agreement (IDA Credit No. 7555-UZ) / Grant Agreement No. TF C4589-UZ   Assignment Title: “Expertise in Prosthetic Devices and Rehabilitation Equipment”.   Package Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): UZ-INSON-CS-CQS-2.1.11.   The Republic of Uzbekistan has received financing from the World Bank for the implementation of the project “Innovative Social Protection System for Inclusion of Vulnerable Populations” (INSON) and intends to apply part of the proceeds towards payment for consulting services under this assignment.   The consulting services (the “Services”) include: analysis and revision of the Assistive Products List (APL), including classification and criteria for product selection and prioritization; development of draft and final technical requirements and specifications for priority prosthetic and orthotic devices and rehabilitation equipment, including equipment planned for procurement for rehabilitation centres; development of a short-term rental and reuse model for assistive products, including assessment of service-delivery models, financial and institutional arrangements, operational procedures, model contracts, inventory management and monitoring tools; preparation of documents and recommendations for subsequent implementation of the rental scheme, including a pilot-ready implementation package. The assignment also includes stakeholder consultations, training of 14 regional trainers (30 hours of in-person training), followed by training of 208 district-level specialists (20 hours online in two groups using a cascade model). The Terms of Reference provide for limited operational testing of the proposed pilot approach, where feasible within the assignment timeframe.   The overall duration of the assignment is seven (7) months. The international key experts shall spend a cumulative minimum of 40 person-days in Uzbekistan, including field visits to at least two regions.   The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) are available at the following link: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1RJ5N9KGvqRp_M5HlMzSaoXShuIk7jk8d/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=104755491226149341341&rtpof=true&sd=true   The National Agency for Social Protection (NASP) under the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan invites qualified consulting firms (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the Services. Interested firms shall provide information on their institutional experience and similar completed assignments, indicating the client, country, contract value, start and completion dates, scope of services performed, and the firm’s role, as well as information demonstrating their capacity to perform the assignment. In the case of a joint venture (JV), it shall be specified which JV member performed each similar assignment cited. The criteria for the firm’s qualifications and relevant experience are as follows:   At least five (5) years of institutional experience in prosthetic and orthotic devices, rehabilitation equipment, assistive technology or rehabilitation service delivery. At least two (2) assignments completed within the last ten (10) years in the above fields, carried out at national level or for an international client. At least one (1) assignment completed within the last ten (10) years involving the development, revision or technical assessment of an assistive products list (APL), product selection and prioritization, or technical/quality assessment of assistive products. At least one (1) assignment completed within the last ten (10) years involving rental, reuse, loan-pool arrangements, refurbishment or maintenance of assistive products, or comparable equipment service-delivery arrangements. At least one (1) completed assignment involving the design and delivery of a structured training/capacity-building programme in two or more locations. Ability to mobilize a qualified team with expertise in prosthetics and orthotics, rehabilitation, assistive technology, APL development, financing and training, with capacity to work in Uzbek and Russian. Experience in Central Asia, the CIS or comparable middle-income health systems is an asset. Experience performing assignments for UN agencies, international financial institutions or national ministries of health or social protection is an asset.   At the expressions of interest stage, the qualifications and relevant experience of the firm will be evaluated. Key experts and their curricula vitae (CVs) will not be evaluated at this stage; the relevant information will be requested from the selected firm together with its technical proposal.   Interested Consultants are referred to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (September 2023) (the “Procurement Regulations”) concerning conflict of interest. The Consultant (including joint venture members and subconsultants) and its affiliates shall not subsequently participate in procurements of goods, works and non-consulting services arising from or directly related to this assignment, including procurements of assistive products and rehabilitation equipment for which specifications are developed under this assignment, as well as services for the organization and operation of rental points (see Section V of the ToR).   Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but must clearly indicate whether the association is in the form of a joint venture (JV) and/or subconsultancy. In the case of a joint venture, its members shall be jointly and severally liable under the Contract.   The consulting firm will be selected using the Consultant’s Qualifications-based Selection (CQS) method in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations.   Further information may be obtained at the address below during working hours from 10:00 to 18:00 (Tashkent time).   Expressions of interest must be submitted in writing to the address below (in person, by post or by e-mail) no later than 4 December, 2026.   INSON Project Implementation Unit Attention: Mr. Mirodil Khusanov – Project Coordinator. 3 Amir Temur Street, Tashkent, Republic of Uzbekistan Tel.: +998 71 239 59 76 E-mail: piuinsonprocurement@gmail.com; cc: m.xusanov@ihma.uz; s.maxmudov@ihma.uz

Responsibilities include project management, coordination of meetings, technical assistance tracking, and resource mobilization. The role requires collaboration with various stakeholders and effective communication to ensure successful project outcomes. Purpose of the recruitment The purpose of this consultancy is to support the effective and efficient planning, development, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of the TVD Programme in the WHO African Region, in accordance with the regional Framework for the integrated control, elimination and eradication of tropical and vector borne diseases endorsed by member states at the 72nd Regional committee in 2022, and relevant WHO strategic and operational plans. The incumbent will support the Team Leader and other technical officers in project management and communication activities. Background The WHO AFRO “Framework for the control elimination and eradication of tropical and vector-borne diseases in the African Region,” endorsed by Member States in August 2022, provides a viable pathway towards member states attaining the stated goals. Three objectives to be achieved by implementing the framework approach include: (i) Support the strengthening of health systems needed by Member States to deliver integrated services for tropical and vector-borne disease; (ii) Support the scaling up of implementation of targeted, integrated tropical and vector-borne disease interventions; (iii) Strengthen the prevention and control of tropical and vector-borne disease outbreaks in epidemic-prone Member States. The Tropical and Vector-borne Disease (TVD) programme of Health Promotion, Disease Prevention and Control (DPC) Cluster/WHO AFFRO provides leadership and vision to the above and related areas of work in the WHO African Region and facilitates planning, programming, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of services in an integrated approach. The team is responsible for joint actions with other teams of the DPC Cluster and other related Clusters to respond to the needs of the population through the integrated delivery of interventions and services. The TVD team manages multiple projects and programmes supporting disease control and elimination across the 47 Member States of the WHO African Region. The growing scope and diversity of the programme portfolio, combined with the need to respond effectively to country-specific technical support requirements, place significant demands on the staff for grant management, programme oversight and performance monitoring. Consequently, The TVD programme has prioritized the position of a Project Assistant and Communication officer, to improve the efficiency and impact of investments in malaria, NTDs and other vector-borne diseases made through the WHO African regional office. The recruitment of a Project Assistant and Communication officer will strengthen the management capacity of the TVD Unit and provide dedicated support to the Team Lead and technical officers in overseeing grants and ensuring effective implementation and performance of the Unit’s programmes. The position will contribute to strengthening grant planning and management, monitoring financial and programmatic performance, identifying implementation challenges and corrective actions, and ensuring timely reporting and accountability to donors. Scope of Work The consultant will be expected to perform the following duties: Project management Support coordination of projects within the TVD programme and work with the appropriate staff to ensure that the project deliverables are on time, within budget and at the required level of quality;  Work with appropriate staff to determine the activities and resources (time, money, equipment, etc) required to complete the project (project workplans) and develop a schedule for the completion of each project; Monitor the progress of each project and recommend adjustments to TVD Team Leader as necessary to ensure the successful completion of the projects. Utilize IT systems to keep track of people, project milestones and progress; Using IT systems, develop forms and records to document and track project activities: Set up files to ensure that all project information is appropriately documented and secured. Planning and administration: Support preparations for regional coordination mechanism meetings which include: the Regional Advisory Group meetings and other critical meetings as assigned by TVD Team Leader;  With technical team, support coordination of the disease programme reviews and the development/revision of malaria strategic plans and NTD master plans in the WHO African region; Support communications with stakeholders (funding and medicine donors, implementing partners) through the appropriate WHO channels and signatories; Ensure that all project personnel receive an appropriate orientation on the TVD Programme and its partners, DPC cluster, AFRO and WHO. Technical assistance tracking Facilitate the set-up, management and maintenance of roster of experts on malaria, case management NTDs and other vector borne diseases in close collaboration with subject matter experts; Facilitate the orgnanisation of pre-deployment briefings, briefing and deployment of experts in the field; Support the development of metrics for assessing and monitoring TVD sub-contractors and their deliverables to ensure guidelines are maintained, timelines adhered to and WHO quality standards are met. postings.text: Driver (Specialized in Heavy Duty Vehicles - Armoured Vehicles - AVs) | FAO - Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations Skip to main content Driver (Specialized in Heavy Duty Vehicles - Armoured Vehicles - AVs) FAO - Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations Syria International Consultant - Contractors Agreement level Speaks Arabic, English Application deadline: December 01, 2026 (13 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) is seeking a Driver specialized in Heavy Duty Vehicles, particularly Armoured Vehicles (AVs), to provide reliable and safe transportation services in Syria. The role involves transporting FAO personnel, maintaining vehicle safety, and ensuring compliance with driving regulations. Candidates must have a valid driver's license, a minimum of three years of relevant experience, and proficiency in English and Arabic. This position is crucial for supporting FAO's mission to enhance agrifood systems and ensure effective operations in the region. Candidate Requirements: Completion of Intermediate and/or Secondary education Valid Driver’s License – D2 Minimum 3 years’ experience in a similar position Flawless safe driving record Experience in Humanitarian agencies and/or driving AVs is an advantage Working knowledge of English and Arabic Syrian Nationality IMPORTANT NOTICE: Please note that Closure Date and Time displayed above are based on date and time settings of your personal device FAO is committed to achieving workforce diversity in terms of gender, nationality, background and culture Qualified female applicants, qualified nationals of non-and under-represented Members and person with disabilities are encouraged to apply Everyone who works for FAO is required to adhere to the highest standards of integrity and professional conduct, and to uphold FAO's values FAO, as a Specialized Agency of the United Nations, has a zero-tolerance policy for conduct that is incompatible with its status, objectives and mandate, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination All selected candidates will undergo rigorous reference and background checks All applications will be treated with the strictest confidentiality FAO’s commitment to environmental sustainability is integral to our strategic objectives and operations. Organizational Setting The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) contributes to the achievement of the 2030 Agenda through the FAO Strategic Framework by supporting the transformation to MORE efficient, inclusive, resilient and sustainable agrifood systems, for better production, better nutrition, a better environment and a better life, leaving no one behind. FAO is a specialized agency of the UN that leads international efforts to defeat hunger. FAO's goal is to achieve food security for all and ensure that people have regular access to enough high-quality food to lead active, healthy lives. With 195 Members (194 countries and the European Union), FAO works in over 130 countries worldwide. FAO Country Offices, working under overall corporate guidance and in line with the Strategic Framework, offer policy advice and support to countries in the mandated areas of FAO, facilitated through partnerships, resources and an active country programme to provide technical assistance, develop capacities and deliver core services while fully observing international standards of accountability to establish leadership and strengthen impact at the country level. The offices deliver on the programmatic priorities of each country as agreed in their respective Country Programming Frameworks (CPFs) aligned to the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) and ensure effective and efficient operations with adequate human and financial resources. Specifically, FAO Country Offices: (i) advocate, inform and support policies and investments in the areas of FAO’s mandate; (ii) provide technical assistance and deliver core services; (iii) assist and catalyse partnership and resource mobilization activities to support agrifood systems transformation; (iv) position FAO as the specialized/authoritative technical agency in food and agriculture and agrifood systems transformation; and (v) ensure risk-smart and accountable operations and management. The position is located in the FAO Country Office in Syria. Reporting Lines Under the general supervision of the FAO Representative in Syria, the overall supervision of the Assistant FAOR Administrative and the direct supervision of Logistics and Fleet specialist in close cooperation with all other FAO staff/colleagues, the incumbent will perform following duties and responsibilities. Technical Focus Provide reliable and safe driving services by driving office staff and visitors, delivering and collecting mail, documents and other items. Tasks and responsibilities - Transport the assigned FAO personnel, designated in Aleppo to several identified locations, districts, and outskirts inside and rural the governorate as official trips/errands. - Travel on official (Convoy - Shuttle) missions from Aleppo to different Syrian governorates and vice versa; - Take part in UN convoys (joint missions) when required; - Maintain an up-to-date Log form/sheet of all conducted trips. The form should be filled with accurate and genuine information such as; dates, times, odometers, and destinations; - Keep a precise record of mileage and fuel consumption in addition to transportation related expenditures, vehicle service and repairs; - Ensure day-to-day preventative check of the assigned AV; checking oil, water, battery, tires, etc; Perform minor repairs (when needed) and timely report for any other necessary repairs in order to keep the vehicle safe and technically sound at all times; maintain the vehicle in clean condition; - Prematurely report the needed regular maintenance of the vehicle to the line supervisor; Immediately report any sudden technical issue, problem, or accident that may happen to the line supervisor; - When involved in an accident, ensure that all organizational/UN and local/country rules, regulations and procedures are followed correctly and properly; - Follow the rules of safe driving and comply with the safety/security standards defined by the UN system in Syria to ensure the safety of both vehicle and passengers in sensitive areas where FAO programmes are implemented; - Collect and deliver mails, documents, pouches, and other items belong to the organization from FAO sub-offce to the concerned governmental agencies, institutions, airport, project sites, etc. as requested. - When needed, assist FAO personnel in performing simple clerical duties; - Perform other related duties as required. CANDIDATES WILL BE ASSESSED AGAINST THE FOLLOWING Minimum Requirements • Completion of Intermediate and/or Secondary education. Possession of a valid Driver’s License – D2. • Minimum 3 years’ experience working in a similar position with a flawless safe driving record. Experience in Humanitarian agencies and/or driving AVs will be an added advantage. • Working knowledge of English and Arabic (Good Command of English Language is an advantage) • Syrian Nationality. FAO Core Competencies • Results Focus • Teamwork • Communication • Building Effective Relationships • Knowledge Sharing and Continuous Improvement Technical/Functional Skills • Knowledge of the local driving rules and regulations • Basic skills in minor vehicle repair • Safe and careful driving manner, familiarity of routes, good sense of directions • Ability to cope with extended working hours Willingness to travel occasionally to remoter locations outside of duty station ADDITIONAL INFORMATION FAO does not charge a fee at any stage of the recruitment process (application, interview meeting, processing) Applications received after the closing date will not be accepted Please note that FAO only considers higher educational qualifications obtained from an institution accredited/recognized in the World Higher Education Database (WHED), a list updated by the International Association of Universities (IAU) / United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO). The list can be accessed at http://www.whed.net/ For additional employment opportunities visit the FAO employment website: http://www.fao.org/employment/home/en/ Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, accreditation, any residency or visa requirements, and security clearances. FAO seeks gender, geographical and linguistic diversity in its staff and international consultants in order to best serve FAO Members in all regions. HOW TO APPLY • To apply, visit the recruitment website at Jobs at FAO and complete your online profile. We strongly recommend that your profile is accurate, complete and includes your employment records, academic qualifications, and language skills • Candidates are requested to attach a letter of motivation to the online profile • Once your profile is completed, please apply, and submit your application • Please note that FAO only considers higher educational qualifications obtained from an institution accredited/recognized in the World Higher Education Database (WHED), a list updated by the International Association of Universities (IAU) / United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO). postings.text: Government of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh Department of Environment Host and Rohingya Enhancement of Lives Project (HELP) DoE Component-“Comprehensive Environmental Impact and Damage Assessment of Rohingya Influx in Cox’s Bazar and Bhasanchar of Chattogram Division 1st Floor, Room: 202, Poribesh Bhaban New Building E/16 Agargaon, Sher-E-Bangla Nagar, Dhaka-1207 www.doe.gov.bd   Memo No.: 22.02.0000.020.76.019 . 26.154                                                            Date:  11/11/2026    Request for Expressions of Interest (Consulting Services – Firm Selection)   Country: Bangladesh Name of the Proposed Project: Host and Rohingya Enhancement of Lives Project (HELP) Grant No .: E325-BD Assignment Title: Development of Turtle Hatchery for conservation Reference No .: S-12 Project ID No : P501274 The People's Republic of Bangladesh has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Host and Rohingya Enhancement of Lives Project (HELP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for Development of Turtle Hatchery for conservation for the ultimate objective of this assignment is to facilitate hatchling production for conservation of sea turtles in Sonapara, Cox’s Bazar. The broad scope of consulting services (“the Services”) includes but not limited to: Inception Situational Report Mid-Term Progress Report Comprehensive Conservation Strategy Report The final report consolidating all Deliverables   Objectives The ultimate objective of this assignment is to facilitate hatchling production for conservation of sea turtles in Sonapara, Cox’s Bazar. The specific objectives are to: (1) understand sea turtle nesting sites’ current situation, threats, and necessary conservation actions in Sonapara; (2) establish and operationalize turtle hatchery; and (3) conduct awareness raising activities.   Scope of Work Conduct an assessment and year-round monitoring of sea turtle nesting at Sonapara Beach The Consultant will identify and map sea turtle nesting sites and conduct focus group discussions (FGDs) with fishers to identify threats (including bycatch, predation, human disturbance, and habitat degradation). The Consultant will monitor nesting throughout the year to capture seasonal patterns and inform conservation actions. Develop a situational report which will cover: (i) identification and characterization of critical nesting habitats; (ii) migration and population studies using appropriate, ethical methods; (iii) development of an inventory of nesting events and hatching success; (iv) documentation of mortality, nesting frequency, and nest fate; and (v) identification and quantification of sources and levels of threats (including bycatch). The Consultant will prepare a comprehensive conservation strategy report summarizing findings and proposing a Conservation Management Plan (CMP) with actionable, long-term strategies, responsibilities, and a time-bound implementation schedule. The report also summarizes the results of all the activities conducted under this assignment.   Establish and manage turtle hatchery The Consultant will establish a turtle hatchery and guard shed with appropriate equipment and security measures. Nests will be managed for safe in-situ incubation and hatching; where in-situ protection is not feasible, the Consultant will implement ex-situ conservation (egg relocation) following accepted protocols and required permits. The Consultant will deploy guards as needed, control predators (e.g., dogs, crows, and other predatory animals), and prevent egg poaching consistent with legal and ethical standards. The Consultant will maintain records of nests managed, relocation activities, hatching success, and predator control actions.   Conduct awareness raising activities The Consultant will conduct awareness meetings with fisher communities on safe handling and release of entangled turtles. The Consultant will identify turtle egg collectors and hold dialogue with them to reduce poaching and promote stewardship. The Consultant will prepare and post informational signboards at key locations, develop and print a sea turtle information poster or leaflet (1,000 copies), and organize media campaigns around turtle hatchling releases and relevant observances (e.g., World Sea Turtle Day), in coordination with local authorities and community groups. The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) can be found at the following website: www.doe.gov.bd The ToR or any further information can be obtained at the address of the undersigned given below, during office hours from 9:00 am to 4:00 pm Bangladesh Standard Time (BST).   The Department of Environment (DoE) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services.  The shortlisting criteria are: a)   General Experience of the Firm in providing services (core business and years in business); b)   The Consultant must have at least 10 years of in-depth working experience on Development of Turtle hatchery in Bangladesh;   Consultants are requested to submit, but not limited to, the following supporting documents in support of the above-mentioned criteria: (i)  The Firm's Incorporation/Trade/registration documents from the country of the firm (ii) Firm’s brochures; (iii) description of similar consultancy contracts, including the scope, contract amount, name of Client, period of the contract (date of contract signing to date of completion), location/ country of the services, etc. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to the Section III, Para 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but shall indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture (i.e. all members of the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable) and/or a sub-consultancy (i.e. the Consultant will be responsible, including for the services of the sub-consultant). In case of an association, the Consultant must explain in the EoI submission (a) the rationale/ justification for the proposed inclusion of the JV members and/or sub-consultants; and (b) the anticipated role and relevant qualifications of each member of the Joint Venture and/or of each sub-consultant for carrying out the assignment. Failure to provide the above explanation in the EoI may risk the association not being shortlisted for the assignment. However, the qualifications/ experience of sub-consultants will not be considered by the Client in the evaluation of Expressions of Interest for Shortlisting purposes. A consulting Firm will be selected following the “Consultant Qualification Selection” method.   Expected date for commencement of the services is March 2027 and the tentative duration of the entire assignment is 12 months. Expressions of Interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person or by mail) by 1500 hours (BST) (GMT + 6 hours) on 29 November, 2026. The authority reserves the right to accept or reject any or all EoIs without assigning any reason, whatsoever.                                                                 Signed Md. Samsuzzaman Sarker Project Director, Host and Rohingya Enhancement of Lives Project (HELP) DoE Component-Comprehensive Environmental Impact and Damage Assessment of Rohingya Influx in Cox’s Bazar and Bhasanchar of Chattogram Division Department of Environment 1st Floor, Room: 202, Poribesh Bhaban New Building E/16 Agargaon, Sher-E-Bangla Nagar, Dhaka-1207, Bangladesh Phone: 02-2222218378, Email: helpdoepd@gmail.com

postings.text: Multimedia and Communications Associate/Consultant | IOM - International Organization for Migration Skip to main content Multimedia and Communications Associate/Consultant IOM - International Organization for Migration Democratic Republic of Congo Both national and international UG - Ungraded level Speaks English, French Application deadline: November 24, 2026 (6 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The International Organization for Migration (IOM) is seeking a Multimedia and Communications Associate/Consultant to support the production and dissemination of multimedia materials in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The role involves capturing and editing high-quality photographs and videos, developing engaging content, and designing communications materials. The consultant will work closely with various teams to ensure that all outputs align with IOM's branding and visibility standards. This position requires strong technical skills in multimedia production and a commitment to ethical storytelling. Candidate Requirements: High school diploma with 5 years experience or Bachelor's degree with 3 years experience Experience in photography, videography, and multimedia content production Proficiency in Adobe Creative Cloud or equivalent software Good writing and editing skills for captions and articles Fluency in French; working knowledge of English is an advantage Ability to work in multicultural environments Job Description Introduction Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.  IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move. IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at  IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration   Project Context and Scope ​​The International Organization for Migration (IOM) is the United Nations Migration Agency, committed to promoting humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. In the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), IOM implements humanitarian, development, peacebuilding and migration governance programmes addressing displacement, protection, community stabilization, durable solutions and migration-related challenges and opportunities. ​Effective communications and visibility are essential to raising awareness of IOM's activities, demonstrating programme results, strengthening donor and partner engagement, and amplifying the voices of displaced persons, other people on the move and host communities. ​Under the overall supervision of the Chief of Mission and the direct supervision of the Media and Communications Officer, the Multimedia and Communications Associate will support the production and dissemination of multimedia and communications materials showcasing IOM's activities and achievements across the DRC, with particular attention on south-eastern DRC. ​The incumbent will provide technical support in photography, videography, video editing, graphic design and digital content production. Working closely with the Media and Communications Officer, programme teams and field offices, the incumbent will help ensure that communications products are accurate, engaging, ethically produced and aligned with IOM's institutional branding, communications standards and donor visibility requirements.   Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing   Programme Support Unit Responsibilities Tasks to be performed under this contract ​​Multimedia Production: Capture, edit and prepare high-quality photographs, videos and other multimedia content documenting IOM's activities, achievements, events, interviews and donor visibility initiatives, ensuring appropriate technical and production standards. ​Content Development and Storytelling: Assist in identifying and documenting human-interest stories, success stories, interviews and testimonials in coordination with programme teams and field offices. Prepare accompanying captions, short articles, social media posts and other written content for review and clearance. ​Graphic Design and Publications: Design and produce communications and visibility materials, including infographics, factsheets, brochures, presentations, banners, social media graphics and other digital or printed products, following IOM's visual identity guidelines and donor branding requirements. ​Digital Communications: Support regular updates to IOM DRC's website and social media platforms by preparing, formatting, and adapting multimedia content for different audiences and communication channels. ​Field Documentation: Support the documentation of programme activities and results through photography, videography and interviews. Undertake field missions, including to remote or humanitarian locations when required and authorized, to collect audiovisual materials in coordination with relevant programme and field teams. ​Media and Event Support: Provide photography, videography, audiovisual and logistical communications support for official visits, donor missions, workshops, campaigns, press events and other activities. Assist in preparing promotional materials and event-related communications products. ​Multimedia Asset Management: Maintain and regularly update the digital archive of photographs, videos, graphics and other communications assets, ensuring appropriate file naming, metadata, captions, consent documentation and secure storage in accordance with IOM procedures. ​Coordination and Collaboration: Liaise with programme teams, field offices and relevant colleagues to gather information, identify multimedia needs and support the timely production of communications materials, under the guidance of the Media and Communications Officer. ​Communications and Visibility Reporting: Compile photographs, videos, success stories, media coverage, social media statistics and other relevant information to support the preparation of project communications updates, donor visibility reports and annual communications reports. ​Perform such other duties as may be assigned.​ Qualifications Required Qualifications and Experience Education ​​High school diploma with at least 5 years of relevant professional experience; or​ ​Bachelor's degree in Multimedia Production, Photography, Film and Video Production, Digital Media, Visual Communications, Journalism, Communications, Graphic Design or a related field from an accredited academic institution, with at least 3 years of relevant professional experience Experience ​​Experience in professional photography, videography, video editing and multimedia content production. ​Experience producing photographs, videos, graphics and other digital content for communications, social media or institutional visibility. ​Experience supporting the development of human-interest stories, interviews, testimonials and other visual storytelling materials. ​Experience using professional photography and videography equipment and multimedia editing software, such as Adobe Creative Cloud, DaVinci Resolve or equivalent tools. ​Experience in graphic design and production of branded communications materials. ​Experience preparing communications and visibility materials for donor-funded programmes, including EU-funded programmes and familiarity with Global Gateway branding, is an advantage. ​Experience documenting humanitarian, community stabilization, border governance, protection or cross-border cooperation activities in eastern DRC is an advantage. ​Experience working with humanitarian, development, UN or other international organizations is an advantage. ​Experience working in eastern DRC or in emergency settings is an advantage.  Skills Good photography, videography and video editing skills, including composition, lighting, sound recording and post-production. Proficiency in multimedia editing and graphic design software, such as Adobe Creative Cloud or equivalent tools. Good visual storytelling skills and ability to produce engaging digital and print communications materials. Good writing and editing skills, including the preparation of captions, short articles and social media content. Ability to present programme activities and results through clear, accurate and accessible visual communications products. Familiarity with digital communications, social media platforms and platform-specific content requirements. Basic understanding of ethical storytelling, informed consent, data protection and donor visibility requirements. Ability to organize and maintain multimedia files and communications archives. Good organizational skills, attention to detail and ability to complete assigned tasks within established deadlines. Ability to work effectively with colleagues and stakeholders in multicultural and multidisciplinary environments.   Languages For this consultancy, fluency in ​French​ is required (oral and written).  ​​Working knowledge of English and/or local languages commonly spoken in eastern DRC is an advantage.​  Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments. Required Competencies IOM’s competency framework can be found at this  link . Competencies will be assessed during the selection process. Values  - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values: Inclusion and respect for diversity : Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion. Integrity and transparency : Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct. Professionalism : Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges. Courage : Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance. Empathy : Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated. Core Competencies  – behavioural indicators Teamwork : Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results. Delivering results : Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes. Managing and sharing knowledge : Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate. Accountability : Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work. Communication : Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way. Notes IOM covers Consultants against occupational accidents and illnesses under the Compensation Plan (CP), free of charge, for the duration of the consultancy. IOM does not provide evacuation or medical insurance for reasons related to non-occupational accidents and illnesses. Consultants are responsible for their own medical insurance for non-occupational accident or illness and will be required to provide written proof of such coverage before commencing work.  Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation. postings.title: Research and Project Assistance - Digital Development and Digital Cooperation UNESCWA - United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Western Asia Beirut CON
postings.text: Research and Project Assistance - Digital Development and Digital Cooperation | UNESCWA - United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Western Asia Skip to main content Research and Project Assistance - Digital Development and Digital Cooperation UNESCWA - United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Western Asia Beirut CON level Speaks Arabic, English, French Application deadline: November 23, 2026 (5 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The Economic and Social Commission for Western Asia is seeking a Research and Project Assistant to provide substantive, research, coordination, documentation, and operational support for digital development initiatives. The role involves assisting with the preparation and follow-up of key forums and workshops, coordinating inputs and timelines, and supporting various product streams related to digital cooperation. The candidate will also be responsible for drafting documents, conducting research, and ensuring quality assurance across deliverables. This position is based in Beirut and is expected to last for 3.5 months. Candidate Requirements: Bachelor's degree in relevant field Minimum two years of research and analysis experience Fluency in English and Arabic Experience in digital cooperation and development Knowledge of sustainable development issues Result of Service Expected outputs comprise: • IGM 6.0 and DCDF 3.0 work packages: the complete set of substantive, coordination and operational materials for preparation, delivery and follow-up — including the Tunisia national workshop and the regional EGM / High-Level Roundtable convened back to back with IGM 6.0 — with maintained contribution and follow-up trackers. • ADA 2.0, ADDR 3.0 and MMM/GM work packages: research and evidence inputs, consultation and comments matrices, consolidated drafting inputs and revised text, annexes, statistical tables and visual aids, validation and issue logs, and updated assessment elements, metadata and guidance. • Integrated delivery and follow-up tracker: a regularly updated workplan covering responsibilities, milestones, deadlines, clearances, versions, action points and interdependencies across the channels and product streams. • Progress and handover documentation: concise periodic progress updates and an organized final handover package of working files, source materials, outstanding actions and cleared versions. Furthermore, support to: NDDRs 3.0 for 12 countries; ADD-FPM 3.0; ESCWA inputs to WSIS+20 follow-up and GDC-related processes, including WSIS-GDC matrices, and participation in global and regional fora; JTC/CRTCM and AWG meetings and related follow-ups; preparations for the LAS Permanent Committee, Executive Bureau and ATICM meetings of December 2026 and January 2027; the DCD-OP, related portals and the Observatories; and general project level support functions across the above. Work Location UN-ESCWA Expected duration 3.5 MONTHS Duties and Responsibilities OBJECTIVES The services of an individual contractor are required to provide substantive, research, coordination, documentation and operational support under ADCD-ASAP, Phase 2, through: • two priority engagement channels: the sixth session of the Committee on Technology for Development (IGM 6.0); and the third Arab Digital Cooperation and Development Forum (DCDF 3.0), targeted for end January 2027, subject to host confirmation, with its three high-level segments — the second High-Level Partners Conference on the Arab Digital Agenda (HLPC.ADA 2.0) the fifth Arab High-Level Forum on WSIS and the 2030 Agenda (AHLF.WSIS 5.0) and the eighth Arab Internet Governance Forum (Arab IGF 8.0) — including their preparatory, delivery and follow-up processes; and • two interlinked product streams: the second Arab Digital Agenda (ADA 2.0); and the third Arab Digital Development Report (ADDR 3.0), underpinned by the National Digital Development Reviews (NDDRs 3.0), together with the Digital Development Measurement and Monitoring Model and its Guiding Manual (MMM/GM) and the Arab Digital Development Framework and Processes Manual (ADD-FPM 3.0). Furthermore, the services support ESCWA’s standing digital cooperation and development processes, platforms and mechanisms, as set out below. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES Under the supervision of the ADCD-ASAP team, the IC will: • support the preparation, delivery and follow-up of IGM 6.0 and of DCDF 3.0 with its HLPC.ADA 2.0 AHLF.WSIS 5.0 and Arab IGF 8.0 components, including concept, background and official documentation, draft agendas, invitations, speaker and stakeholder coordination, briefing and presentation materials, talking points, summary records, outreach materials and follow-up actions. • support the Tunisia national workshop on the National Digital Development Review and the regional expert group meeting / High-Level Roundtable of Digital Development Leaders, convened back to back with IGM 6.0, including concept and information notes, agendas, invitations, participant coordination, documentation, session messages and follow-up. • coordinate inputs, timelines, clearances and operational arrangements with the ADCD-ASAP team, relevant ESCWA units, member countries, the League of Arab States and other regional and international partners. • support preparatory workshops, expert group meetings, consultations, coordination meetings and capacity-building activities linked to the channels and product streams, including participant coordination, documentation, concise minutes, action points and follow-up. In relation to the two interlinked product streams, the IC will: • ADA 2.0: support desk research, stakeholder consultations, consolidation of inputs, drafting and revision of substantive sections, evidence tables and annexes, and validation, editing and follow-up documentation. • ADDR 3.0 and NDDRs 3.0: support the compilation, validation and analysis of country and regional evidence; examine datasets and country submissions, identify gaps and inconsistencies and maintain validation and issue logs; prepare statistical tables, graphs and other visual aids; assist in drafting and reviewing technical inputs; and support expert review and consultation processes. • MMM/GM and ADD-FPM 3.0: support the revision, documentation and quality assurance of both instruments, including information elements, metadata, assessment instruments, guidance, country inputs and capacity-building materials. • ensure substantive and terminological coherence across the channels and product streams, including accurate cross-references and consistent use of agreed concepts, classifications and version labels; and proofread and edit outgoing documents for adherence to United Nations style and ESCWA formats and publishable readiness. • prepare communication, outreach and basic web-ready materials, and support ESCWA’s Digital Cooperation and Development online platform (DCD-OP) and related portals (ADA, CPF, NDDR-ADDR) by organizing, updating and quality-checking content and resources for publishing, in coordination with the relevant ESCWA units. Furthermore, the IC will support the following standing processes, mechanisms and support functions: • NDDRs 3.0 for 12 countries: support country inputs and their validation, national consultations, drafting and review, and follow-up with country counterparts. • Global and regional processes: support ESCWA inputs to WSIS+20 follow-up and Global Digital Compact (GDC)-related processes, including WSIS-GDC matrices, and to global and regional fora and mechanisms (e.g. the WSIS Forum, UNGIS, CSTD and IGF 2026), by consolidating inputs and drafting briefing and background notes. • Observatories: support the development, population and maintenance of the regional and national Digital Development and Digital Cooperation Observatories. • JTC/CRTCM and Arab Working Group meetings: contribute to the preparation and organization of the ESCWA–LAS ADA Joint Technical Committee and Core Research and Technical Cooperation Mechanisms (JTC/CRTCM) series, and co-organize the LAS Arab Working Group on ICT Strategy (AWG) series, in support of ADA 2.0, NDDRs 3.0 and MMM/GM, by drafting information notes, agendas, lists of invitees and reports, and supporting one-to-one country follow-ups. • LAS intergovernmental meetings: support preparations for the meetings of the LAS Permanent Committee and Executive Bureau, and of the Arab Telecommunications and Information Technology Council of Ministers (ATICM), of December 2026 and January 2027, including background documentation, agenda items, submissions on ADA 2.0 and ADDR 3.0, and follow-up. • General project level support: provide, under supervision, the full range of project-level support functions — correspondence and the production of large, complex documents, reports, tables, presentations and trackers; calendars, meeting scheduling, attendance and minutes; version control, deadline tracking and information flow with the relevant ESCWA units; and all arrangements for official events and meetings (e.g. room reservations, guest and participant lists, invitations, catering, seating arrangements, background documentation and special equipment), in coordination with internal and external stakeholders and partners as relevant. • perform other related tasks and duties as assigned. Qualifications/special skills A Bachelor's degree in information society, digital cooperation and digital development, economics, development studies, sustainable development or related area is required. All candidates must submit a copy of the required educational degree. Incomplete applications will not be reviewed A minimum of two years of professional work experience in research and analysis relating to the Arab region is required. Experience and knowledge of information society, digital cooperation and digital development, economics and sustainable development issues are desirable. Experience with an international organization in a developmental field is desirable. Languages English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat; and Arabic is a working language of ESCWA. For this position, fluency in English and Arabic is required. Note: “Fluency” equals a rating of ‘fluent’ in all four areas (speak, read, write, and understand) and “Knowledge of” equals a rating of ‘confident’ in two of the four areas. Additional Information Recruitment for this position is on a local basis. The incumbent is required to have the legal right to live and work in the specified working location. No Fee THE UNITED NATIONS DOES NOT CHARGE A FEE AT ANY STAGE OF THE RECRUITMENT PROCESS (APPLICATION, INTERVIEW MEETING, PROCESSING, OR TRAINING). THE UNITED NATIONS DOES NOT CONCERN ITSELF WITH INFORMATION ON APPLICANTS’ BANK ACCOUNTS. postings.text: National Project Workforce-Research Associate - Pulses Pre-Breeding | ICRISAT - The International Crops Research Institute for the Semi-Arid Tropics Skip to main content National Project Workforce-Research Associate - Pulses Pre-Breeding ICRISAT - The International Crops Research Institute for the Semi-Arid Tropics Hyderabad, Patancheru National Research Associate - Pulses Pre-Breeding level Speaks English Application deadline: December 12, 2026 (24 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool ICRISAT is seeking a Research Associate for the Pulses Pre-Breeding National Project to support disease screening and gene discovery in pigeonpea. The role involves coordinating trials, managing project execution, and publishing research findings. The candidate will bridge classical breeding with genomics and oversee technical personnel. This is a contract position based at ICRISAT Headquarters in Hyderabad, India. Candidate Requirements: Ph.D. in Plant Breeding or Genetics Experience in legumes Knowledge of pre-breeding technologies Skills in wide hybridization and molecular biology Statistical skills and data management Fluency in English with publication record Key skills Wide-hybridization resistance-breeding trait mapping utilization crop wild relatives Additional/Preferred Skills Quantitative and qualitative research plant breeding genomics, molecular biology research Preferred Qualifications Ph.D. in Plant Breeding Ph.D. in Genetics About ICRISAT   ICRISAT is a non-profit, non-political organization that conducts agricultural research for development in Asia and Africa, working with partners around the world. Drylands cover about 45% of the world's land, are home to 2.3 billion people (one in three) and support 45–50% of the world's livestock. ICRISAT's vision is a prosperous, food-secure and resilient dryland tropics. ICRISAT is headquartered in Patancheru, Hyderabad, India, with two regional hubs and eight country offices in Africa. For more information visit - www.icrisat.org Role Purpose   ICRISAT seeks applications from dynamic and motivated professionals for the position of National Project Workforce - Research Associate (Pulses Pre-Breeding), to support the cluster of Genebank (Wide Hybridization) under the Global Research Program - Accelerated Crop Improvement. The incumbent will be responsible for multi-location disease screening, co-ordinating assembly development, gene discovery in pigeonpea, along with any additional tasks assigned by the Principal Investigator. The position is based at ICRISAT Headquarters, Patancheru, Hyderabad, Telangana, India. Key Responsibilities:   Coordinate and lead disease screening trials at key hot-spot locations across India; implement standardized phenotypic evaluation protocols and epidemiological scoring to identify resistant introgression lines under heavy disease pressure. Harvest untapped genetic diversity from crop wild relatives by executing wide crosses, cytogenetic characterizations, and genomic characterization of pigeonpea gene pool. Supervision of computational genomic analysis; investigate genome architecture, structural variations, and evolutionary research. Discover, validate, and deploy high-throughput molecular markers for downstream marker-assisted selection (MAS). Bridge classical plant breeding, cytogenetics, and computational genomics to transition validated, high-value pre-breeding lines and derivatives into national downstream breeding pipelines. Oversee overall project execution, including managing field and laboratory technical personnel, budget tracking, technical documentation, high-impact scientific publications, and resource mobilization to fulfil all project objectives. Participate in resource mobilization with groundnut research teams. Publish research findings in peer reviewed journals. Participate actively in project review and planning meetings and in reporting on progress. Collaborate with research staff and technicians within and from other clusters/disciplines per the project requirement. Execute experiments related to stem rot screening and gene discovery in adherence to the defined schedules and timeline and in compliance with the institute policies. Reporting and maintaining accurate and high-quality data files required to prepare project reports. Support the Principal Investigator in writing technical reports. Responsible for completing the assigned activities.   Essential Qualifications:   The candidate should have a PhD in Genetics and Plant Breeding, with experience in legumes. Knowledge of the latest technologies applicable to pre-breeding, cyto-genetics, molecular biology, and genomics. Knowledge of wide hybridization, ploidy estimation, sequencing, Gene discovery and characterization and populations development and field-based experiments. Statistical skills, knowledge of electronic data collection, databases, data management and interpretation. Fluency in spoken and written English and excellent publication record in international peer-reviewed journals Experience with applied research related to innovations in legume pre-breeding would be an added advantage   Terms of Appointment This is a contract role for 24 months (02 years). It may be renewed based on performance and the Institute’s continuing need for the position. How to apply The position will remain open until a suitable candidate is identified. Shortlisting will start from 12 December 2026. All applicants should apply with their latest resume, and the names and contact information of three references that are knowledgeable about their professional qualifications and work experience. All applications will be acknowledged; however, only short-listed candidates will be contacted. Applicants must be nationals of the country of assignment or possess a valid work permit and legal authorization to work in the country to be eligible to apply for this position. ICRISAT is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to increasing diversity and maintaining a progressive and inclusive workplace. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of their ethnicity, race, gender, religious beliefs, sexual orientation, age, marital status or whether they have a disability. postings.text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION) THE FEDERAL DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF ETHIOPIA LOWLANDS LIVELIHOOD RESILIENCE PROJECT – PHASE II (LLRP-II) Credit No.: IDA-7519-ET Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for Route Selection and Survey, Feasibility Study, Detailed Engineering Design, ESIA, and Tender Document Preparation for Four Gravel Access Roads: Kelem–Selegn, Goldiya–Alfature, Kolango–Tsemaha, and Hana–Erka and Three Bridges: Kolango, Tikiboko Bezo River, and Hana River Projects in South Ethiopia Region  Reference No.: ET-SE-RPCU-571226-CS-QCBS The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project – Phase Two (LLRP-II), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The consulting services (the “Services”) shall comprise route selection and survey, feasibility studies, detailed engineering design, Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA), and preparation of tender documents for the following four (4) gravel access road projects and three (3) bridge projects located in the South Ethiopia Regional State. Project information S. No Project Name Location Estimated Road Length (km) 1 Kelem to Selegn Gravel  Road South Omo Zone , Dasenech Woreda 30 Km 2 Goldiya to Alfature  Gravel Road South Omo Zone, Benatsemay Woreda 25 Km 3 Kolango to Tsemaha Gravel  Road Alle Zone Kolango-Zuriya Woreda 25 Km 4 Hana to Erka Gravel  Road South Omo Zone, Salamago Woreda 17 Km   S. No Project Name Location Estimated Bridge Span Length (m) 1 Kolango Bridge Alle Zone Kolango-Zuriya Woreda 50m 2 Tikiboko Bezo River Bridge South Omo Zone ,Malle Woreda 50m 3 Hana River Bridge South Omo Zone, Salamago Woreda 30m   The Services will be carried out in two phases, following the latest Ethiopian Roads Administration (ERA) design manuals and quality manual, the LLRP-II environmental and social instruments and the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF):   (a)  Phase I – Route Selection and Survey, and Feasibility Study: identification and multi-criteria comparison of at least three alternative routes; site reconnaissance and investigation; stakeholder consultation; traffic counts and axle load surveys; full topographic survey and Digital Terrain Model; preliminary design; ESIA of the selected route; preliminary cost estimates; economic evaluation; and climate and natural hazard vulnerability assessment.   (b) Phase II – Detailed Engineering Design, ESIA and Preparation of Bidding Documents: materials and site investigation; geometric, drainage, pavement, geotechnical and bridge/structural design, including an independent bridge design check; road safety design and audit; utilities and private accesses; estimate of the construction contract period; final ESIA and Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP); and preparation of bidding documents based on the World Bank Standard Procurement Documents, including technical specifications, drawings, bills of quantities and the Engineer’s cost estimate.    The implementation period is 3 (three) calendar month, from contract signing. Expected start date of assignment will be within 7 days from contract signing ensuring full consistency with the TOR referred to in this REOI.   The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below.   The South Ethiopia Regional State, Irrigation and Lowlands Development Bureau, Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project (LLRP-II) Regional Project Coordination Unit now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:   (a)  Core business and years in business: the firm’s core business shall be in road/highway engineering consultancy services. Provide the company profile, certificate of registration and number of years in business. (b) General experience: experience in civil engineering consultancy services (studies, design and/or construction supervision of roads, bridges or other civil infrastructure) during the last ten (10) years. (c)  Specific experience: experience in assignments of similar nature and complexity, i.e. feasibility studies and detailed engineering design of roads (new construction, rehabilitation or upgrading, including gravel/low-volume roads) and of bridges, covering route selection, topographic surveys, hydrological and hydraulic studies, drainage and bridge structures, ESIA and preparation of bidding documents, preferably in arid, semi-arid or lowland areas and under projects financed by the World Bank or other international development partners. For each assignment, indicate the client, location, road length and/or bridge span, contract value, duration, scope of services and the firm’s role, supported by contract or completion certificates. (d) Technical and managerial capability of the firm: organizational structure, survey equipment (e.g. GPS and total stations), access to soil and materials testing laboratories, road design and economic evaluation software, quality assurance systems, and capacity to mobilize multidisciplinary field teams to remote areas of South Ethiopia Region.   Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.   The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, Seventh Edition, 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.   A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality- and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.   Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours, 8:30 A.M. to 5:30 P.M. local time, on working days.   Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, in hard copy) on December 02, 2026 at 3:00 P.M. local time.   South Ethiopia Regional State, Irrigation and Lowlands Development Bureau Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project, Phase Two (LLRP-II) Regional Project Coordination Unit (RPCU) Attn: Procurement Officer, Room No. 10 Jinka, South Ethiopia Region, Ethiopia Tel: +251 -933326263; +251 -91 687 6489 E-mail: amnendere12@gmail.com, belaynehfekadu19@gmail.com, millionteklie172@gmail.com

Three objectives to be achieved by implementing the framework approach include: (i) Support the strengthening of health systems needed by Member States to deliver integrated services for tropical and vector-borne disease; (ii) Support the scaling up of implementation of targeted, integrated tropical and vector-borne disease interventions; (iii) Strengthen the prevention and control of tropical and vector-borne disease outbreaks in epidemic-prone Member States. postings.text: Senior Strategic Partnership Specialist | FAO - Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations Skip to main content Senior Strategic Partnership Specialist FAO - Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations Italy International Consultant - Contractors Agreement level Speaks Chinese, Arabic, English, French, Russian Application deadline: December 01, 2026 (13 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The Senior Strategic Partnerships Specialist at FAO will support the strategic positioning, partnership development, and resource mobilization efforts of the Agrifood Systems Transformation Unit. This role involves fostering strategic partnerships, expanding engagement with various stakeholders, and mobilizing resources for agrifood systems transformation initiatives. The incumbent will also develop partnership strategies, advise on funding opportunities, and facilitate coordination across FAO divisions. The position requires a strong background in strategic partnerships and resource mobilization within the context of food and agriculture. Candidate Requirements: Advanced university degree in relevant fields or bachelor's with additional experience At least 10 years of relevant experience in strategic partnerships and resource mobilization Experience engaging with governments, research institutions, and international organizations Working knowledge of English; knowledge of a second FAO language is an asset CALL FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST - VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT : IMPORTANT NOTICE: Please note that Closure Date and Time displayed above are based on date and time settings of your personal device FAO is committed to achieving workforce diversity in terms of gender, nationality, background and culture. Qualified female applicants, qualified nationals of non-and under-represented Members and person with disabilities are encouraged to apply; Everyone who works for FAO is required to adhere to the highest standards of integrity and professional conduct, and to uphold FAO's values FAO, as a Specialized Agency of the United Nations, has a zero-tolerance policy for conduct that is incompatible with its status, objectives and mandate, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination All selected candidates will undergo rigorous reference and background checks All applications will be treated with the strictest confidentiality FAO’s commitment to environmental sustainability is integral to our strategic objectives and operations. Organizational Setting The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) contributes to the achievement of the 2030 Agenda through the FAO Strategic Framework by supporting the transformation to MORE efficient, inclusive, resilient and sustainable agrifood systems, for better production, better nutrition, a better environment, and a better life, leaving no one behind. The Division of Agrifood Systems and Food Safety (ESF) at FAO provides strategic leadership to drive agrifood system transformation by supporting FAO headquarters, decentralized offices, Members and partners in taking a systems approach to policy, programmes and projects, including through normative products, methods and tools; documentation and collective learning of systems approaches; and support for implementation at the national and subnational level. Within ESF, the Agrifood System Transformation Unit provides thought leadership, technical expertise, and operational support to advance the adoption and implementation of a systems approach to agrifood systems transformation. This work is guided by a broader, holistic vision of food systems transformation—one that recognizes the interconnectedness of environmental, social, economic, and governance dimensions and seeks to drive sustainable change across all levels of the system. Reporting Lines The Senior Strategic Partnerships Specialist will report to the Director, ESF. Technical Focus The Senior Strategic Partnerships Specialist supports the strategic positioning, partnership development and resource mobilization efforts of the Agrifood Systems Transformation Unit and the wider Division of Agrifood Systems and Food Safety (ESF). The incumbent contributes to strengthening the visibility, influence and financing of agrifood systems transformation by fostering strategic partnerships, expanding engagement with traditional and non-traditional partners, and supporting the mobilization of resources for global, regional and country-level initiatives. The role supports the development of strategic narratives, partnership and fundraising approaches, engagement with bilateral and multilateral donors, International Financial Institutions (IFIs), foundations, research institutions, private-sector actors, coalitions and networks, and contributes to the design and advancement of resource mobilization and partnership opportunities that accelerate agrifood systems transformation. Particular attention will be given to expanding partnerships beyond traditional donor relationships and strengthening engagement with strategic partners and global platforms. Tasks and responsibilities • Advise and support the Director of the Agrifood Systems and Food Safety Division on strategic partnerships, stakeholder engagement and resource mobilization priorities. • Support the strategic positioning of ESF and its agrifood systems transformation agenda through coherent messaging and external visibility initiatives that strengthen FAO's leadership on agrifood systems transformation. • Support the design, launch, coordination and expansion of strategic partnerships that advance agrifood systems transformation objectives. • Develop and advise on partnership and resource mobilization strategies, including approaches to engage new partners, refine partnership and funding modalities, and strengthen long-term collaboration opportunities. • Develop and cultivate relationships with existing and prospective partners, expanding engagement to governments, bilateral and multilateral donors, International Financial Institutions (IFIs), foundations, research institutions, civil society organizations, coalitions, networks and private-sector partners. • Support or represent the Director of the Agrifood Systems and Food Safety Division in engagements, outreach activities, bilateral meetings and events geared at strengthening partner and resource mobilization efforts. • Advise and support technical teams in translating priorities, programmes and knowledge products into funding and partnership propositions. • Identify, assess, and advance funding and partnership opportunities, coordinating follow-up actions and ensuring progress on agreed priorities • Monitor trends, policy developments, donor priorities and financing opportunities relevant to agrifood systems transformation and provide strategic analysis and recommendations. • Support the preparation of briefing materials, presentations, communications products, partnership reports and engagement materials for internal and external audiences. • Facilitate coordination across FAO divisions, decentralized offices, technical teams and external partners to advance partnership and resource mobilization objectives. • Provide day-to-day technical, strategic and coordination support related to partnership development, stakeholder engagement and resource mobilization activities, and perform other related duties as required CANDIDATES WILL BE ASSESSED AGAINST THE FOLLOWING Minimum Requirements • For Consultants: Advanced university degree in Agricultural, Biological, Environmental, Food or Social Science, Natural Resource Management, Economics, International Development or Relations, International or Public Policy, Programme or Project Management, Business or Public Administration, Public Relations or Affairs, Communications, or another field directly relevant to the work of FAO. Consultants with bachelor's degree need two additional years of relevant professional experience. • For PSAs: University degree (or technical degree certificate) from an institution recognized by the International Association of Universities (IAU)/UNESCO in public policy, public administration, social science, political science, Agricultural, Biological, Environmental, Food or Social Science, Natural Resource Management, Economics, International Development or Relations, International or Public Policy, Programme or Project Management, Business or Public Administration, Public Relations or Affairs, Communications, or another field directly relevant to the work of FAO • At least 10 years of relevant experience in strategic partnerships, resource mobilization, programme or project management, stakeholder engagement, business development and/or related fields, including engagement with governments, research institutions, international organizations, civil society, private-sector actors and development partners. • Working knowledge (level C) of English. Knowledge of a second FAO language is an asset (Arabic, Chinese, French or Russien). FAO Core Competencies • Results Focus • Teamwork • Communication • Building Effective Relationships • Knowledge Sharing and Continuous Improvement Selection Criteria • Extent and relevance of experience on establishing new strategic partnerships • Extent and relevance of resource mobilization experience • Extent and relevance of experience working in UN and international agency system • Extent and relevance of experience of working on the theme of food and agriculture Please note that all candidates should adhere to FAO Values of Commitment to FAO, Respect for All and Integrity and Transparency ADDITIONAL INFORMATION FAO does not charge any fee at any stage of the recruitment process (application, interview, processing) Please note that FAO will only consider academic credentials or degrees obtained from an educational institution recognized in the IAU/UNESCO list Please note that FAO only considers higher educational qualifications obtained from an institution accredited/recognized in the World Higher Education Database (WHED), a list updated by the International Association of Universities (IAU) / United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO). This role involves developing a monitoring and evaluation framework, managing a regional database, and tracking progress against climate and health indicators. The specialist will produce data summaries and dashboards, prepare reports for donors, and support country offices with data collection and quality assurance. This position is crucial for enhancing the CHE unit's capacity to report on health impacts related to climate change. WHO seeks to promote health, ensure everyone can attain the highest level of health, keep the world safe and serve the vulnerable through partnerships, people and countries.
