postings.text: Consultancy for Staff Team Building and Wellbeing | We Effect Skip to main content Consultancy for Staff Team Building and Wellbeing We Effect Nairobi National Consultancy level Speaks English Advanced degree (Masters level) or higher Application deadline: November 25, 2026 (7 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool We Effect is seeking a qualified facilitator for a team-building and wellbeing session aimed at enhancing work-life balance and psychosocial wellbeing among its staff in East Africa. The facilitator will design and deliver an interactive session that promotes trust, communication, and collaboration within the team. The session will include professional learning, guided reflection, and practical activities to help staff manage workload pressures and support each other's wellbeing. The facilitator must create a safe and inclusive environment for sensitive discussions and ensure that all activities are engaging and participatory. Candidate Requirements: Relevant degree in psychology, counselling, or related field Experience in facilitating employee wellbeing and work-life balance sessions Proven team building and group facilitation experience Strong interpersonal skills for managing sensitive conversations Understanding of confidentiality and psychological safety TERMS OF REFERENCE   Facilitation of Staff Team Building, Work-Life Balance and Psychosocial Wellbeing Session   We Effect - East Africa   Assignment   Team Building and Wellbeing Facilitator   Venue   TBC   Proposed date(s)   9 th December 2026   Duration   One full-day session, including preparation and brief post-session reporting   Participants   We Effect staff in East Africa – approximately 15 participants   Application deadline   25 th November 2026   1. Background   We Effect is an international development cooperation organisation founded in 1958 by the Swedish cooperative movement, with a vision of a sustainable and just world free from poverty. Working through cooperatives and other member-based organisations, We Effect supports people living in poverty to strengthen their livelihoods and secure their rights. In East Africa, its programmes in Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania focus on sustainable rural development and adequate housing, promoting gender equality and strengthening communities’ resilience to climate change. This work is guided by We Effect’s current strategy, which places the Right to Food at its core.   Following restructuring and transitional processes that happened between 2025/2026, there has been changes in roles, in some cases increased responsibilities and the team members are slowly finding their space and adapting to the new structure and additional roles. In this context, the session will provide space for staff to reflect, connect and identify practical individual and team approaches to managing workload pressures, protecting time for rest and personal life, and supporting one another’s wellbeing through the transition.    We Effect is committed to fostering a healthy, inclusive and collaborative working environment for its staff in East Africa. As part of its staff wellbeing and team development efforts, We Effect intends to engage a qualified facilitator to design and deliver an interactive team-building session focusing on work-life balance, psychosocial wellbeing and stronger workplace relationships.   The sessions should combine professional learning, guided reflection, and practical team-building activities. It should be engaging and participatory rather than lecture-based, and should enable staff to connect, learn, and identify practical ways of supporting individual and collective wellbeing. Further, it should bring out personal experiences, reflections, and recommendations among the team members on how to forge ahead as a team.   2. Purpose of the Assignment   The purpose of the assignment is to engage a professional facilitator who can teach, guide sensitive workplace conversations and bring staff together through inclusive and enjoyable activities. The facilitator will create a safe environment for reflection on work-life balance and psychosocial wellbeing while strengthening trust, communication, and collaboration across the team. The aim is to further enhance the psychological safety of staff and foster team spirit.   3. Objectives   Increase staff awareness of work-life balance, psychosocial wellbeing, and their contribution to a healthy and productive workplace.   Equip participants with practical tools for managing stress, setting healthy boundaries, and building personal resilience.   Enhance psychological safety by f acilitat ing constructive conversations , feedback and recommendations on workplace wellbeing in a professional manner in a safe, secure, trusted , nonjudgmental environment devoid of personalized discussions or infringement of individuals privacy .   Strengthen team connection, mutual understanding, trust, communication, and collaboration.   Enable staff to agree on practical individual and team commitments that support healthier ways of working.   4. Scope of Work   The facilitator will be expected to:   Hold an inception discussion with We Effect to understand the team context, participant profile, expectations and desired outcomes.   Develop and submit a detailed session design and agenda that balances learning, reflection, interaction and recreation.   Facilitate practical conversations on work-life balance, stress awareness, healthy boundaries, resilience, coping strategies, supportive workplace relationships and access to appropriate professional support.   Design team-building activities that encourage connection, communication, collaboration, appreciation of different strengths and a sense of belonging.   Ensure activities are inclusive and sensitive to differences in culture, age, gender, personality, physical ability and individual comfort levels.   Provide all required facilitation materials and handouts and submit a concise post-session report with key group-level observations and recommendations.   5. Expected Facilitation Approach   The approach should be professional, warm, inclusive, reflective and enjoyable. The facilitator should use a suitable mix of:   Short expert presentation and practical wellbeing tools   Guided conversations and individual reflection   Small-group discussions and experiential learning   Team challenges, energizers and recreational activities   Any other participatory approach that the facilitator may deem necessary   Closing reflection and practical commitments   Long lecture-style presentations should be minimized. Sensitive discussions must be handled in a manner that protects dignity, confidentiality, voluntary participation, and psychological safety.   6. Key Deliverables   An inception discussion and agreed facilitation concept.   A detailed agenda, methodology , and activity plan submitted before the session.   Participant materials, tools and any equipment required for facilitation.   Professional facilitation of the agreed full-day team building and wellbeing session.   A brief post-session report summarizing activities, group-level themes, participant feedback and practical recommendations. The report must not attribute sensitive comments to individual staff members.   7. Required Qualifications and Experience   The lead facilitator should demonstrate:   Relevant professional training at basic degree level in psychology, counselling psychology, organizational psychology, human resource management, organizational development, occupational health, coaching or a related field.   Demonstrated experience facilitating employee wellbeing, psychosocial wellbeing, work-life balance, resilience or workplace wellness sessions.   Proven experience in team building, group development and facilitation of diverse or multicultural teams.   Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to manage sensitive conversations professionally and translate technical wellbeing concepts into practical workplace applications.   A clear understanding of confidentiality, safeguarding, professional boundaries and psychological safety.   Appropriate mental health, psychology or counselling expertise within the proposed facilitation team where psychosocial content forms a substantial part of the methodology .   8. Proposal Submission Requirements   Interested consultants or firms should submit the following:   A brief technical proposal demonstrating understanding of the assignment including    proposed methodology and indicative programme for the session.   A consultant/company profile and CV(s) of the proposed facilitator(s).   Attach copies of relevant academic and professional qualifications or certifications.   A t least two comparable assignments and contactable client references.   A financial proposal showing professional fees, taxes and any reimbursable or activity-related costs separately presented in Kenya shillings .   Confirmation of availability for the proposed date.   9. Evaluation Criteria   Evaluation criterion   Weight   Understanding of the assignment and proposed methodology   25%   Relevant qualifications and professional competence   15%   Experience in psychosocial wellbeing/workplace wellness   20%   Team-building and group facilitation experience   20%   Comparable assignments and references   10%   Financial proposal and value for money   10%   Total   100%   10. Confidentiality and Professional Conduct   The facilitator must maintain confidentiality and conduct the assignment with professionalism, respect and cultural sensitivity. Participants must not be pressured to disclose personal experiences, health information, family circumstances or other sensitive matters in group settings. Any wellbeing concerns requiring specialized support should be handled through appropriate professional referral rather than group intervention.   11. Submission of Proposals   Proposals should be submitted electronically on the Impactpool portal no later than [25/11/2026].   Requests for clarification may be sent to [procurement.ea@weeffect.org].   12. Reservation   We Effect reserves the right to accept or reject any proposal, request clarification, negotiate elements of a proposal, or cancel the procurement process without awarding a contract. Submission of a proposal does not create any contractual obligation on the part of We Effect.       Ethics and Anticorruption Clause   We Effect has zero tolerance towards corruption and fraud. The consultant/service provider shall act with integrity, transparency and honesty and shall not offer, request, give or accept any bribe, improper payment, gift or other undue benefit. Any actual or potential conflict of interest must be promptly disclosed. Any substantiated breach may result in disqualification, termination of the contract and/or referral to the relevant authorities, in accordance with We Effect’s Anti-Corruption and Integrity Policy, Code of Conduct and procurement requirement       At Impactpool we do our best to provide you the most accurate info, but closing dates may be wrong on our site. postings.text: National Consultant / Administrative Support (Local Post for Nationals of Azerbaijan)) | UN WOMEN - United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women Skip to main content National Consultant / Administrative Support (Local Post for Nationals of Azerbaijan)) UN WOMEN - United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women Baku National Senior level Speaks Azerbaijani, English Application deadline: November 25, 2026 (7 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool UN Women is seeking a National Consultant / Administrative Support to provide programmatic, administrative, and logistical support for the implementation of its Azerbaijan Bi-Annual Workplan 2026-2027. The role involves coordinating activities, maintaining records, and supporting financial management and stakeholder engagement. The consultant will work closely with various teams and partners to ensure effective program execution and reporting. This position is office-based in Baku, Azerbaijan. Candidate Requirements: Completion of secondary education Bachelor’s degree in business administration or related fields (desirable) At least 7 years of experience in administration, procurement, HR, or logistics (4 years with Bachelor's degree) Experience with multiple office software packages Experience with ERP systems, preferably Oracle Cloud (desirable) Fluency in Azerbaijani and English Background: UN Women, grounded in the vision of equality enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations, works for the elimination of discrimination against women and girls; the empowerment of women; and the achievement of equality between women and men as partners and beneficiaries of development, human rights, humanitarian action and peace and security.  In Azerbaijan, UN Women works in partnership with government institutions, civil society organizations, academia, the media, and public and private sector actors to advance national priorities on gender equality and women’s empowerment. Its work is grounded in the advancement of women’s rights and aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) 2026–2030. The women’s economic empowerment (WEE) portfolio focuses on transforming care systems; advancing women in the world of work; partnership with the private sector, including implementation of the Women’s Empowerment Principles (WEPs); and promoting gender-responsive climate action. Cross-cutting issues include social norms, financing for gender equality, and gender-responsive macroeconomic policies.  The Project Associate will provide programme, administrative and logistical support to the implementation of UN Women’s Azerbaijan Bi-Annual Workplan (BWP) 2026-2027.. The role will support the planning, coordination, delivery and monitoring of activities across these areas, contributing to the achievement of the BWP’s planned results. Reporting to the Women’s Economic Empowerment Programme Specialist, based in the UN Women Country Office in Tbilisi, Georgia, the Project Associate will support the implementation of Azerbaijan BWP 2026-2027. The Project Associate will work closely with programme and operations teams in Azerbaijan, Georgia and the Europe and Central Asia (ECA) Regional Office, and with Responsible Parties in Azerbaijan, to facilitate coordinated implementation, reporting and follow-up on planned activities and results. Description of Responsibilities/ Scope of Work The national consultant will be responsible  for : Provide administrative support to programme implementation and monitoring: Provide administrative support in preparing programme work plans, budgets, implementation schedules and other programme documentation. Support the collection, compilation and organization of programme data and information required for routine monitoring, reporting and follow-up. Collect and compile information and supporting documentation from partners and follow up on outstanding submissions and documentation. Maintain programme records, files, trackers and supporting documentation and ensure that information is organized and regularly updated. Support the compilation and formatting of narrative and financial information received from Responsible Parties for programme monitoring and reporting purposes. Prepare and compile supporting information and documentation required for programme/project audits and follow-up on requested documentation. Support routine correspondence and follow-up with Responsible Parties, partners and other stakeholders regarding programme implementation and administrative requirements. Provide administrative support to  programme financial management: Support monitoring of programme budgets and expenditures by maintaining and regularly updating internal budget and expenditure tracking tools. Compile financial information and supporting documentation received from partners for review by relevant programme and operations personnel. Support the collection, verification for completeness, organization and filing of supporting documentation. Prepare and organize supporting documentation required for payments, procurement and other financial and administrative processes for submission to the responsible UN Women personnel. Maintain organized records of programme expenditures, commitments and supporting documentation and follow up on outstanding documents as required. Provide administrative  and logistical  support to the Programme Unit: Undertake logistical and administrative arrangements for meetings, workshops, consultations, trainings, events and missions. Coordinate practical arrangements with participants, partners, service providers and other stakeholders, including invitations, participant lists, venues, materials and other logistical requirements. Support travel arrangements for the Programme Team and other programme participants, including preparation and compilation of required travel documentation. Prepare and organize meeting documentation, briefing materials, presentations, participant lists and other supporting materials. Support documentation of meetings and programme activities, including preparation of meeting notes, attendance records and follow-up lists. Support the preparation and formatting of presentations, briefing packages, correspondence and other programme materials. Provide administrative support to  coordination, reporting and knowledge management : Compile and organize information from donors, partners and programme teams for reports, briefing notes, databases and other programme documentation. Support the collection and consolidation of inputs for periodic programme and donor reporting. Maintain and regularly update contact lists, activity trackers, reporting calendars and other programme management tools. Support the organization and filing of programme knowledge products, visibility materials, reports and other relevant documentation. Provide administrative support to documenting lessons learned, good practices and programme results. Support the organization of trainings, consultations and knowledge-sharing activities for partners and other stakeholders. Provide administrative support to stakeholder engagement and programme coordination: Support the organization and coordination of meetings and consultations with government institutions, civil society organizations, private sector actors, development partners and other stakeholders. Support correspondence, scheduling and administrative follow-up with partners and stakeholders. Maintain records of agreed follow-up actions and support tracking of their completion. Support the preparation and organization of background materials and documentation for stakeholder meetings and consultations. Other support: Provide other administrative, logistical and programme support within the scope of the assignment, as required for the effective implementation of UN Women’s Azerbaijan Bi-Annual Workplan 2026–2027. Consultant’s Workplace and Official Travel This is a office-based consultancy to be provided in Baku, Azerbaijan. Competencies : Core Values: Integrity; Professionalism; Respect for Diversity. Core Competencies: Awareness and Sensitivity Regarding Gender Issues; Accountability; Creative Problem Solving; Effective Communication; Inclusive Collaboration; Stakeholder Engagement; Leading by Example. Please visit  this link  for more information on UN Women’s Values and Competencies Framework:  Functional Competencies: Commitment to continuous improvement  Risk management Partnerships building  Resilience  Negotiation  Required Qualifications: Academic Background: Completion of secondary education is required. Bachelor’s degree in business administration or related fields is desirable. Relevant Work Experience: At least 7 years (or 4 years in case of Bachelor’s degree) of progressively responsible experience in administration, procurement, HR, or logistic support service is required ; Experience in working in a computer environment using multiple office software packages is required; Experience in the use of ERP systems, preferably Oracle Cloud, is desirable;  Experience in supporting a team is desirable. Languages: Fluency in Azerbaijani and English is required. Statements: In July 2010, the United Nations General Assembly created UN Women, the United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women. The creation of UN Women came about as part of the UN reform agenda, bringing together resources and mandates for greater impact. It merges and builds on the important work of four previously distinct parts of the UN system (DAW, OSAGI, INSTRAW and UNIFEM), which focused exclusively on gender equality and women's empowerment. Diversity and inclusion: At UN Women, we are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive environment of mutual respect. UN Women recruits, employs, trains, compensates, and promotes regardless of race, religion, color, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, ability, national origin, or any other basis covered by appropriate law. All employment is decided on the basis of qualifications, competence, integrity and organizational need. If you need any reasonable accommodation to support your participation in the recruitment and selection process, please include this information in your application. UN Women has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and UN Women, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination. All selected candidates will be expected to adhere to UN Women’s policies and procedures and the standards of conduct expected of UN Women personnel and will therefore undergo rigorous reference and background checks. (Background checks will include the verification of academic credential(s) and employment history. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional information to conduct a background check.) Note: Applicants must ensure that all sections of the application form, including the sections on education and employment history, are completed. If all sections are not completed the application may be disqualified from the recruitment and selection process . postings.text: Senior Multimedia and Communications Associate/Consultant | IOM - International Organization for Migration Skip to main content Senior Multimedia and Communications Associate/Consultant IOM - International Organization for Migration Congo DRC Both national and international UG - Ungraded level Speaks English, French, Spanish Application deadline: November 24, 2026 (6 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The Senior Multimedia and Communications Associate/Consultant at IOM will support the development and dissemination of multimedia and communications materials that highlight the organization's work in north-eastern DRC. This role involves visual storytelling through photography, videography, and graphic design, ensuring that all communications products align with IOM's branding and standards. The incumbent will collaborate with various teams to create engaging content, manage digital communications, and document program activities. The position requires a strong background in multimedia production and excellent organizational skills. Candidate Requirements: High school diploma with 6 years experience or Bachelor's degree with 4 years experience Experience in professional photography, videography, and multimedia content production Ability to produce high-quality photos and videos for communications Experience in graphic design and producing branded materials Proficiency in multimedia editing software like Adobe Creative Cloud Strong writing and editing skills for various content types Ability to coordinate field content collection Knowledge of digital communications and social media platforms Fluency in English; knowledge of French or Spanish is a plus Job Description Introduction Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.  IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move. IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at  IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration   Project Context and Scope ​Under the overall supervision of the Chief of Mission and the direct supervision of the Media & Communications Officer, the Senior Multimedia and Communications Associate will support the development, production and dissemination of high-quality multimedia and communications materials showcasing IOM's work in north-eastern DRC.  ​The incumbent will play a key role in visual storytelling, with particular emphasis on professional photography, videography, video editing, graphic design and digital content production. Working closely with programme teams, field offices and relevant partners, the incumbent will ensure that communications products are engaging, accurate, ethically produced and aligned with IOM's institutional branding, communications standards and donor visibility requirements.​    Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing Programme Support Unit  Responsibilities Tasks to be performed under this contract ​​Multimedia Production: Produce and edit high-quality photographs, videos and other multimedia content documenting IOM's activities and achievements, including interviews, human-interest stories, events, promotional videos and donor visibility materials, ensuring professional standards in filming, photography, editing and post-production. ​Content Development and Storytelling: Identify and develop compelling human-interest stories, success stories, beneficiary testimonials and other communications content in collaboration with programme teams and field offices. Draft and edit accompanying captions, articles, social media posts and other written materials. ​Graphic Design and Publications: Design and produce visually engaging communications and visibility materials, including infographics, factsheets, brochures, newsletters, presentations, banners, social media graphics and other digital or printed products, ensuring compliance with IOM's visual identity and donor branding requirements. ​Digital Communications: Support the management and regular updating of IOM DRC's website and social media platforms by preparing, adapting, publishing and scheduling multimedia content tailored to different audiences and communication channels, in coordination with relevant communications focal points. ​Field Documentation: Coordinate with programme managers and field teams to identify opportunities for documenting programme activities and results. Undertake field missions, including to remote or humanitarian locations when required and authorized, to collect audiovisual materials and develop communications products. ​Media and Event Support: Provide photography, videography, audiovisual and communications support for official visits, donor missions, workshops, campaigns, press events and other activities. Assist in preparing promotional materials, media packages and event-related communications products. ​Multimedia Asset Management: Help maintain an organized digital archive of photographs, videos, graphics and other communications assets, including appropriate file naming, metadata, captions, consent documentation, access controls and secure storage to facilitate future retrieval and use. ​Coordination and Collaboration: Liaise with IOM programme teams, field offices, implementing partners and other stakeholders to identify communications needs, coordinate content production and support consistent institutional messaging. ​Reporting: Prepare comprehensive and visually engaging Annual Communications and Visibility Reports for donors, showcasing key achievements, results, success stories, media coverage and communication activities.  ​Perform such other duties as may be assigned.​  Qualifications Required Qualifications and Experience Education ​​High school diploma with at least six years of relevant professional experience; or ​Bachelor's degree in Multimedia Production, Photography, Film and Video Production, Digital Media, Visual Communications, Journalism, Communications, Graphic Design or a related field from an accredited academic institution, with at least four years of relevant professional experience.​  Experience ​​Demonstrated experience in professional photography, videography, video editing and multimedia content production. ​Proven ability to independently produce high-quality photos, videos and digital content for institutional communications, social media and donor visibility. ​Experience developing human-interest stories, interviews, testimonials and other visual storytelling materials. ​Experience producing communications and donor visibility materials for EU-funded programmes, including familiarity with Global Gateway branding, is an advantage. ​Experience documenting community stabilization, border governance, protection or cross-border cooperation activities in eastern DRC is an advantage. ​Proficiency in professional photography and videography equipment and editing software, such as Adobe Creative Cloud, DaVinci Resolve or equivalent tools. ​Experience in graphic design and producing branded communications materials. ​Experience with humanitarian, development or international organizations, including field assignments, is an advantage. ​Knowledge of ethical storytelling, informed consent, data protection and donor visibility requirements is desirable. ​Experience working in the region and/or in an emergency setting an advantage; and, ​Experience in working in UN or other international organizations.​  Skills Excellent photography, videography and editing skills, including filming, lighting, sound recording and post-production. Proficiency in professional multimedia editing software, such as Adobe Creative Cloud or equivalent tools. Strong visual storytelling and graphic design skills, with the ability to produce engaging digital and print communications materials. Strong writing and editing skills, including for articles, captions and social media content. Ability to translate programme results and technical themes into accessible, accurate communications products for border communities, government counterparts and donors. Ability to coordinate field content collection across multiple territories and partners, while respecting security, protection and publication-clearance procedures. Good knowledge of digital communications, social media platforms and content requirements. Ability to independently plan, produce and deliver high-quality multimedia products within tight deadlines. Strong organizational, coordination and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively in multicultural teams.  Languages For this consultancy, English is the required language; IOM’s official languages are English, French, and Spanish.   Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments. Required Competencies IOM’s competency framework can be found at this  link . Competencies will be assessed during the selection process. Values  - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values: Inclusion and respect for diversity : Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion. Integrity and transparency : Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct. Professionalism : Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges. Courage : Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance. Empathy : Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated. Core Competencies  – behavioural indicators Teamwork : Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results. Delivering results : Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes. Managing and sharing knowledge : Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate. Accountability : Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work. Communication : Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way. Notes IOM covers Consultants against occupational accidents and illnesses under the Compensation Plan (CP), free of charge, for the duration of the consultancy. IOM does not provide evacuation or medical insurance for reasons related to non-occupational accidents and illnesses. Consultants are responsible for their own medical insurance for non-occupational accident or illness and will be required to provide written proof of such coverage before commencing work.  Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation. Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, accreditation, any residency or visa requirements, security clearances. postings.text: Quality Management System support – Consultant | Bioingred Tech S.A.S. | Antioquia BioCompetitiva | GGGI - Global Green Growth Institute Skip to main content Quality Management System support – Consultant | Bioingred Tech S.A.S. | Antioquia BioCompetitiva GGGI - Global Green Growth Institute Antioquia, Itagüí Consultancy Level 3 level Speaks English, Spanish Application deadline: November 23, 2026 (5 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool Bioingred Tech S.A.S. is seeking a consultant to provide specialized technical support for the implementation of a Quality and Food Safety Management System aligned with Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP). The consultant will work closely with the company to ensure readiness for sanitary authorization and GMP certification processes. Key responsibilities include developing a work plan, conducting regulatory diagnostics, aligning documentation, and providing training to personnel. The consultancy is part of the Antioquia BioCompetitiva Project aimed at enhancing the bioeconomy in the region. Candidate Requirements: Colombian citizen or valid work permit holder Professional degree in relevant fields (e.g., Industrial Microbiology, Chemical Engineering) Postgraduate degree in Integral Process Management or related fields Minimum five years of experience in Good Manufacturing Practices and food safety management systems Experience with INVIMA compliance-readiness processes (desirable) Strong analytical, writing, and presentation skills Consultancy Level: 3  Consultancy Type: Deliverable Contract Value :   2.100 USD Contract Duration: 30/11/2026 ~ 23/03/2027 Application Deadline:   23/11/2026 10 PM (KST) Project Background GGGI works in partnership with countries around the world to strengthen their capacity and advance green growth policies and investments that can positively impact the lives of millions of people. The organization collaborates with national governments, multilateral institutions, public agencies, and the private sector to support the development of economies that are robust, resource-efficient, low-carbon, and resilient to climate change. GGGI implements a diverse portfolio of programs across developing countries. Through these in-country initiatives, complemented by global products and services, the organization delivers results through an integrated approach that combines evidence-based policy planning, technical assistance, and investment facilitation, aligned with national development priorities. GGGI also promotes knowledge generation and management activities that strengthen the theoretical and empirical foundations of green growth, provide practical guidance for policymakers, and help create enabling conditions for both public and private green investments. In Colombia, GGGI has been working closely with the national government since 2014 to advance green growth policies and investments. The organization has established strategic partnerships with institutions such as the Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development, the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development, the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit, and the National Planning Department (DNP), among others. Within the framework of the UK PACT (Partnering for Accelerated Climate Transitions) Bio Rural Project (2024–2027), the Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI), the Government of Antioquia, and the Caja de Compensación Familiar de Antioquia – COMFAMA signed a Special Cooperation Agreement to implement the initiative "Antioquia BioCompetitiva." The project seeks to accelerate the scaling of innovative bioeconomy solutions in the Department of Antioquia through two strategic components: (I) promoting knowledge transfer and capacity-building processes, with a focus on circular bioeconomy and the internationalization of bioproducts; and (II) strengthening productive, technological, and commercial capacities within the department through an integrated value-chain development approach. Under the second component, three calls for proposals will be implemented to accelerate the development of the bioeconomy ecosystem while strengthening strategic value chains in the department. These calls include: Bioeconomy acceleration support for microenterprises affiliated with COMFAMA. Investment scaling support for four companies linked to bioeconomy value chains. MAPBIO Antioquia Edition. Through the Investment scaling support call, four companies were selected to receive specialized acceleration support based on the innovation potential, environmental impact, and market opportunities of their bio-based products: Company Bioproduct Sector Product Category Location Agroexport Hass S.A. Agricultural Agricultural bio-inputs Copacabana Bioingred Tech S.A.S. requires the structuring and implementation of a Quality and Food Safety Management System, aligned with the requirements of the National Food and Drug Surveillance Institute (INVIMA), Resolution 2674 of 2013 on Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP), Decree 3075 of 1997, Resolution 2115 of 2007 (drinking water quality), the Codex Alimentarius guidelines, and the requirements of the Itagüí Health Secretariat, so that the plant is sanitarily authorized and prepared for its GMP certification process. Objectives of the assignment The objective of this consultancy is to is to provide specialized technical support the articulation, documentation alignment, and monitoring  the phased implementation of the Quality and Food Safety Management System based on Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) of Bioingred Tech S.A.S., under the Antioquia BioCompetitiva Project, providing technical guidance and recommendations to support the company's readiness for its sanitary authorization and GMP certification processes before INVIMA and the Itagüí Health Secretariat. Deliverables and payment schedule Under the overall supervision of the GGGI Colombia team, and in direct coordination with the beneficiary company, Bioingred Tech S.A.S., the Consultant will and provide specialized technical input for the alignment of the plant's Quality and Food Safety Management System, consolidated for monitoring and payment purposes into three (3) deliverable packages. The assignment includes the following activities: 1. Work plan and methodology: A detailed work plan incorporating the consultancy coordination, implementation-support and progress-monitoring schedule, information requirements, and data collection processes for Bioingred Tech S.A.S. This deliverable must include the initial diagnostic scope of the company's regulatory situation, together with the stakeholder coordination arrangements with the company. 2. Quality and Food Safety Management System (GMP) – Bioingred Tech S.A.S. Support the alignment and monitor the phased implementation of the plant's Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) system, under the supervision of the GGGI Contract Supervisor and in direct coordination with the beneficiary company, through six (6) operational phases: Provide technical inputs for the regulatory diagnostic and planing phase, identifying gaps against Resolution 2674 of 2013 for review. A review of the corresponding work/implementation plan, and of the sanitary layout and risk matrix. A documentation alignment and GMP implementation phase, covering the programs, procedures, and records required under Resolution 2674 of 2013 (facilities, personnel, sanitation, raw materials, manufacturing, packaging and distribution, quality assurance, traceability, and corrective action plans), as specifically listed in the approved work plan. Coordination of training and capacity-transfer phase for Bioingred's personnel on the GMP documentation and records. An implementation-support and progress-monitoring phase, providing technical follow-up, identifying implementation issues, and recommending remedial actions on the roll-out of the documented procedures on the plant floor for the company's consideration. An internal readiness review phase, comprising an on-site review, classification of findings, recommendations, and a corrective action plan for implementation by the company. 3. Final report : consolidated closing report for Bioingred Tech S.A.S., including training evidence, implementation coordination records, and the internal readiness review report with identified findings, recommendations, and a corrective action plan for implementation by the company. Out of scope The following activities are not part of the scope of this consultancy for Bioingred Tech S.A.S., unless separately assessed, quoted, and expressly approved by COMFAMA/GGGI: Execution of civil works, facility upgrades, or modifications to the plant's infrastructure. Supply, purchase, or installation of equipment, utensils, measuring instruments, or furniture. Development of product formulations. Laboratory testing (physicochemical, microbiological, or other analytical services). Management, filing, or processing of applications before health authorities (INVIMA or others), as well as payment of fees, licenses, or certifications. The certification process before the certifying body and support during the external certification audit. Attendance and support during official inspection, surveillance, and control visits, or client audits, unless contracted as an additional scope. Development or implementation of management systems other than GMP (for example, HACCP, ISO 9001, ISO 22000, or FSSC 22000), unless expressly agreed as part of the project. Ongoing operational activities of the company (routine completion of records, daily execution of cleaning and disinfection programs, pest control). Guarantee of registration, authorization, certification, or regulatory approval. For the sake of clarity, the consultant is not responsible for the outcome of the regulatory process, as approvals from INVIMA, the Itagüí Health Secretariat, or any other sanitary authority or certification body depend entirely on factors beyond the consultant's control. D

postings.text: Avis à Manifestation d’Intérêt (Services Consultants) AMI : N°    012 /2026/ADET/FP2E/CP/SPM/SD du 16/11/2026   Recrutement d’un Consultant individuel pour la réalisation de l’étude sur l'implication du secteur privé dans la nutrition au Bénin La présente sollicitation de manifestation d’intérêt fait suite au plan de passation des marchés publié sur le STEP en août 2026. Dans le cadre de ses missions de coordination des interventions en matière d’alimentation et de nutrition au Bénin, l’Agence nationale de l’Alimentation et de la Nutrition (ANAN) a été désignée par le Gouvernement du Bénin comme entité de mise en œuvre du programme multisectoriel ALAFIA I : Nourrir le Bénin pour l’avenir, avec l’appui financier de la Banque mondiale et du Mécanisme de financement mondial (Global Financing Facility en anglais, GFF). Ainsi, pour la concrétisation de ce Programme, l’ANAN envisage d’utiliser une partie du montant de cet appui financier pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat relatif au recrutement d’un consultant individuel pour la réalisation de l’étude sur l’implication du secteur privé dans la nutrition au Bénin . Le processus de recrutement est conduit par le Projet de Formation Professionnelle pour l’Emploi au Bénin (FP2E) sous la tutelle de l'Agence de Développement de l’Enseignement Technique (ADET), chargé de la préparation du programme ALAFIA I, au profit de l’ANAN. La mission a pour objectif général d’analyser la situation actuelle du partenariat public-privé en nutrition au Bénin et de proposer des stratégies concrètes pour renforcer l’implication du secteur privé. À cet effet, le Consultant sera chargé des tâches ci-après : revue documentaire : analyse des politiques, stratégies et cadres réglementaires liés à la nutrition et au secteur privé, ainsi que des expériences nationales et internationales pertinentes de partenariat public-privé en nutrition ; cartographie des acteurs : identification et catégorisation des acteurs du secteur privé (entreprises agricoles, entreprises de transformation agroalimentaire, distributeurs, ONG, etc.) et analyse de leur niveau d’implication dans la nutrition ; analyse des partenariats existants : identification des initiatives de partenariat public-privé en nutrition (fortification, alimentation scolaire, prévention et traitement de la malnutrition, chaînes de valeur, etc.) et évaluation de leur performance, de leur durabilité et de leur impact ; analyse des contraintes et opportunités : identification des obstacles à l’engagement du secteur privé (réglementaires, financiers, techniques, etc.) et mise en évidence des opportunités de collaboration ; consultation des parties prenantes : organisation d’entretiens et/ou de focus groups avec les acteurs publics et privés, et recueil de leurs perceptions et recommandations ; proposition de mécanismes de renforcement : élaboration d’un cadre stratégique de partenariat public-privé en nutrition, proposition d’actions d’incitation du secteur privé et identification de modèles de collaboration adaptés au contexte béninois. La durée de la mission est de 45 jours ouvrables , à compter de la date mentionnée dans l’ordre de service de démarrage. Le Coordonnateur  du FP2E, représentant l’Autorité contractante, invite les Consultants individuels éligibles à manifester leur intérêt pour la fourniture des services décrits ci-dessus. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir les informations indiquant qu’ils sont qualifiés pour exécuter lesdites prestations (curriculum vitae faisant ressortir les diplômes, les expériences acquises, les missions similaires réalisées, les employeurs, les périodes de réalisation avec précision de la durée, etc.) ainsi que les preuves de réalisation des missions similaires. Le dossier de manifestation d’intérêt comprend : une lettre de manifestation d’intérêt datée et signée, précisant la mission ; un curriculum vitae (CV) détaillé, daté et signé ; le tableau récapitulatif des expériences dans le domaine ; les pièces justificatives des expériences déclarées : attestations ou certificats de travail, attestations de bonne fin d’exécution ou de service fait, accompagnés des extraits des contrats correspondants (trois premières pages et page de signature) ; les copies des diplômes ou attestations de diplômes exigés dans le présent avis. Nota bene : Seules les expériences appuyées par les moyens de preuve indiqués au point 11 seront prises en compte lors de l’évaluation. Un Consultant individuel sera sélectionné conformément à la méthode de « Sélection de Consultants individuels » décrite à la Section VII (paragraphes 7.34 et suivants) du Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) de la Banque mondiale, édition de juillet 2016, révisée en novembre 2017, août 2018, novembre 2020, février 2025 et septembre 2025 (ci-après « le Règlement de Passation des Marchés »). À l’issue de l’évaluation comparative des qualifications et de l’expérience des candidats, effectuée sur la base de la grille figurant au point 11, seul le Consultant classé premier sera invité à soumettre une proposition technique et financière en vue de la négociation du contrat. Les manifestations d’intérêt, rédigées en langue française, doivent parvenir au plus tard le __02___/____12___/ 2026 à 10 heures précises (heure de Cotonou, GMT+1), suivant l’une des modalités ci-après : dépôt physique , sous pli fermé, en deux (02) exemplaires (un original et une copie) accompagnés d’une version électronique en fichier unique sur clé USB, au Secrétariat de l’Agence de Développement de l’Enseignement Technique (ADET), sis à Cotonou, Immeuble TWECY MELO 28, Rue du commerce 5.123, Tél : +229 01 53 22 22 22 / 01 21 60 43 47 ; transmission par voie électronique , en fichier unique, aux adresses suivantes : secretariat_adet@adet.bj avec copie obligatoire à spm.fp2e@adet.bj. Le pli ou l’objet du courriel doit porter la mention « Recrutement d’un consultant (individuel) pour la réalisation de l’étude sur l’implication du secteur privé dans la nutrition au Bénin ». Les plis seront ouverts le même jour, soit le _02__/___12_/ 2026 à 10 heures 30 minutes (heure de Cotonou, GMT+1), à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessus, en présence des Consultants qui souhaitent y assister. Les Consultants intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations complémentaires au Secrétariat de l’ADET, à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessus, tous les jours ouvrables de 08 heures à 12 heures 30 minutes et de 14 heures à 17 heures 30 minutes. Les Termes de référence de la mission peuvent être consultés sur le site web de l’ADET (https://www.adet.bj), retirés au Secrétariat de l’ADET ou obtenus sur demande adressée par voie électronique à secretariat_adet@adet.bj avec copie obligatoire à spm.fp2e@adet.bj.   L’évaluation des manifestations d’intérêt se fera sur la base des critères et de la notation ci-après :   Critères d’évaluation Note pour le critère Sous-critères d’évaluation et note Moyens de Preuve à fournir par le candidat Diplôme universitaire (Bac+5 minimum) en nutrition, santé publique, économie, développement ou domaine connexe 15 Diplôme universitaire de niveau Bac+5 au moins en nutrition, santé publique, économie, développement ou domaine connexe = 15 points Diplôme de niveau inférieur à Bac+5 = 00 point Copie du diplôme ou de l’attestation de diplôme   Expérience générale d’au moins sept (07) ans dans les domaines de la nutrition, des systèmes alimentaires ou du développement 20 Moins de 07 ans d’expérience = 00 point 07 ans d’expérience = 15 points Plus de 07 ans d’expérience = 15 points + 01 point par année supplémentaire, dans la limite de 05 points Curriculum vitae daté et signé. Copies légalisées des attestations de travail, des attestations de bonne fin d’exécution ou de service fait, précisant le client, l’objet, la période et appuyées des trois premières pages ainsi que la page de signature des contrats correspondants. Expérience avérée dans la mise en œuvre de partenariats public-privé en nutrition, incluant la fortification des aliments, l’alimentation scolaire ou la mobilisation des entreprises locales dans les chaînes de valeur alimentaires 45 15 points par mission prouvée , dans la limite de trois (03) missions, soit 45 points au maximum Copies légalisées des attestations de bonne fin d’exécution ou de service fait Expérience en analyse institutionnelle et en élaboration de stratégies 15 A raison de 5 points/mission prouvée Bonne connaissance du contexte béninois ou ouest-africain 05 5 points/mission   TOTAL 100     En cas d’égalité de score, le consultant qui aura réalisé plus des missions avérées dans la « mise en œuvre de partenariats public-privé en nutrition, incluant la fortification des aliments, l’alimentation scolaire ou la mobilisation des entreprises locales dans les chaînes de valeur alimentaires » sera privilégié. Tous les documents doivent être en français ou traduit en français y compris les diplômes, attestation de bonne fin d’exécution, curricula vitae…… L’autorité contractante se réserve le droit de ne pas donner suite à cette procédure.                                                                    &

postings.text: Ministry of Ecology, Sustainable Development, and Northern Region Development The Montenegro Waste Sector Improvement Project (MWSIP) Request for Expressions of Interest National Municipal Waste Composition Study for Montenegro with a Chapter 33 Plastic Own Resource Module Consulting Services: CQS Loan No. P510187- ME Reference No. MNE-WMRP-9949-ME-CS-CQS-26-1.1.1  November 17, 2026 The Government of Montenegro (the Recipient) has received financing from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development – ‘’World Bank’’ toward the costs for implementation of ‘ Waste Management Reform Project (WMRP), (the Project)’’. The Ministry of Ecology, Sustainable Development, and Northern Region Development - MESDNRD (the Client) as the lead implementing agency for the project, intends to apply part of these proceeds to the payments for Consulting services. The Waste Management Reform Project (WMRP ) aims to enhance the Country’s waste management capacity and sector performance, supporting Montenegro’s progress toward EU accession. The objective of the WMRP project adopts an integrated approach through three main components (i) strengthen institutional capacity for solid waste management, (ii) improve the performance of solid waste services in selected municipalities, and (iii) enhance environmental conditions at targeted waste disposal site. The Ministry of Ecology, Sustainable Development, and Northern Region Development (MESDNRD) (the “Client”) is seeking to engage an experienced and qualified Consultancy firm (the “Consultant”) to support of the Montenegro Waste Management Reform Project (the “Project”). The objective of this particular assignment is to establish a statistically robust, nationally representative and seasonally differentiated baseline on the quantity and composition of municipal waste generated in Montenegro, including a technically defensible basis for estimating plastic packaging waste contained in municipal waste and for supporting future Chapter 33 reporting and projections while the Scope of services and deliverables are clearly defined within the ToR. The (MESDNRD) through the Technical Service Unit (TSU) now invites eligible Consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consult-firm (Legal entity) should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services in subject, with demonstrated experience in waste composition studies, statistical sampling and analysis, and waste management data assessment. The Consultant will work closely with relevant stakeholders ensuring compliance with Montenegro’s relevant policies, EU regulations, and international best practices. * It is anticipated that the Consultant should complete the work over a maximum duration of 10 months. The qualification and evaluation criteria are: The Consultant (Firm) should meet the following qualification criteria: 1. General experience: At least five (5) years of professional experience in waste management studies, waste characterization, waste data analysis or related environmental consulting services ---------------------------15. 2. Relevant assignment experience: Successful completion of at least two (2) comparable assignments within the last seven (7) years involving municipal waste composition analysis, waste characterization studies or statistically representative waste sampling and analysis –--------------------------------------------------------- 40.   3. Statistical and methodological capacity: Demonstrated experience in designing and implementing statistically representative sampling methodologies, including data processing, statistical analysis and preparation of analytical reports ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------20. 4.. Waste packaging and EU reporting experience: Demonstrated experience in at least one assignment involving packaging waste data, recycling statistics, Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) systems or EU waste reporting requirements -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------15. 5. Field implementation capacity: Demonstrated experience in organizing and supervising field sampling campaigns, waste sorting operations and associated quality assurance and quality control procedures--- -10. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Total Scores 100 Experience in EU Member States, EU candidate countries or Western Balkan countries shall be considered an advantage but shall not constitute a mandatory eligibility requirement. Documented experience in Chapter 33 plastic own resource data or EU plastic-packaging waste calculation and reporting, and in applying SWA-Tool or an equivalent statistically justified waste composition methodology, shall also be considered an advantage. The Consultant may demonstrate compliance with the above requirements through the combined experience of the members of a joint venture, where applicable It is expected that the interested Consultant’s company within the submitted ‘’EoI’’ shall prepare and present a table listing (reference list) which will provide the following information: Contracting authority/client data and contact information to whom the consultancy service was performed, (contract-project detailed description, contract value for performed services and contract implementation period). (name, e-mail, phone numbers for verification purposes).  The Consultant firm may also submit other documents and which are not listed above in order to justify general qualifications and qualifications relevant to the assignment it considers relevant, such us indicative list of the key staff/key personnel (team) that is generally available for this kind of work. *CVs or biodata for Key Expert’s- (staff) are not required and will not be evaluated at this stage . Consultants may associate to enhance their qualifications. The associations should clearly indicate the form of the association (Joint-venture, Consortium, sub-consultancy; member in charge; other member/s and or sub- consultants). Joint ventures should submit letter/confirmation, indicating their intent to form a joint venture if awarded the contract and shall provide the above-mentioned information for each member of the joint venture. *Consultant may only submit one expression of interest. postings.text: Head of Administration - Contract Agent FGIII - EU DELEGATION TO SWITZERLAND - Job No 529955 | EEAS - European External Action Service Skip to main content Head of Administration - Contract Agent FGIII - EU DELEGATION TO SWITZERLAND - Job No 529955 EEAS - European External Action Service Bern Both national and international FG III, Function Group 3, Contract Agent level Speaks English, French Application deadline: December 01, 2026 (13 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The European External Action Service (EEAS) is seeking a Head of Administration for its Delegation in Bern, Switzerland. This contract agent position involves overseeing the day-to-day operations of the Delegation under the authority of the Head of Delegation. Candidates must meet specific eligibility criteria, including passing the EPSO CAST exam and possessing relevant educational qualifications and professional experience. The role requires strong organizational skills, experience in administrative functions, and the ability to work in a multicultural environment. Candidate Requirements: Passed EPSO CAST in FG III or registered in EPSO Permanent CAST Post-secondary education or secondary education with 3 years of experience Fluency in English and French EU national with full citizenship rights Experience in EU Delegation administration Team management experience Knowledge of budget management and tender procedures Computer literacy and familiarity with EU IT tools Contract type: Contract Agent Deadline for applications is 01/12/2026  at 12.00 hours (midday, Brussels time) . WE ARE The European External Action Service (EEAS) is the European Union’s diplomatic service. Since 2011, the EEAS carries out the EU’s Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP) to promote peace, prosperity, security, and the interests of the EU across the globe. It brings together European civil servants, diplomats from EU Member States, national experts and local staff worldwide. The EEAS supports the High Representative in the exercise of her mandate to steer the Union’s CFSP, including the Common Security and Defence Policy (CSDP), to represent the EU on issues relating to the CFSP and to chair the Foreign Affairs Council. It also supports her as Vice-President of the Commission with regard to her responsibilities within the Commission, including the coordination of other aspects of the EU’s external action. The EEAS works in close cooperation with the EU Member States, the General Secretariat of the Council, the services of the Commission and the Secretariat General of the European Parliament. The EEAS Headquarters are in Brussels. It is also responsible for the management of the network of 145 Union Delegations and Offices worldwide. These Diplomatic Representations play a vital role in representing the EU in the country where they are based, in promoting the values and interests of the EU, and in building networks and partnerships. They are responsible for all policy areas of the relationship between the EU and the host country/organisation. WE PROPOSE The position of Head of Administration, contract agent FGIII as per article 3a of the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants of the European Union (hereafter, the “CEOS”). PLACE OF EMPLOYMENT City, COUNTRY:                                SWITZERLAND, Bern LCA:                                                        0 % POST AVAILABLE:                            Immediately LEGAL BASIS The vacancy is to be filled in accordance with the conditions foreseen in the relevant provisions of the CEOS, in particular Article 82 thereof.  Subject to having passed the CAST exam, the successful candidate will be offered a contract agent position (Function Group III), as per Article 3a of the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants of the European Union (CEOS), on the basis of a contract with an initial duration of 3 years. This contract may be renewed not more than once for a fixed period of not more than 5 years. Any further renewal shall be for an indefinite period. WE LOOK FOR The Head of Administration will be responsible, under the authority of the Head of Delegation (HoD), for the day-to-day running of the Delegation. Eligibility criteria According to the conditions set out in Article 82 of the CEOS and in Article 2 of the  Commission Decision C(2017) 6760 final , which is applicable to the EEAS by virtue of the  Decision ADMIN(2018) 4 of the High Representative , in order to be eligible for this post of contract agent FG III, candidates must: have passed a valid EPSO CAST in FG III; or be registered in the EPSO Permanent CAST for FG III ( https://epso.europa.eu/en/job-opportunities/open-for-application ). In the latter case, while the registration will render the candidate eligible for the selection procedure, the recruitment of a candidate on this vacant post will be subject to his/her successfully passing the CAST exam; meet the minimum qualifications for engagement as contract agent FG III: (i) Have a level of post-secondary education attested by a diploma; or  (ii) a level of secondary education attested by a diploma giving access to post-secondary education, and appropriate professional experience of at least three years; or  (iii) in exceptional circumstances and where justified in the interest of the service, professional training or professional experience of an equivalent level (related to the nature of the tasks and qualifications indicated in the Job Description). have the capacity to work in languages of CFSP and external relations (English and French) necessary for the performance of their duties; be a national of one of the Member States of the EU and enjoy full rights as a citizen . Additional eligibility criteria in case of an internal call for expression of interest: Be an EEAS contract agent in the function group concerned by the call for expression of interest; AND Having been recruited under Article 3b of the CEOS and assigned to the EEAS Headquarters for no less than 3 years; OR  Having been recruited under Article 3a of the CEOS and temporarily assigned to the EEAS Headquarters for at least 2 years. Selection criteria Proven pertinent experience in one or several of the following areas: -      working in the administrative section of an EU Delegation; -      handling of staff matters, ideally as team leader; -      tender procedures, preparation of contracts; -      management of an annual operating budget, including preparation, adjustment and monitoring its execution; including financial commitments and payments  -      follow-up, adjustment and verification of the execution of the authorised budget -      knowledge of SUMMA, ARES, e-DAS, e-Del-HRM, e-EPC, Security Portal, IMMOGEST, MIPS, SYSPER (either as a user or having completed relevant training modules). -      experience in preparing high-level missions from HQ logistically, protocol-wise and security-wise; -      experience in Delegation security management (support to the DSC and dealing with day-to-day security matters). Successful experience in team management and/or equivalent professional experience                 Proven experience and/or training in team management. General skills and competencies Candidates should demonstrate: -      a sense of initiative, very good organisational skills and a service minded attitude; -      a capacity to assure quality, speed and accuracy in performing complex tasks in a multicultural environment; -      a proven experience and/or training in oral and written communication; -      computer literacy, and an ability to work with Windows applications. Furthermore Experience in external relations;  experience in handling secure communications and classified information; knowledge of IT tools used in EU institutions (ARES, MIPS, Sysper2, etc.); experience of working in a team in multi-disciplinary and multi-cultural environment; experience in managing large infrastructure projects;  previous experience in EU institutions and/or EU Delegations, notably from the administrative section; fluency in German or French; and strong command of the other language  will be considered as assets. Working languages Capacity to work in languages of the CFSP and external relations necessary for the performance of their duties (EN and FR). POSTING POLICY EEAS career development policy places the need for staff to develop a mix of competences at its core, e.g. working in various fields of expertise and responsibilities in the course of a person's career, including postings at Headquarters and Delegations.  Contract staff in Delegations is usually posted for 2, 3, 4 or 6 years in a given EU Delegation. Call for interest to apply for postponement or early mobility will be launched annually prior to the publication of the mobility exercise. Staff are reminded that extension and early mobility are not a right. Contract staff assigned to a post where the living conditions allowance (LCA) determined in accordance with Article 10 of Annex X to the Staff Regulations of Officials of the EU (SR) is 30% or 35% may participate in the mobility exercise after 4 years . Contract staff assigned to a post where the LCA is 40% may participate in the mobility exercise after 3 years . Contract staff assigned to a non-family post may participate in the mobility exercise after 2 years .  For candidates currently posted in compound-confined, non-family posting, please refer to Article 6, point 2(g) of the Decision ADMIN(2021) 221. Within the mobility exercise, contract staff may be temporarily assigned to the EEAS Headquarters in Brussels; such assignment shall remain exceptional and depends on the availability of posts. The assignment shall be for no less than two years, unless a derogation is granted by the Head of the Division RM.BHR.3 ‘Selection and Recruitment’ in the interest of the service. The assignment shall be for no more than four years, in accordance with Article 118 of the CEOS and Article 3 of Annex X to the SR. The member of contract staff temporarily assigned to the EEAS Headquarters shall be included in the mobility exercise in time to be reassigned to a Union Delegation before he/she reaches the maximum period of 4 years. Candidates currently in the EEAS Headquarters are expected to have served at least three years in the Headquarters by the expected time of posting in Delegation. Derogation to this rule may only be granted by the competent Authority Authorised to Conclude Contracts of Employment (AACC) in the interest of the service. External candidates may also apply to any vacancy position published for posts in Delegations. It is in the interest of the service to ensure that staff members in Delegations are able to complete full postings before reaching the age of retirement. Before taking any final decisions on nominations, the competent AACC will ensure on a case-by-case basis, in accordance with the SR and CEOS, that the successful candidates will indeed be able to complete the relevant full posting for the post for which they are selected. As stated in Article 6(2)(a) of the Decision ADMIN(2020) 35, applications from candidates not fulfilling this requirement will be examined by the AACC for exceptional and justified reasons and in the interest of the service. CONDITIONS OF RECRUITMENT AND EMPLOYMENT CONFLICT OF INTEREST AND SECURITY RISKS As a matter of policy, applications of individuals who have the dual nationality of the host country or whose family member has the nationality of the host country will be considered eligible for a posting in that host country only as a positive result of a case-by-case assessment. In that regard, the EEAS examines if there could be a conflict of interest and a risk of a possible refusal by the host country to grant diplomatic immunity to the staff member and or his/her partner and/or family, as well as possible security risks.
