postings.title: UN Women National Consultant – Country Gender Equality Profile for Pakistan (CGEP), Islamabad, Pakistan UN WOMEN - United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women Islamabad Senior
postings.text: UN Women National Consultant – Country Gender Equality Profile for Pakistan (CGEP), Islamabad, Pakistan | UN WOMEN - United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women Skip to main content UN Women National Consultant – Country Gender Equality Profile for Pakistan (CGEP), Islamabad, Pakistan UN WOMEN - United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women Islamabad National Senior level Speaks Punjabi, English, Sindhi, Urdu Application deadline: November 25, 2026 (7 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool UN Women is seeking a National Consultant to develop a comprehensive Country Gender Equality Profile (CGEP) for Pakistan. The consultant will be responsible for research, evidence generation, stakeholder consultations, and drafting the CGEP, ensuring alignment with various gender equality frameworks. This role involves engaging with multiple stakeholders, conducting qualitative and quantitative analyses, and delivering evidence-based recommendations. The consultancy is based in Islamabad and requires travel to provinces for consultations. Candidate Requirements: Master's degree in relevant field 7+ years of experience in qualitative and quantitative research Experience in gender analysis and drafting reports Knowledge of global gender equality frameworks Experience in gender statistical analysis Familiarity with Pakistan's national data systems Experience facilitating multi-stakeholder consultations Fluency in Urdu and English Knowledge of regional languages is an asset Background and Context The United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women (UN Women) is the UN entity dedicated to gender equality and the empowerment of women. In Pakistan, UN Women and UNFPA co-chair the UN Gender Theme Group (GTG), the inter-agency coordination mechanism on Gender Equality and Women’s Empowerment (GEWE) under the UN Country Team (UNCT). As part of ongoing efforts to strengthen gender equality accountability, the UN in Pakistan is developing a Country Gender Equality Profile (CGEP), a comprehensive, intersectional and evidence-based analysis of the state of GEWE in Pakistan. The CGEP is a formal deliverable under the GTG Workplan 2026 and responds to the global Gender Equality Acceleration Plan (GEAP). Its development will take into consideration the GEAP, the UNCT Gender Strategy for Pakistan 2025–2027, the UNCT-SWAP Gender Equality Scorecard and other relevant guidance and tools. It will serve as a primary evidence base for the Country Analysis (CA) and planning under the UNSDCF, including its extension to 2029. The CGEP is a UNCT product, developed and owned collectively by all UN agencies, with the GTG co-chairs (UN Women and UNFPA) providing technical leadership in partnership with the Ministry of Human Rights (MoHR). This consultancy is funded by UN Women. The CGEP Consultant will have overall responsibility for the research, evidence generation, stakeholder consultations, analysis, drafting, validation, fact-checking and finalization required for the development of the CGEP. This includes undertaking and/or coordinating the literature and desk review, collection and analysis of primary and secondary data, national and provincial consultations, key informant interviews (KIIs), focus group discussions (FGDs), translation of relevant consultation inputs, and preparation of analytical and drafting inputs for the final CGEP. Scope of the CGEP:                                                                                                                                        The CGEP will cover the national level (Federal/ICT) and all four provinces (Punjab, Sindh, KP, Balochistan) as well as AJK and Gilgit-Baltistan. Terminology and arrangements for stakeholder engagement in AJK and GB will be agreed during inception. It will include provincial and national stakeholder consultations, comprehensive gender analysis aligned with the 12 critical areas of the Beijing Platform for Action (BPfA), The analysis and recommendations will take into consideration the global GEAP, the UNCT Gender Strategy for Pakistan 2025–2027, the UNSDCF, the UNCT-SWAP Gender Equality Scorecard and other relevant frameworks and tools. The process will include a comprehensive literature and desk review, review and analysis of national and sub-national quantitative and qualitative data, stakeholder mapping, KIIs, FGDs and multi-stakeholder consultations at national and provincial levels, including engagement with government, civil society, women’s rights organizations, organisations of persons with disabilities (OPDs), academia, development partners, UN entities and other relevant stakeholders, as identified through the approved methodology. The CGEP Consultant will actively engage with the UN Gender Theme Group (GTG), the Programme Management Team (PMT), the CGEP Task Team and other relevant inter-agency groups, as well as the Ministry of Human Rights, throughout the CGEP development process. This includes presenting the Inception Report and draft findings to relevant UN coordination structures, incorporating inter-agency feedback, and facilitating consultations with relevant stakeholders at national and provincial levels. The primary objective of this consultancy is to deliver a comprehensive Country Gender Equality Profile (CGEP) for Pakistan, including the underlying research, evidence collection, stakeholder consultations, qualitative and quantitative analysis, drafting, support to validation, and finalization, in line with UN Women’s corporate CGEP guidance and the UNSDCF. The CGEP will provide evidence-based findings and recommendations to inform gender-transformative programming, GEWE financing discussions and UNCT gender equality accountability, taking into consideration the global GEAP and the UNCT Gender Strategy for Pakistan 2025–2027. The assignment comprises 40 working days distributed across the contract period, including time for revisions. The Inception Report will establish an agreed review and clearance schedule, identifying submission dates, reviewer responsibilities and deadlines for consolidated feedback. The GTG Secretariat will coordinate feedback from the relevant national, inter-agency and regional reviewers. Final submission will incorporate agreed comments received within this schedule. Any changes to contractual deadlines or the level of effort will require approval through the applicable UN Women contract amendment procedures.  Document Structure (indicative): a profile with no more than 30 pages Executive Summary (2 pp.) Introduction and Methodology (2-3 pp.)  Pakistan Country Context (2-3 pp.) Legal and Policy Framework incl. CEDAW status (3 pp.) Findings by BPfA critical areas / SP Impact Areas (11-13 pp.)  Partnerships and Financing for GEWE (2 pp.) Recommendations and GEAP linkages (3-4 pp.)  Annexes Guiding Principles: The CGEP must be grounded in international norms and standards (2030 Agenda, CEDAW, BPfA, UNSCR 1325), apply an intersectional and LNOB lens, ensure national ownership through active engagement of government and non-governmental counterparts, and apply a do-no-harm approach throughout. United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women Description of Responsibilities/ Scope of Work Within the assignment, the Consultant will have overall responsibility for undertaking and/or coordinating all research, evidence-generation, consultation, analytical and drafting functions required for the development and finalization of the CGEP. The Consultant shall ensure that all activities identified in the approved Inception Report are completed with the required methodological and quality standards and within the agreed timeline. The Consultant’s responsibilities shall include, but not be limited to: undertaking a comprehensive literature and desk review of existing gender data, research, policy documents, analytical reports, evaluations and other relevant sources at national and sub-national levels, including the UNCT Gender Strategy for Pakistan 2025–2027, and reflecting its relevant priorities and commitments in the analysis and recommendations; identifying, assessing, validating and analyzing relevant quantitative and qualitative data sources, including official statistics, administrative data, household and specialized surveys, Census data and relevant UN and other authoritative sources; developing and administering KII, FGD and multi-stakeholder consultation tools in accordance with the approved methodology; planning, conducting, coordinating and documenting national and provincial consultations, KIIs, FGDs and stakeholder engagements across Federal/ICT, Punjab, Sindh, KP, Balochistan, AJK and Gilgit-Baltistan, as agreed in the approved Inception Report; ensuring meaningful and appropriately inclusive engagement with relevant government institutions, civil society, women’s rights organizations, OPDs, academia, development partners, UN entities and other relevant stakeholders; translating relevant consultation inputs, notes, transcripts and substantive stakeholder contributions from Urdu and relevant regional languages into English; conducting qualitative and quantitative analysis of primary and secondary data and consultation findings; drafting and/or overseeing the drafting of assigned sections of the CGEP and ensuring analytical coherence across all sections; preparing consultation materials, presentations, briefing materials, documentation of meetings and consultation findings, and maintaining a record of substantive feedback received; undertaking fact-checking, editing and internal quality checks; supporting the independent peer-review process coordinated by UN Women and the GTG co-chairs; and addressing review comments to ensure the accuracy, consistency and traceability of evidence presented in the CGEP; incorporating feedback from the CGEP Task Team, GTG, PMT, UNCT, government and external stakeholders into successive drafts and the final validated CGEP. Where the Consultant proposes to engage or utilize research, data, translation, analytical or other technical support for any component of the assignment, such support shall be managed and quality-assured by the Consultant and shall not relieve the Consultant of any responsibility or liability for the quality, accuracy, completeness, confidentiality, timeliness or delivery of the outputs and obligations under this contract. All deliverables and substantive outputs shall remain the responsibility of the Consultant and shall be submitted by the Consultant to UN Women. Research ethics, informed consent and data protection: The Consultant shall conduct all KIIs, FGDs and other consultations in accordance with UN Women policies on research ethics, data protection and safeguarding, applying the principles of do-no-harm, confidentiality and voluntary participation. In particular, the Consultant shall: (i) obtain voluntary, informed consent from every participant before any KII or FGD, explaining the purpose of the consultation, how the information will be used and stored, the limits of confidentiality, and the participant’s right to decline to answer or withdraw at any time; (ii) protect the privacy, safety and anonymity of participants, with particular care for women and girls, survivors of violence, persons with disabilities and other marginalized groups, and avoid collecting personally identifiable information unless it is essential; (iii) store, transfer and dispose of all data, including recordings, transcripts and notes, securely, and share them with UN Women only in anonymized form unless explicit consent for attribution has been given; (iv) include the consent procedures, ethical safeguards and a data-management and data-protection plan in the Inception Report for UN Women approval; and (v) report immediately to UN Women any ethical, protection or safeguarding concern that arises during the consultations. Deliverable 1: Undertake a review

This consultancy is home-based and will be commissioned on an as-needed basis until December 2027. Candidate Requirements: Advanced degree in relevant fields At least one year of relevant work experience Experience in gender assessments and analyses Fluency in Ukrainian and working knowledge of English Strong analytical and communication skills Background: UN Women, grounded in the vision of equality enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations, works for the elimination of discrimination against women and girls; the empowerment of women; and the achievement of equality between women and men as partners and beneficiaries of development, human rights, humanitarian action and peace and security. In Ukraine, by 2029, UN Women aims to ensure that more women and girls, including those at the greatest risk of being left behind, lead, influence and benefit from inclusive, gender-responsive humanitarian action, governance, recovery, rights and economic growth. As part of its work in Ukraine, UN Women supports national and local stakeholders in strengthening institutional capacities to advance gender equality and women’s empowerment, integrate gender perspectives into policies, programmes and organizational practices, and implement Ukraine’s national and international commitments on equal rights and opportunities for women and men. This work involves cooperation with public authorities, local self-government bodies, civil society, enterprises, institutions and organizations across different sectors. UN Women has supported governmental institutions in the development and updating of the State Strategy on Ensuring Equal Rights and Opportunities for Women and Men until 2030 and its respective Action Plans. The Strategy provides a comprehensive framework for coordinated actions by central executive authorities, local authorities, civil society organizations and other stakeholders to advance gender equality in Ukrainian society. In accordance with Activity 4, Task 3 (Strategic and Operational Objective 1) of the Operational Plan for the implementation of the State Strategy on Ensuring Equal Rights and Opportunities for Women and Men for the period up to 2030 for 2025–2027, gender audits are envisaged as one of the instruments for strengthening institutional  capacity to integrate the principles of equal rights and opportunities for women and men into organizational policies and practices. A gender audit  assesses how an enterprise, institution or organization  integrates gender equality principles into its internal policies, procedures, organizational culture, human resources practices, working environment, decision-making processes and other relevant areas of  operation. By identifying gaps and good practices , it provides a basis for  practical recommendations and measures  to strengthen gender mainstreaming and  ensure equal rights and opportunities for women and men. Gender audits may therefore be relevant to a broad range of enterprises, institutions and organizations, regardless of their sector, size or form of ownership, that seek to strengthen gender-responsive institutional practices and create more equal, inclusive and non-discriminatory working environments. UN Women intends to provide technical support for gender audits in selected enterprises, institutions and organizations, regardless of their form of ownership, to support national gender equality commitments and respond to requests from partner organizations and institutions. Organizations receiving support will be identified on the basis of relevant requests, programme priorities and the agreed scope of engagement. For this purpose, UN Women is seeking Gender Audit Consultant(s), engaged as national consultants under retainer arrangements, to support the preparation and conduct of gender audits and the development of practical recommendations and action plans for enterprises, institutions and organizations in Ukraine. The gender audits will be carried out on the basis of two resources: the Methodological Recommendations for Conducting Gender Audits by Enterprises, Institutions, and Organizations, approved by Order of the Ministry of Social Policy of Ukraine No. 448 of 9 August 2021 (the Methodological Recommendations)and the Step-by-Step Guide “Gender Audit: Roadmap and Practical Advice”, developed by UN Women in cooperation with the Office of the Government Commissioner for Gender Equality Policy and the Ministry of Social Policy, Family and Unity of Ukraine, with financial support from Sweden. The consultant will report to the Programme Specialist and will be supported by the designated Programme Analyst, who will serve as the focal point for coordination, contractual and payment-related matters for each assignment. For each assignment, UN Women will specify whether the consultant will act as the solo gender audit practitioner or as a member of a gender audit team working with another national expert. The written assignment brief will identify the consultant’s individual responsibilities, outputs and coordination arrangements. Within  the agreed role, the consultant will provide technical and methodological support to selected enterprises, institutions and organizations, regardless of their form of ownership, throughout the gender audit process, in accordance with the applicable methodology and thescope agreed with UN Women and the respective organization. Description of Responsibilities /Scope of Work Depending on the agreed scope and assigned role, the consultant will contribute to the following tasks in coordination with UN Women and the participating organization: Support the preparation of an organization-specific gender audit methodology and workplan, adapting the Methodological Recommendations and Step-by-Step Guide identified above, including a list of documents and materials for desk review, a survey questionnaire, interview guides and other required tools. Support a validation session with the participating organization’s gender audit working group and incorporate agreed comments into the draft methodology for technical review based on the comments received. Provide technical inputs during expert discussions, consultations, and working group meetings throughout the audit process.  Support facilitation of the knowledge-sharing activities, gender audit training sessions and other related events for the participating organization’s working group and other stakeholders. Support the  desk review of organizational and regulatory documents, materials and data in accordance with the areas of analysis specified in the agreed methodology. Support the administration of the online survey and conduct key informant interviews and, where needed, focus group discussions and workshops, in accordance with the guidance provided in the agreed methodology Support the analyses of the collected primary data and support triangulation of findings from the desk review, survey, individual interviews and other data-collection methods. Assist with drafting the gender audit report drawing on the analysis of internal documents, administrative statistics, and collected primary data, including good practices, areas for development and recommendations. Support the validation of the draft report with the participating organization and assist with finalizing the report based on the comments received. Support the organization of the presentation of gender audit’s key findings and recommendations;  Support the development and finalization of an action plan to address the issues identified through the audit and implement its recommendations;  Provide agreed follow-up support to implement gender audit recommendations, including developing or updating policy documents and strategies, delivering training and facilitating consultations, where needed and agreed with the participating organization.   Retainer Arrangements Services will be commissioned on an as-needed basis  from 1 January  to  31 December 2027, subject to programme needs, availability of funds and the consultant’s availability , up to a maximum of 175 working days per consultant over the contract period. This ceiling does not constitute a guaranteed allocation of working days. UN Women does not guarantee any minimum quantity or value of services. Engagement under this retainer does not constitute  a continuous full-time assignment. Before each assignment begins, UN Women and the consultant will agree  on a written assignment brief specifying the organization receiving support, the  consultant’s role, tasks , expected outputs, acceptance criteria, delivery dates, authorized working days, and any approved travel.  The brief will remain within the scope and ceilings of the signed contract and will not itself amend the contract. Work will begin only following UN Women’s written authorization and completion of any required contractual approvals.  Changes to an assignment’s scope, working days or deadlines require prior written agreement and any necessary contractual approval. UN Women will maintain a cumulative record of days commissioned and used against  each consultant’s approved  contractual  ceiling. Requests from participating organizations or public  institutions do not  independently authorize additional work or changes to the contract.     Outputs  Each written assignment brief will specify the outputs required from the consultant, their delivery dates and the authorized working days. Depending on the agreed scope, outputs may comprise one or more of the following: An organization-specific audit workplan and adapted methodology; Document review findings; Survey and interview tools; A documented analysis of collected data, either as a standalone analytical product or as an identifiable component of the gender audit report, as specified in the assignment brief; A draft and/or final gender audit report; A presentation of findings and documented responses to validation comments; A draft institutional action plan and, where commissioned, a finalized action plan reflecting consolidated review comments; Agreed training materials, policy revisions and follow-up advisory products. Outputs will be reviewed against the scope, methodology, acceptance criteria and deadlines agreed in the assignment brief. The consultant will address consolidated review comments within the agreed scope and timetable. Validation by the participating organization does not replace UN Women’s acceptance of the consultant’s outputs for contractual and payment purposes. Assignments will be remunerated at the daily rate specified in the signed contract. Payment will be based on the actual authorized working days satisfactorily performed, supported by accepted outputs and a record of days worked. The UN Women Programme Specialist will certify satisfactory completion in accordance with the contract and applicable UN Women procedures. Payments will remain within the authorized assignment amounts and the overall contractual financial ceiling. postings.posting_type: Request for Expression of Interest / Quality And Cost-Based Selection
postings.text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI) (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)   Country: Republic of Türkiye Project: Türkiye Flood and Drought Management Project (P179313) Loan No./Credit No./Grant No.: 9707-TR Assignment Title: Flood Forecasting and Early Warning System in 6 River Basins (Marmara, Yeilrmak, Sakarya, Bat Akdeniz, Akarçay and Burdur) Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): TR-DGWM-573893-CS-QCBS Market Approach: Open International Competition Contract Type: Lump Sum Contract Duration: 600 calendar days from the commencement date   1. The Government of the Republic of Türkiye has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Türkiye Flood and Drought Management Project (P179313), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. 2. The consulting services (“the Services”) include the expansion, enhancement, integration and operationalization of the National Flood Forecasting and Early Warning System (TATUS) in six river basins (Marmara, Yeilrmak, Sakarya, Bat Akdeniz, Akarçay and Burdur). The Services comprise, among others: integration of the six targeted river basins into the existing TATUS platform and integration with five previously established basins to establish a unified national-scale forecasting network; development, calibration, validation and operationalization of hydrological forecasting models, including modelling of regulated/reservoir-controlled basins; integration and consolidation of meteorological, hydrological, satellite and third-party data, including real-time data acquisition and API interfaces; enhancement of alarm, warning and notification mechanisms; enhancement of the web-based user interface, visualization, reporting, role-based access and interoperability with relevant external systems; system architecture, database and software integration, cybersecurity, data protection, testing and quality assurance; and training, user documentation and support. The assignment also includes a six-month system operation phase during which the Consultant will operate the integrated system and resolve operational issues. The assignment is expected to be implemented mainly from Ankara, with activities in the six river basins identified above. The total contract duration is 600 calendar days from the commencement date. 3. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: https://www.tarimorman.gov.tr/SYGM/Sayfalar/Detay.aspx?SayfaId=186 . 4. The Directorate General of Water Management (DGWM) of the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. 5. A consulting firm is allowed to submit the expression of interest alone if it considers itself to be fully qualified on its own for the assignment, as it is not mandatory for consultants to associate with any other firm(s), whether foreign or local. Alternatively, if consultants themselves choose to associate to enhance their qualifications and capability for the assignment, then such associations may either be as a Joint Venture (i.e. all members of the joint venture shall be jointly and severally responsible) and/or Sub-consultants (i.e. the Consultant will be responsible, including for the services of the sub-consultant). In case of an association, the Consultants must explain in the EOI submission (a) the rationale for forming the association and (b) the anticipated role and relevant qualifications of each member of the Joint Venture and/or of each sub-consultant for carrying out the assignment, to justify the proposed inclusion of the JV members and/or sub-consultants in the association. Failure to provide the above explanation in the Expression of Interest may risk the association not being shortlisted for the assignment. Please note that in the evaluation of EOIs of associations for shortlisting purposes, only the qualifications of the JV members will be taken into account whereas the qualifications of proposed sub-consultants will not be considered. 6. The shortlisting criteria are as follows, in which specific experience of the Consultant relevant to the assignment will be considered of paramount importance: i. General Experience of the Consultant (as a firm): The Consultant (as a firm) should have been in the general consulting services sector for at least 10 year sprior to the deadline for submission of the expression of interest. ii. Specific Experience of the Consultant (as a firm) relevant to the assignment in providing similar services under contracts of comparable size: The Consultants (as a firm) should have specific experience providing similar consulting services under contracts completed within the last 10 years prior to deadline for submission of EOIs in the development of flood risk management plans (including for regulated river basins or those with dams), flood forecasting and early warning systems, hydrological units, real-time data comparison, web-based systems, and related information technologies. Note: Key experts will not be considered during the shortlisting process. 7. To demonstrate their qualifications and experience in meeting the above shortlisting criteria, Consultants are requested to submit, at a minimum, the supporting documentation listed below. A consultant firm can only use its own qualifications and experience and not those of its parent, sister or subsidiary companies or its employees. (i)      The firm's incorporation/trade/registration documents issued by the concerned government authority of the country of the firm. (ii)     The firm’s company brochures including the core areas of business; and (iii)    Completed Form-1 (attached to this Request for Expression of Interest) to provide information on similar contracts. This should include the name and reference number of the contract, a brief description of the scope of work, contract amount, period of the contract, name of the client and country of assignment, and role of the Consultant in the contract. Copies of completion certificates/references of clients of completed contracts are not required to be submitted with the EOI. In the subsequent stage, at the time of submission of proposals, the Client may request the shortlisted Consultants to submit such supporting completion certificates. 8. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Project Financing (Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services) (September 2023), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest. 9. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations. 10. Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours, from 10:00 to 16:00 (Turkish time). 11. Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, by mail or by e-mail) by 16:00 (Turkish time) on 25/12/2026   Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry General Directorate of Water Management Flood and Drought Management Department Attn: Cihat Adsz (Section Manager) Address: Betepe Mahallesi Alparslan Türke Caddesi No: 71 Yenimahalle / ANKARA, Postal Code: 06560 E-mail: sygm.worldbank@tarimorman.gov.tr Website: https://www.tarimorman.gov.tr/SYGM/   Attachment: Form-1 (Similar Contracts) Terms Of Reference (TOR)

postings.text: MINISTÈRE DE LA PLANIFICATION ET DE LA PROSPECTIVE COMMISSION NATIONALE DES TIPPEE SECRÉTARIAT PERMANENT AVIS À MANIFESTATION D’INTÉRÊT (Services de consultant - Sélection de firmes) N° : 10-2026/UCP/PASBAP Paye : Gabon Projet  : Projet d’Accès aux Services de Base et d’Amélioration des Performances » (PASBAP) Financement : Prêt BIRD N°P5110-GA / ID : P179643 Objet : Recrutement d’un(e) cabinet/Firme pour l’Étude sur le plan national d’électrification géolocalisée à moindre coût au Gabon pour un accès universel à l’électricité. Le Gouvernement de la République Gabonaise met en œuvre, avec l’appui financier de la Banque mondiale, le Projet d’Accès aux Services de Base et d’Amélioration des Performances (PASBAP). Ce projet vise à étendre et améliorer l’accès à l’eau potable, à l’assainissement et à l’électricité, en cohérence avec les priorités nationales de développement et dans la continuité du PASBMIR clôturé en 2023. Il comprend quatre composantes majeures : (i) l’amélioration de l’accès à l’eau et à l’assainissement, (ii) le renforcement de l’accès aux services énergétiques , (iii) l’amélioration de la gouvernance sectorielle , et (iv) la gestion du projet et le suivi-évaluation . La mise en œuvre opérationnelle est assurée par le Ministère de l’Accès Universel à l’Eau et à l’Énergie (MAUEE), en coordination avec les entités techniques concernées, sous la supervision d’une Unité de Gestion du Projet établie au sein de la CNTIPPEE. Les services de consultant (« les Services ») comprennent le « Recrutement d’un(e) cabinet/Firme pour l’Étude sur le plan national d’électrification géolocalisée à moindre coût au Gabon pour un accès universel à l’électricité. ». Les Termes de Référence (TdRs) sont disponibles à l’adresse indiquée ci-dessous.   La Commission Nationale des Travaux d’Intérêt Public pour la Promotion de l’Entreprenariat et de l’Emploi (CN-TIPPEE) invite dès à présent les consultants admissibles (« Consultants ») à faire part de leur intérêt à fournir les services décrits ci-dessous. Les consultants intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et une expérience pertinente pour l’exécution desdits services ( en adressant une manifestation d’intérêt au Secrétaire Permanent ). Les critères de sélection de la firme sont les suivants : Les consultants seront évalués sur la base de leurs qualifications, expériences et capacités techniques en lien avec les prestations demandées : 1. Expérience générale de la firme : Le consultant devra justifier d’une expérience avérée d’au moins dix (10) ans dans les domaines de la planification énergétique, de l’accès à l’électricité, de l’électrification rurale et de la réalisation d’études techniques et stratégiques dans le secteur de l’énergie. 2. Expérience spécifique pertinente : Le consultant devra démontrer avoir réalisé avec succès au cours des dix (10) dernières années au moins trois (03) missions similaires portant sur : La planification géospatiale de l’électrification et l’élaboration de plans directeurs d’accès à l’électricité ; L’analyse des options d’électrification au moindre coût intégrant les solutions raccordées au réseau, les mini-réseaux et les systèmes autonomes ; L’utilisation d’outils et plateformes d’analyse géospatiale appliqués à la planification énergétique ; La projection de la demande d’électricité et l’identification des scénarios d’expansion du réseau ; La préparation et l’exploitation de bases de données géoréférencées pour des études d’électrification. Une expérience en Afrique subsaharienne constituera un atout majeur. NB : Les experts individuels ne seront pas évalués au stade de la manifestation d’intérêt. À l’issue de la manifestation d’intérêt, un cabinet /une firme sera retenu (e) et consulté (e) à partir de la méthode de Sélection fondée sur Qualité et le Coût (SFQC) et ce, conformément aux procédures définies dans le Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs de FPI » Les consultants intéressés peuvent obtenir les termes de référence y relatifs ou des informations complémentaires  par courrier électronique à : ( fmbongo@cntippee.org )   et ( mallelaauguste@cntippee.org ) ou par téléphone au +241 76 57 30 30 ou +241 74 12 45 45 ou +241 77 82 85 92 aux heures suivantes : de 8h00 à 16h00 (heure locale). Les plis porteront la mention suivante : « Recrutement d’un(e) cabinet/Firme pour l’Étude sur le plan national d’électrification géolocalisée à moindre coût au Gabon pour un accès universel à l’électricité ». Les manifestations d’intérêt doivent être fournies par courrier électronique à l’adresse ci-dessous au plus tard le  4 décembre 2026  à  12h00  (heure locale du Gabon). Agence d’exécution : CNTIPPEE. À l’attention de : Secrétaire Permanent ; Adresse : Pont de Gué-Gué, impasse André MBA OBAME, villa N°117, BP. 22, Libreville, Gabon. Téléphone : +241 76573030 / +241 74124545/+241 77828592 Courriels : (tippeegabon@cntippee.org), copie à (fmbongo@cntippee.org) et (mallelaauguste@cntippee.org) Site web : www.cntippee-gabon.org .

postings.text: INVITACIÓN A PRESENTAR EXPRESIONES DE INTERÉS República de El Salvador Proyecto: “Proyecto Crecer y Aprender Juntos: Desarrollo Integral de la Primera Infancia en El Salvador Convenio de Préstamo No. BIRF No. 9067-SV Solicitud de Expresiones de Interés    SBCC No. SBCC 39/2026 MINEDUCYT-BIRF   ”DISEÑO E IMPLEMENTACIÓN DE UN CURSO ESPECIALIZADO CON METODOLOGÍA DE TALLERES PARA FORMADORES DE FORMADORES DE PRIMERA INFANCIA DE EDUCACIÓN SUPERIOR”   1. El Gobierno de la República de El Salvador ha recibido un préstamo del Banco Internacional de Reconstrucción y Fomento (BIRF), Convenio de Préstamo N° BIRF 9067-SV, para financiar el costo del Proyecto “Crecer y Aprender Juntos: Desarrollo Integral de la Primera Infancia en El Salvador” y se propone utilizar parte de los fondos para efectuar los pagos bajo el contrato de esta consultoría. 2. El Ministerio de Educación, Ciencia y Tecnología (ejecutor de dicho préstamo), a través de la Dirección de Compras Públicas (DCP), invita a firmas consultoras elegibles (“Consultores”), a indicar su interés en proporcionar los servicios de la ”DISEÑO E IMPLEMENTACIÓN DE UN CURSO ESPECIALIZADO CON METODOLOGÍA DE TALLERES PARA FORMADORES DE FORMADORES DE PRIMERA INFANCIA DE EDUCACIÓN SUPERIOR”, cuyo plazo de ejecución es de 180 días calendarios. Los consultores interesados deberán proporcionar información que indique que están cualificados para suministrar los servicios (folletos, descripción de trabajos similares, experiencia en condiciones similares, disponibilidad de personal que tenga los conocimientos pertinentes, etc.). Los consultores se podrán asociar con el fin de mejorar sus calificaciones.  3. Los Términos de Referencia de la consultoría, se encuentran descritos en el Anexo 1, y pueden consultarse en el siguiente enlace: https://goo.su/5GRzN . Asimismo, pueden obtenerse de forma gratuita, por cualquiera de los procedimientos que se detallan a continuación: a. Presentarse a la Dirección de Compras Públicas, Ministerio de Educación, Ciencia y Tecnología, Plan Maestro Centro de Gobierno, Edificio A-1 Segundo Nivel, San Salvador, El Salvador, teléfono: 2592-3038, los días hábiles a partir del 17 de noviembre al 01 de diciembre de 2026 , en horario de 7:30 a. a 12:00 m. y de 13:00 a 15:30 horas (hora El Salvador GMT-6).  b. Ingresar al sitio web del Ministerio de Educación, Ciencia y Tecnología: https//www.mined.gob.sv en la sección AVISOS o en el sitio electrónico de compras públicas. www.comprasal.gob.sv, para la descarga gratuita del documento, durante el período comprendido del 17 de noviembre de 2026 , durante las 24 horas y hasta las 15.30 hora (Hora El Salvador GMT-6) del 01 de diciembre de 2026.   4. Las firmas consultoras interesadas deberán proporcionar información y documentación (Currículum de la firma y Constancias de trabajos realizados) que demuestren que tienen las calificaciones requeridas y la experiencia pertinente para realizar esta Consultoría. Los criterios para la preselección son los siguientes: Criterio de evaluación Experiencia General de la Firma 1. Firma consultora con experiencia en proyectos de diseño curricular e instruccional, desarrollo de formaciones presenciales y virtuales de formación de formadores o programas formativos dirigidos a docentes como: cursos, diplomados, especializaciones o programas de formación. La gestión logística y despliegue territorial en la implementación de procesos formativos presenciales a nivel zonal o de país.  Experiencia Específica de la Firma  1. Experiencia comprobable a través de portafolio digital en el diseño curricular e instruccional, diseño de contenidos y materiales como: Objetos Virtuales de Aprendizaje (OVA), videos, separatas o folletos, presentaciones, piezas gráficas, infografías, recursos de gamificación, entre otros. 2. Experiencia comprobable en la implementación de proyectos formativos en modalidad presencial dirigidos a formadores de formadores de Instituciones de Educación Superior como: cursos, diplomados, especializaciones o programas de formación.  3. Experiencia comprobable en el diseño y montaje de entornos virtuales de aprendizaje, sites web o plataformas para la gestión de recursos educativos, con énfasis en usabilidad, accesibilidad y experiencia de usuario para adultos. Para la conformación de la lista corta, se seleccionarán a las firmas que acrediten la mayor experiencia en los servicios requeridos, mediante contratos, constancias, órdenes de compra, certificaciones, referencias u otros medios probatorios. Esto hasta alcanzar el mínimo o máximo de firmas consultoras requeridas en el numeral 7.   5. Este proceso se efectuará en el marco de la modalidad expresión de interés, Selección Basada en Calidad y Costo (SBCC) detallada en las Regulaciones de Adquisiciones para Prestatarios en Proyectos de Inversión del Banco Mundial, sexta edición (Febrero de 2025.), y está abierta a todos los interesados de países elegibles, según se definen en dichos lineamientos. Adicionalmente, se solicita a los interesados referirse al numeral 3.14, de la Sección III. Gobernanza, relativo al Conflicto de Intereses, que textualmente establece lo siguiente: “El Banco exige que las empresas o los individuos que participan en las adquisiciones correspondientes a operaciones de financiamiento para proyectos de inversión no tengan conflictos de interés” y a los numerales 3.16 y 3.17, que establecen las referidas regulaciones en materia de conflicto de interés para los Servicios de Consultoría. 6. Las firmas consultoras (Consultores) pueden conformar asociaciones temporales con otras empresas nacionales o extranjeras para mejorar sus calificaciones y capacidades y pueden ser de largo plazo (independientes de un proceso de adquisición en particular) o conformarse para participar en un proceso de adquisición específico, pero deberán indicarlo claramente a través de documento impreso. (Ver numeral 5.38 de las referidas regulaciones). 7. Del conjunto de firmas que hayan presentado expresión de interés, se conformará una lista corta de entre 5 y 8 las empresas elegibles entre las que se postulen y se les invita a presentar sus propuestas, para elegir a la firma ganadora se tendrá en cuenta el Método “Selección Basada en Calidad y Costos (SBCC)”, establecido en las Regulaciones de Adquisiciones para Prestatarios en Proyectos de Inversión del Banco Mundial, sexta edición (febrero de 2025.). 8. Las firmas interesadas pueden obtener información adicional sobre este proceso solicitándola, hasta el día 23 de noviembre de 2026, dirigidas a la Arquitecta Carolina Astrid Ortiz Jiménez, Coordinadora para Adquisiciones de la DCP-BIRF, en horario de 7:30 a las 12:00 horas y de 13:00 a 15:30 horas (Hora El Salvador GMT-6) en la dirección o correo electrónico detallados en el numeral 10.   9. Asimismo, se les informa que se realizará una reunión virtual informativa con el objetivo de ampliar el alcance o alguna inquietud de los ofertantes. Esta reunión se llevará a cabo el día 20 de noviembre de 2026, de las 9:00 a 10:00 horas (hora de El Salvador), por medio de este link: meet.google.com/itp-vxzf-rba o marcar el:(SV) +503 2113 9520 PIN:  286 882 122 6655#. El documento cual será enviado de forma editable a las firmas que lo soliciten por medio del siguiente correo electrónico: christian.villalta@mined.gob.sv 10. Las expresiones de interés deberán hacerse llegar por escrito a más tardar a las 15:30 horas (Hora El Salvador GMT-6) del día 01 de diciembre de 2026 , a la siguiente dirección: Ministerio de Educación, Ciencia y Tecnología, Dirección de Compras Públicas, Plan Maestro, Centro de Gobierno, Edificio A-1, Segundo Nivel, San Salvador, El Salvador, Centro América Dirigidos  Licenciada María Guadalupe Moran de Albergue, o vía correo electrónico christian.villalta@mined.gob.sv  con copia a carolina.ortiz@mined.gob.sv 11. Todos los documentos deberán estar escritos en el idioma Castellano. En caso los instrumentos estén redactados en idioma extranjero, se podrán presentar traducciones simples. 12. Las Firmas Consultoras deberán remitir la siguiente documentación: a. Carta de Expresión de Interés (según modelo del Anexo 2). b. Información general de la firma (según modelo del Anexo 3). c. Documento que indique la intención de formar un consorcio firmado por los Representantes Legales de las partes involucradas (si corresponde). d. Antecedentes de la firma e. Describir detalladamente la experiencia de la firma en función de lo establecido en el anexo 4. f. Fotocopia simple de contratos, constancias que indiquen la experiencia de la firma. g. Fotocopia simple del Documento constitutivo de la empresa. h. Fotocopia simple del Documento de Identidad de la persona que funge como Representante Legal.  i. Fotocopia simple de la Credencial de Elección del Representante Legal o su equivalente en el país de origen. j. Carta compromiso anticorrupción para proveedores y contratistas (socios de negocios) [ISO 37001:2025 SGA 8.5] (Anexo 6)   Los documentos antes mencionados, pueden ser consultados en el siguiente enlace: https://goo.su/5GRzN     San Salvador, 17 de noviembre de 2026

postings.text: Consultant - Social Media | UNCCD - United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification Skip to main content Consultant - Social Media UNCCD - United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification Remote | Bonn CON level Speaks English Application deadline: November 26, 2026 (8 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The Consultant - Social Media will provide comprehensive social media management services for the G20 Global Land Initiative (GLI). This role involves creating engaging content, optimizing social media presence on platforms like LinkedIn, Instagram, and Facebook, and fostering brand awareness. The consultant will work closely with the communications teams to accelerate audience growth and engagement, conduct performance assessments, and collaborate with various teams for impactful messaging. The position is home-based and requires a minimum of 75 working days. Candidate Requirements: Bachelor’s degree in marketing, communications, or related field Minimum 5 years of experience with partners Experience with Instagram, Facebook, and LinkedIn Solid experience in managing online communities Familiarity with Adobe Creative Suite and social media tools Understanding of brand positioning Desirable understanding of environmental challenges Fluency in English Result of Service The consultant will deliver comprehensive social media management services to the G20 GLI, encompassing support for visualization and publication designs. The key focus will be on strategically activating and optimizing G20 GLI social media presence across LinkedIn, Instagram, and Facebook platforms. Work Location Home-based Expected duration 75 working days Duties and Responsibilities Background note: Desertification, along with climate change and the loss of biodiversity were identified as the greatest challenges to sustainable development during the 1992 Rio Earth Summit. Established in 1994, the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD) is the sole legally binding international agreement linking environment and development to sustainable land management. The Convention seeks to support countries to address Desertification, Land Degradation, and Drought (DLDD). (www.unccd.int) The G20 (or Group of Twenty) is the annual international forum for the governments of 19 industrialized countries and the European Union (EU). The G20 Leaders' Declaration, issued on Sunday, 22 November 2020, launched a "Global Initiative on Reducing Land Degradation and Enhancing Conservation of Terrestrial Habitats" (G20 GLI). Building on existing initiatives and on a voluntary basis, the G20 countries share the ambition to achieve a 50 percent reduction in the amount of degraded land by 2040. The G20 GLI with oversight from UNCCD, will focus on capacity building, engaging the private sector and civil society and showcasing success. GLI is looking for a skilled consultant with expertise in social media management to assist the communications teams in managing and optimizing the G20 GLI social media accounts. The social media specialist is expected to create engaging content, foster brand awareness, and drive social media growth. Duties and Responsibilities: 1. Under the overall supervision of the Communications Coordinator of the G20 Global Land Initiative, and in consultation with the G20 team and relevant UNCCD Communications team, the Social Media Consultant is expected to accomplish the following tasks: 2. Produce strategic and engaging social media content and campaigns for Initiative's channels (Instagram, LinkedIn and Facebook), based on a comprehensive social media strategy in pursuit of the G20 mandate to GLI; 3. Accelerate audience growth and engagement across all channels, including through collaborations with strategic, UNCCD and GLI teams, partners 4. and social media partners as well as user-generated content; 5. Ensure growth and timely production of monthly newsletter and provide social media support as needed and/or on request to the Executive Office; 6. Conduct regular data-driven and centered assessments of performance, and adjust tactical approach, as needed to achieve the strategic goals; 7. Collaborate with design, website and relevant UNCCD & GLI staff and teams for impactful messaging and cross-platform promotion; 8. Monitor and flag potential communications risks, including misinformation, unauthorized use of assets and to meet the required quality and standard of UN communication; 9. Maintain an organized digital repository of all social media visual assets and templates, including past notes and assets handed over by previous consultants; 10. Any other associated tasks that are requested. Qualifications/special skills A bachelor’s degree in marketing, communications, public relations, digital media, journalism, law, social sciences or a related field is required. Minimum 5 years of working experience with partners is required. Experience with Instagram, Facebook and LinkedIn, and ability to understand, interpret and apply their analytics is required. Solid experience in managing and growing online communities, fostering engagement and responding to user inquiries or feedback is required. Familiarity with production of communication products and expertise in the following specialized software is an advantage: Adobe Creative Suite (InDesign, Illustrator, Photoshop, etc), Mailchimp or BREVO, Hootsuite and Trello. Understanding of brand positioning and experience in maintaining brand consistency across social media platforms is desirable. An understanding of environmental challenges and solutions is desirable. Previous experience in working in the UN is desirable Languages Fluency in spoken and written English is required. Knowledge of another official United Nations language is desirable. Additional Information Only individuals who can act as independent, individual economical operators are qualified to apply. Individuals who can provide their services only on account of an institution or enterprise are not eligible under this procedure. Individuals engaged under a consultancy or individual contract will not be considered “staff members” under the Staff Regulations and Rules of the United Nations Secretariat and will not be entitled to benefits provided therein (such as leave entitlements and medical insurance coverage). Their conditions of service will be governed by their contract and the General Conditions of Contracts for the Services of Consultants and Individual Contractors. Consultant and individual contractor is responsible for determining tax liabilities and for the payment of any taxes and/or duties, in accordance with local or other applicable laws. No Fee THE UNITED NATIONS DOES NOT CHARGE A FEE AT ANY STAGE OF THE RECRUITMENT PROCESS (APPLICATION, INTERVIEW MEETING, PROCESSING, OR TRAINING). THE UNITED NATIONS DOES NOT CONCERN ITSELF WITH INFORMATION ON APPLICANTS’ BANK ACCOUNTS. Candidates are responsible for complying with deadlines and are encouraged to submit applications well ahead. Before applying, please make sure that you have read the requirements for the position and that you qualify. Applications from non-qualifying applicants will most likely be discarded by the recruiting manager. postings.title: Consultant – Review of Library and Archives Services and Organizational Structure UNOG - United Nations Office at Geneva Remote | Geneva CON
postings.text: Consultant – Review of Library and Archives Services and Organizational Structure | UNOG - United Nations Office at Geneva Skip to main content Consultant – Review of Library and Archives Services and Organizational Structure UNOG - United Nations Office at Geneva Remote | Geneva CON level Speaks English, French Application deadline: November 25, 2026 (7 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The United Nations Office at Geneva is seeking a consultant to review its Library and Archives Services and organizational structure in the context of the UN80 Initiative. The consultant will assess the relevance and efficiency of current services, analyze emerging technologies, and provide actionable recommendations for organizational reform. The role requires a comprehensive evaluation of user needs, productivity, and cost-effectiveness, along with the development of future-state options for service delivery. The position is remote with potential on-site visits and is expected to last for three months. Candidate Requirements: Advanced university degree in information management, library science, archival sciences, political science, or international relations 10 years of progressive experience in leading libraries or archives institutions Experience conducting organizational reviews or management consulting assignments Experience in organizational restructuring and digital transformation of library/archives services Fluency in English and knowledge of French Result of Service The final consolidated report shall include: Findings and analysis; Assessment of emerging technologies and future service requirements; Productivity and cost-effectiveness review; Assessment of organizational structure and management arrangements; Options for organizational reform; Actionable recommendations in support of the UN80 Initiative and a future-ready state for Library & Archives. Work Location Remote with on-site visit(s) Expected duration 3 months Duties and Responsibilities In the context of the UN80 Initiative and General Assembly guidance on programmatic realignment, structural change and organizational efficiency, the UN Library & Archives Geneva seeks an external review of its library and archives services and its structure to assess continued relevance, efficiency, organizational positioning, staffing structure, and service delivery models. Responding to requests from the United Nations General Assembly’s Advisory Committee on Administrative and Budgetary Questions (ACABQ), particular attention shall be given to technological developments, evolving user needs, workload and performance data, opportunities for resource optimization, potential reorganization scenarios, post distribution and levels, and measures to eliminate possible duplication with other UNOG services. The review shall provide an evidence-based assessment and actionable recommendations to support future budgetary and organizational decisions. Scope of Work A. The consultant(s) shall conduct a review of the library and archives services and organizational structure of the United Nations Library & Archives Geneva in the context of the UN80 Initiative, focusing on: 1. Evolution and Relevance of Services Assess how user needs and service demands have evolved. Evaluate the continued relevance of current library and archives services. Identify services that should be maintained, transformed, consolidated or discontinued. 2. Impact of Emerging Technologies Assess the implications of AI, automation, digitization, and other emerging technologies. Identify opportunities for further innovation, automation and efficiency gains. 3. Efficiency, Productivity and Cost-Effectiveness Analyze workload indicators, outputs, performance data and resource utilization. Assess productivity and cost-effectiveness of current operations. Identify opportunities for efficiency improvements. 4. Organizational Structure and Management Review the organizational structure, staffing model, and management arrangements within the context of all functions of UN Library & Archives Geneva, including management of cultural activities and artworks management. Assess the appropriateness of staff levels, roles and functional titles. Recommend alternative organizational arrangements where warranted. Identify functions that may be delivered remotely, centralized, shared, outsourced or otherwise reorganized. Assess potential efficiency gains and resource implications. Assess possible overlap, synergies and coordination with other entities at UNOG, including UNIS. 5. Future-State Options Develop organizational options for the future delivery of services, including: Optimization of the current model; Structural realignment; Shared-service arrangements; Other cost-effective models consistent with the objectives of the UN80 Initiative. Methodology The review shall be supported by: Workload indicators; Expected outputs; Productivity assumptions; Performance information; Relevant industry standards Consultations with stakeholders, notably Member States and research partners. The consultants shall focus their work on their relevant subject expertise (library or archives services), while engaging with each other on themes and opportunities that cut across library and archives services and for drafting and submitting a consolidated report. Qualifications/special skills Advanced university degree (Master's degree or equivalent) in information management, library science, archival sciences, political science or international relations is required. A first-level university degree (Bachelor degree or equivalent) in combination with two additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. 10 years progressive experience in leading a national library, university library, library of an international organization, archives institution or similar knowledge-management organization. Experience conducting organizational reviews, audits, or management consulting assignments. Experience in organizational restructuring and digital transformation of library/archives services. Familiarity with the UN system or other international organizations. Languages English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. Fluency in English and knowledge of French are required for this position. Knowledge of an additional official UN language is an advantage. Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish are the official languages of the United Nations Secretariat. Additional Information Not available. No Fee THE UNITED NATIONS DOES NOT CHARGE A FEE AT ANY STAGE OF THE RECRUITMENT PROCESS (APPLICATION, INTERVIEW MEETING, PROCESSING, OR TRAINING). THE UNITED NATIONS DOES NOT CONCERN ITSELF WITH INFORMATION ON APPLICANTS’ BANK ACCOUNTS. postings.text: Procurement Notices - UNDP-MDG-00913 - PRC019844- RECRUTEMENT CABINET / OSC -EVALUATION HYPOXIE- POLLUTION MARINE PRC019844- RECRUTEMENT CABINET / OSC -EVALUATION HYPOXIE- POLLUTION MARINE Procurement Process RFP - Request for proposal Office UNDP-MDG - MADAGASCAR Deadline 04-Dec-26 @ 03:00 AM (New York time) Published on 18-Nov-26 @ 12:00 AM (New York time) Reference Number UNDP-MDG-00913 Contact UPM MADAGASCAR - upm.mg@undp.org This specific tender is managed via the new supplier portal system of UNDP Quantum. If you are interested in submitting a bid for this tender, you must subscribe following the instructions in the user guide . If you have not registered a profile with this system, you can do so by following the link for Supplier Registration . If you already have a supplier profile, please access the negotiation using quicklink or please login to the Supplier Portal , then search for the negotiation using the reference number UNDP-MDG-00913 , following the instructions in the user guide . Introduction ***DEMANDE DE PROPOSITION*** Le Programme des Nations Unies pour le Développement ci-après dénommé PNUD invite par la présente les cabinets /osc potentiels à présenter une offre conformément aux termes de références et s exigences tels qu'ils figurent dans la présente demande de proposition. Cette demande de proposition est lancé pour sélectionner le cabinet ayant une expertise pour réaliser la mission ci-après : " E valuation nationale de référence sur la sensibilisation à l’hypoxie marine et à la pollution par les nutriments et la mise en place des valeurs de référence des indicateurs du S&E dans le cadre du Projet Océan Propre et Sain " Les propositions peuvent être soumises au plus tard à la date limite indiquée dans le système, directement sur le portail. Il est de votre responsabilité de vous assurer que votre offre est soumise avant la date limite. Les offres reçues après la date limite de soumission en dehors du portail en ligne, pour quelque raison que ce soit, ne seront pas prises en compte pour l'évaluation. Les offres doivent être soumises directement dans le portail des fournisseurs de Quantum en suivant ce lien : http://supplier. quantum.partneragencies.org/ en utilisant le profil que vous pouvez avoir dans le portail. Si vous ne vous êtes jamais inscrit auparavant, vous pouvez enregistrer un profil en utilisant le lien d'inscription partagé via l'avis de passation de marchés et en suivant les instructions des guides disponibles sur le site Web du PNUD : https://www.undp.org/procurement/business/resources-for-bidders . Ne créez pas de nouveau profil si vous en avez déjà un. Utilisez la fonction de mot de passe oublié au cas où vous ne vous souviendriez pas du mot de passe ou du nom d'utilisateur de l'enregistrement précédent. Les services proposés seront examinés et évalués sur la base de l'exhaustivité et de la conformité de la proposition et de sa réactivité aux exigences de la demande de propositions et de toutes les autres annexes fournissant des détails sur les exigences du PNUD. La proposition qui est conforme à toutes les exigences, qui répond à tous les critères d'évaluation et qui offre le meilleur rapport qualité-prix sera sélectionnée et se verra attribuer le contrat. Toute offre qui ne répond pas aux exigences sera rejetée. Tout écart entre le prix unitaire et le prix total sera recalculé par le PNUD, et le prix unitaire prévaudra, et le prix total sera corrigé. Si le Prestataire de services n'accepte pas le prix final basé sur le nouveau calcul et la correction des erreurs par le PNUD, sa Proposition sera rejetée. Le simple fait de soumettre une proposition implique que le prestataire de services accepte sans réserve les conditions générales du PNUD. Veuillez noter que le PNUD n'est pas tenu d'accepter une proposition, ni d'attribuer un contrat ou un bon de commande, ni d'être responsable des coûts associés à la préparation et à la soumission d'une proposition par un prestataire de services, quel que soit le résultat ou la manière de mener le processus de sélection. La procédure de contestation des fournisseurs du PNUD a pour but d'offrir une possibilité de recours aux personnes ou aux entreprises qui ne se sont pas vu attribuer un bon de commande ou un contrat dans le cadre d'un processus de passation de marché concurrentiel. Si vous estimez que vous n'avez pas été traité de manière équitable, vous pouvez trouver des informations détaillées sur les procédures de contestation des fournisseurs dans le lien suivant : http://www.undp.org/content/undp/en/home/operations/procurement/business/protest-and-sanctions.html Le PNUD encourage chaque fournisseur potentiel à prévenir et à éviter les conflits d'intérêts, en divulguant au PNUD si vous, ou l'un de vos affiliés ou membres du personnel, avez participé à la préparation des exigences, de la conception, des estimations de coûts et d'autres informations utilisées dans cette demande de propositions. Le PNUD applique une tolérance zéro en matière de fraude et d'autres pratiques proscrites, et s'engage à prévenir, identifier et traiter tous les actes et pratiques de ce type à l'encontre du PNUD, ainsi que des tiers impliqués dans les activités du PNUD. Le PNUD attend de ses fournisseurs de services qu'ils adhèrent au Code de conduite des fournisseurs des Nations Unies, disponible sur ce lien : https://www.un.org/Depts/ptd/sites/www.un.org.Depts.ptd/files/files/attachment/page/pdf/unscc/conduct_english.pdf. The G20 Leaders' Declaration, issued on Sunday, 22 November 2020, launched a "Global Initiative on Reducing Land Degradation and Enhancing Conservation of Terrestrial Habitats" (G20 GLI). Building on existing initiatives and on a voluntary basis, the G20 countries share the ambition to achieve a 50 percent reduction in the amount of degraded land by 2040. The G20 GLI with oversight from UNCCD, will focus on capacity building, engaging the private sector and civil society and showcasing success. postings.text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – SELECTION OF INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANTS)   Republic of Uzbekistan Uzbekistan Digital Inclusion Project Credit No.: 7425-UZ   Assignment Title: AI and Technology Ecosystem Adviser – International Individual Consultant Reference No.: UZ-DIP-582910-CS-INDV   The Republic of Uzbekistan has received financing from the International Development Association toward the cost of the Uzbekistan Digital Inclusion Project. “Administration of Technology Park of Software and IT” LLC (IT Park), as the Implementing Agency, intends to apply part of the proceeds to engage an individual consultant as AI and Technology Ecosystem Adviser to the CEO of IT Park Uzbekistan, under Subcomponent 1.1 of the Project. Under Subcomponent 1.1, the Project supports IT Park Uzbekistan’s AI and technology ecosystem agenda, including the implementation of AI strategy, priority AI initiatives, international technology partnerships and the commercialization of innovations, in line with Uzbekistan’s Strategy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence Technologies until 2030. The Adviser will support the CEO of IT Park in prioritising, designing and delivering AI ecosystem initiatives, partnerships and programmes, and in strengthening IT Park’s internal capacity to manage its AI agenda. Results are expected to contribute to the Project Development Objective through the creation of digital jobs, growth of AI-enabled IT services exports and inclusion of women, youth, persons with disabilities and the regions. The consulting services (“the Services”) include, but are not limited to: assessment of existing AI initiatives, capabilities and AI-readiness, and recommendation of priorities for a 12-month AI ecosystem work plan; advice on strategic AI-related decisions, including decision papers on proposed AI programmes, centres, partnerships and investment initiatives; identification and engagement of international technology partners, and support for cooperation proposals and authorised negotiations; support for applied AI initiatives and the commercialisation of innovations developed by local startups and IT Park residents; advice on mechanisms to attract AI talent and strengthen IT Park’s institutional capacity, including working sessions for IT Park staff; support to the CEO across IT Park’s strategic directions (startups and venture investment; export and international positioning; Uzbekistan as a regional technology hub; support to IT Park residents and their AI adaptation; and R&D, data and robotics). The assignment is proposed for a period of 12 months. The Adviser will work in a hybrid format, under a time-based contract. postings.text: CFCV/2026/051 Consultant (Senior Advisor Disaster Risk Governance) | IOM - International Organization for Migration Skip to main content CFCV/2026/051 Consultant (Senior Advisor Disaster Risk Governance) IOM - International Organization for Migration Remote | Home Based - May require travel Both national and international UG - Ungraded level Speaks English Application deadline: December 01, 2026 (13 days) Apply Summary by Impactpool The International Organization for Migration (IOM) is seeking a Senior Advisor for Disaster Risk Governance to provide specialized advisory inputs and quality assurance for disaster management initiatives in Southeast Asia. The consultant will support the development of a Compendium of Best Practices and two policy briefs focused on integrating disaster risk reduction and climate change adaptation. This role requires expertise in ASEAN institutional frameworks and disaster management practices. The position is home-based and involves collaboration with IOM's technical teams and ASEAN stakeholders. Candidate Requirements: Master's degree in relevant field; PhD preferred 10+ years of experience in disaster management or related fields In-depth knowledge of ASEAN disaster management cooperation Experience with ASEAN disaster management architecture Strategic and technical advisory experience in regional disaster management Experience in reviewing policy briefs and strategic publications Ability to adapt to ASEAN policy language and practices Experience engaging with senior government officials and stakeholders Strong analytical and communication skills Fluency in English; knowledge of other ASEAN languages is a plus Job Description Reference No.                 : CFCV/2026/051 Position Title                  : Senior Advisor Disaster Risk Governance  Duty Station                   : Homebased Organization Unit          :  Mobility & Resilience Unit Classification                  : Consultancy Type of Appointment    : Consultancy Report to                         : Programme Coordinator for Disaster, Climate and Resilience Estimated Start Date     : As soon as possible Closing Date                   : 1 December 2026 Background Disaster risks in Southeast Asia are becoming more intense and complex, with impacts on communities, livelihoods, economies, and infrastructure. Over the past two decades, ASEAN has built substantial experience in disaster management through the implementation of the ASEAN Agreement on Disaster Management and Emergency Response (AADMER), covering prevention, mitigation, preparedness, response, and recovery. These efforts are supported by wider regional commitments, including the ASEAN Community Vision 2045, the ASEAN Leaders’ Declaration on Sustainable Resilience, the ASEAN Disaster Risk Communication Framework, the ASEAN-UN Plan of Action 2026–2030, and the ASEAN-EU Strategic Partnership Cooperation Framework 2023-2027. A wide range of practices and lessons have emerged through regional cooperation and national implementation of AADMER, providing a strong foundation for continued learning across ASEAN. The AADMER Work Programme 2026-2030, particularly Priority Programme 2 on Prevention and Mitigation, provides further space to connect these experiences with knowledge exchange, policy reflection, and capacity building, and to support their wider application across ASEAN Member States. Under the initiative titled “Advancing Disaster Risk Governance through the Integration of DRR and CCA”, supported by the European Union, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) is working to support the ASEAN Committee on Disaster Management (ACDM) Working Group on Prevention and Mitigation (P&M) facilitated by the Disaster Management and Humanitarian Assistance (DMHA) Division, the ASEAN Secretariat in the implementation of three complementary areas of work: 1.    The development of the Compendium of Best Practices on Disaster Management: Commemorating 20 Years of AADMER;  2.    The preparation of two policy briefs focusing on risk-informed planning for Disaster Risk Reduction and Climate Change Adaptation integration and national and sub-national implementation of Community Based Disaster Risk Management. [DK2.1][PZ2.2] Together, these activities will support ASEAN Member States in documenting experience, examining implementation lessons, and strengthening approaches to prevention and mitigation planning. To strengthen the institutional alignment [BS3.1][MP3.2]of these activities with ASEAN’s disaster management and other related areas of framework, IOM will engage a Senior Advisor to provide specialized advisory inputs and quality assurance throughout the development of project outputs. Drawing on expertise in ASEAN institutional frameworks and practices,[BS4.1][MP4.2] AADMER terminology and formulations, relevant document structures and review processes, as well as the specific priorities and sensitivities of ASEAN Member States, the Advisor will support IOM in adapting the content, framing and presentation of outputs to the ASEAN context to ensure their relevance and appropriateness for consideration by the ASEAN Secretariat and relevant ASEAN sectoral bodies. Purpose and Nature of the Consultancy  The purpose of the consultancy is to provide senior advisory review and quality assurance so that selected IOM-led outputs and activities are institutionally accurate, appropriately framed and consistent with ASEAN and AADMER terminology, formats, sensitivities and working practices. The Advisor will provide strategic guidance, institutional perspectives and quality assurance across three areas of work: 1. Advisory review and quality assurance of the Compendium of Best Practices on Disaster Management: Commemorating 20 Years of AADMER, in close coordination with the Compendium development team composed by IOM experts; 2.Advisory support and technical review of two policy briefs on DRR-CCA integration and Community-Based Disaster Risk Management (CBDRM), in close coordination with the Policy Briefs development teams composed by IOM experts. The consultancy is expected to contribute to ASEAN and AADMER-specific expertise, including guidance on institutional positioning, policy relevance, terminology, framing and consistency with regional priorities and practices. The assignment will be implemented in close collaboration with IOM's multi-level technical team, drawing on expertise from IOM Country Offices, the Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific, and relevant technical specialists from Headquarters. Specifically, the consultant will support the IOM project team in the following areas: A.    Specialized Advisory and Quality Assurance for the AADMER Compendium The Advisor will provide specialized advisory inputs and institutional quality assurance at selected stages of the Compendium development process. Responsibilities include analyzing research findings, preparing technical materials, and facilitating stakeholder engagement. The report will present the consultant's analysis and contextualization of the findings, the methodology used for stakeholder consultation and validation, a synthesis and assessment of the technical feedback received, identified evidence gaps and contextual factors, refined conclusions, and recommendations or priorities for follow-up.
